## 0. Words

One word for each thing. The phase sections use the same words. Where a code name forces a second word, the table
names it.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| view | One window cut from a source slice: centred, shifted or rescaled. Many views come from one source slice. Code name: "window" (B1). |
| image | The pixels the model sees: one view, 512 x 512 (LIDC CT) or one RIGA fundus view. |
| row | One training example: a view plus its prompt and its target. |
| rows root | The folder of rows that one run trains on (B1: 8,320 rows = 260 steps x 32, the V1 budget of section 6.2; B1.2 builds whole 20-step blocks). |
| outline | A lung-nodule (or optic disc/cup) boundary. |
| polygon text | The outline written as JSON text on a 0-1000 grid. The model writes it. |
| outline length | Tokens of a certified target without the end token. The longest LIDC train doctor outline is 1,181 tokens, 1,182 with the end token; 0 of 23,469 are above 1,200 [measured: docs/implementation2.0/notes/A1.md F9 (counts the end token) and B1.md F8 (does not); re-run 2026-11-08 with docs/implementation2.0/notes/A1_tokcount_probe.py, Qwen3-VL-2B tokenizer]. A limit check that counts the answer cap counts the end token: `L - soft_punish_cache >= 1,182 + 32` (B3.7, C7 and 99_back decision 13 must use this one form). |
| doctor | One human rater. An image has up to 4 doctors. Code names: "rater", "voter". |
| answer | One polygon text written by the model. TRL name: "completion". |
| group | The 8 answers for one prompt in one RL step. |
| step | One RL optimiser step: generate, score, update. |
| R5 step time | 23.65 s, the mean over all R5 shared-prefix steps [measured: runs/r5/shared_rl.json timing_s.per_step]. 23.43 s (steps 3-15) is used only inside the C speed gates. |
| miss | An image whose mean IoU_tc over its K = 8 answers is below 0.1 (the K-mean rule) [code: experiments/phase2/final_eval.py:26-30]. Test 10.8 %, val 12.6 % [measured: runs/r5/eval/eval_{test,val}/items.jsonl]. |
| found image | An image that is not a miss. |
| missed answer | One answer with IoU_tc below 0.1 (used by the B3 reward). |
| test | The test split (2,200 images). Read once, on the final candidate only, after the owner closes the 4B gate (section 3). Never called "exam". Exception: A3 re-scores the R5 model on test to check equivalence (A-G3). No choice is made from it. |
| checker | The CUDA engine (`cuda/gpucheck.cpp`) that tests if an outline is legal (13 defect classes) and scores it. |
| score | IoU against the set of doctors, boundary F, area, Betti topology. |
| legal | An outline with none of the 13 defects. |
| polygonizer | The code that turns a mask into rings (an outline). |
| gate | A test with a number. Work moves on only when the gate passes. |
| Mac | The development machine. Costs nothing. |
| box | A rented Vast AI GPU host (RTX 5090, 32 GB). Costs money. |
| rental | One session on one box, from launch to teardown. Rentals are named V1, V2, V3, V4 (section 6). |
| launch config | A `RunArgs` YAML (like `experiments/phase2/configs/r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml`). `make preflight` stamps it and `launch.sh --config` names it. V1: `b1_launch.yaml`; V2: `c_launch.yaml`; V3: `b3_launch.yaml` (section 6). V4: `specs/e_v4.yaml`, which after E6 is a `RunSpec` and is both launch config and plan file (E6 step 8b). |
| plan file | A `steps:` YAML that `run.sh` runs on the box (V1: `b1_rows.yaml`, `a3_measure.yaml`). It is never stamped: `preflight.load` builds `RunArgs(**raw)`, and a `steps:` key raises `TypeError` [code: experiments/phase2/preflight.py:49-56; experiments/phase2/train_sft.py:77-101]. |
| session spend | `policy.spend()` now minus `policy.spend()` at the launch of the current rental. It includes the bandwidth estimate of `policy.accrued` (section 6 inputs). Every "$" stop rule, skip rule and `BudgetStop` value in section 6 uses it. The ledger total is already $16.90 [measured: sum of `cost_usd` in experiments/phase2/vast/ledger.csv, 133 rows, 2026-11-08]. |
| layer | One of: `core`, `geom`, `verify`, `data`, `policy`, `rl`, `sft`, `infra`. A layer imports only layers below it. |
| kernel | A custom CUDA function (K1, K2, K3 in section 5). |
| archive | Move old code to `archive/<name>/` with a note. Archived code is never imported. |
| draft | A kernel folder that is not built into the package. |

**Id prefix rule.** Every gate, risk and session id carries its phase prefix: `A-G1`, `B-DG1..B-DG18` (B data gates:
21 gates, DG1-DG18 plus DG1b, DG9b, DG14b; B.6.1), Gate B1, Gate B2, Gate B3 (B run gates), `C-G-EQ1`, `C-G-SP1`,
`D-G1`, `E-G1`, `DOC-G1`, `CLEAN-G1`; front risks `FR1..FR15`; B sessions `B-S1`, `B-S2`; D rentals `R-D1`, `R-D2`.
Inside its own phase a gate may drop the prefix (B writes `DG15`, C writes `G-EQ2`). A reference from another phase
always uses it. Task ids (`A1`, `D3`) keep no prefix. "R5" is always the run.

**Paths.** All paths are relative to the repo root. Notes named M1-M3, T1-T3, CL2, K1-K3 are copied into
`docs/implementation2.0/` by DOC1 (kernels are already in `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/`). No tracked text may cite the
session scratchpad or an absolute `/[p]rivate/tmp` or `/[U]sers/` path. (The plan writes these patterns with brackets,
as regex classes, so that DOC4 check 14 does not match its own text; DOC1 step 0.)

Tags on facts: `[measured: file]`, `[code: file:line]`, `[paper: arXiv id]`, `[web: source]`, `[estimate]`,
`[unverified]`. A measurement made during planning is `[measured: <file or command>, 2026-11-08]`.

## 1. Summary and order of work

Where we are. Test IoU is 0.645 and boundary F is 0.816 on 2,200 test images. Legal is 0.994, precision 0.695, recall
0.748 [measured: runs/r5/eval/eval_test/final_eval.json]. The doctor ceiling is 0.732. Found images score 0.722
against 0.740 (old ceiling definition; A2 recomputes it fairly). The loss is misses: 10.8 % of test images. The
cause is data. RL trained on centred views (offset median 0.018 of the side). The test is shifted (median 0.265)
[measured: docs/research/notes/rl_plateau_diagnosis_2026-11-08.md]. Phase B uses one offset definition (union box):
test median 0.262, 36.7 % above 0.3 (807 of 2,200) [measured: docs/implementation2.0/notes/b1_out/geom.json,
recomputed 2026-11-08]. The diagnosis note uses another centre.

**Priority (owner rule).** Dataset quality is the highest priority. B1 (build the centred, shifted and rescaled
training views, then audit them) runs first. Its B data gates, including the coverage gates B-DG7..B-DG10 against
the train shifted law, must pass on the Mac before any paid RL run. The first paid run is the B1 run itself (V1,
section 6.2).

What we do, in one line each:

- **A. Measure fairly.** Patient-cluster CIs, a fair ceiling, saved answers, medoid choice, GED/HM-IoU, NVTX marks,
  a TRL start-up check, a true outline-length count.
- **B. Quality. DATA FIRST.** B1 builds and audits the training views (centred, shifted, rescaled) before any spend.
  B2 matches trainer and vLLM numbers. B3 changes the reward (location term for misses, no std division).
- **C. GPU speed.** Pixels on the GPU, memo for prompts and rope, one weight push, fewer host syncs. B uses the C code
  only when C-G-EQ1..6 pass and C-G-SP1 passes. C-G-SP1 is relative to the baseline arm of the same rental: fast
  mean <= baseline mean - 3.4 s (mode A) or - 2.7 s (mode B). These are today's 20.0 s and 20.7 s written as a
  distance from R5's 23.43 s (C must follow). C-G-C (<= 18 s) needs C7 and C8 and is measured in the first run after Gate B3. The B3 run keeps the 1,536
  limit and no runaway cap (B3.9).
- **D. CUDA core.** The CUDA polygonizer in production, GPU EDT/GED/HM-IoU, work-optimal kernels (K1, K2).
- **E. Code structure.** Seven layers plus `core`, a typed run spec, one TRL adapter.
- **DOC.** One docs site, drift tests, one source for headline numbers.
- **CLEAN.** Archive old code, delete dead code, use libraries where they clearly help.

DATA FIRST means two things. No GPU is rented for training until the B data gates pass on the Mac. The first paid
rental is the B1 run, not infrastructure checks. The B data gates B-DG1..B-DG18 (21 gates, B.6.1) cover leakage
(patient, series, SHA-256, rows root), window checks, contour-to-slice checks, padded windows, coverage against the
shifted law, and quality reports.

**Outline limit: a higher limit lengthens the wait.** The owner asked whether raising the limit to 1,800 tokens
removes the wait. It does not. Writer time per step = 5.61 s + 4.3 ms x the longest outline in the step (r = 0.92,
R5 steps 3-15) [measured: runs/r5/shared_rl.json, re-fit 2026-11-08]. A runaway outline runs to the limit; 5 of
those 13 steps had one at 1,536 [same file]. Against a step whose longest outline is 600 tokens, a runaway costs
4.3 ms x (1,536 - 600) = 4.0 s at 1,536 and 4.3 ms x (1,800 - 600) = 5.2 s at 1,800. So 1,800 adds about 1.1 s to
every step with a runaway. The limit is set from the counted true outline lengths (A8's count task), not raised. The
longest LIDC train doctor outline is 1,182 tokens with the end token, and 0 of 23,469 are above 1,200 [measured:
docs/implementation2.0/notes/A1.md F9; re-run 2026-11-08]. RIGA differs: 1 train outline is above 1,536 [same probe],
so a RIGA run keeps 1,536 until its own count (C7 step 4). C7 points here.

**End state under (b') (the one rule; B3.10, C10, C.8.3, E "When E starts" and 99_back decision 1 point here).**
Under (b') no rental follows V1. So Gate C-adopt (V2) and Gate B3 (V3) are never read, and C10 and B3.10 never
fire. Code whose adoption gate needs V2 or V3 therefore never lands on `main`. `main` then never holds a temporary

### 1.1 After V1: decision table

V1 is the one paid experiment that fits $3. The owner approves this table with the V1 item list (6.1 step 0), so the
result cannot bend it. The rules named are Gate B1's hard rules (B.6.2). This is the only copy of the table: B.4.1
and 99_back decision 2b point here.

| Gate B1 result | Next paid step | Code | Final candidate (the one model that reads test) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pass | B-S2 (B3 on the B1 rows root) after the owner's budget decision | B1.8 runs | Best of B1 and B3 on val-select by the Gate B3 rules. A tie goes to B1 (the simpler model) |
| Fails only the far-miss rule (IoU CI lower bound > 0) | B3 on the B1 rows root (the location term targets the misses that are left) | B1.8 runs | As above |
| Fails the IoU rule or the difference-in-differences rule (no data effect) | No B3 spend. Mac diagnosis on A3's and B1's saved answers (per-cell logs). The 4B gate is decided now, on B1's val numbers | B1.8 runs (the effect failed, not the path: every later run reads a rows root; B1.8) | R5, unless the 4B arm wins on val |
| B1 stopped early: `rl.json` has `partial: true` (a crash, then `train_rl --merge-last`, 6.2) and N < 260 steps | Gate B1 is computed on the merged checkpoint-N and labelled "partial run, N steps". The row the rules give applies, but a pass does not lead to B-S2 until the owner reviews it | As the row the rules give | As the row the rules give |
| Fails the offset < 0.15 guard, the edge guard, legal share or the frozen-view hash (each B1 and A3 `final_eval.json` `view_content_sha256` equals its `frozen_views.json` entry, DG15); or the edge baseline is missing after the 6.2 fallback (under (b'), or when V2 item 1b fails again) | Stop. Owner review | B1.8 runs in the commit after the owner's written review closes, unless that review drops the rows path (B1.8) | R5 |

The view-identity correlation of A-G3 is not a Gate B1 rule. When it fails, Gate B1 still pairs with A3's items and
drops only the R5 report line (B.6.2).

The C and D Mac work does not depend on the row taken. The 4B gate is evaluated after the last 2B run that the
budget allows: B1 if B-S2 is not funded (99_back decision 17 must follow).

## 2. Target architecture and code organization

### 2.1 Requirements

- GPU everywhere. CPU only where it cannot be avoided. Each CPU item has a reason (phase sections 3.3).
- Pixels do not come back to the CPU after the 32 images of a step are decoded and uploaded (25.2 MB uint8, C1).
  Only scores leave the device.
- Known CPU exceptions: PNG decode (32 per step; no GPU PNG decoder) and vLLM's own image lane (HF preprocess of
  32 images, about 201 MB fp32 H2D, its own vision encode). The vLLM lane goes only if C6b passes (C.3.3).
- One verifier with no torch, TRL, transformers, vLLM, peft or datasets.
- Old code is archived, not left beside new code.
- Library code in `src/objdel` with tests in `tests/`. Experiments are thin modules in `experiments/<phase>/`
  (the CLAUDE.md rule; a move needs the owner to edit that rule first).

### 2.2 Layers (from phase E section 3.1, with round-1 placement fixes)

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| experiments/<phase>/*.py   thin CLIs        specs/*.yaml   typed run specs      |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| infra   vast (offers, ledger, remote, chain), bundle, preflight,                |
|         hf (+ licenses/), secrets; repo root comes from core.provenance         |
+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| rl    build, trl_adapter (ALL private    | sft   config, rows, train, select    |
|       TRL touches), forward, rows,       |       (rl and sft never import       |
|       reward, config, run,               |        each other)                   |
|       vllm_sync, vllm_requests           |                                      |
+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| policy  models, prompt, rows, caches (Vision/Rope/ImageMemo), gpu_pixels,       |
|         marks (NVTX), sampler (eval only), evaluate, vision,                    |
|         callbacks (TraceStep: used by rl and sft)                               |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| data    store (source store), lidc, riga, splits, targets/, probes, prepare,    |
|         windows, coverage, quality, audit (hack_audit)                          |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| verify  reward (spec, score, cache, advantages), metrics, stats, gates,         |
|         ceiling, select, device, store (doctor stores), api, http ([serve])     |
|         NO torch / trl / transformers / vllm / peft / datasets                  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| geom    engine (only importer of _gpucheck), text, shape, rings (polygonize     |
|         seam), topology, volume, certify, box   (CUDA: cuda/gpucheck.cpp)       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| core    spec (RunSpec, pydantic), provenance (repo_root, code_hashes)           |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Rule: a layer imports only layers below it. `import-linter` makes the rule a test, and the contract is `exhaustive`.

Placement decisions (one table; the phases follow it):

| Module | Home | Why |
|---|---|---|
| NVTX marks (A6 `train/nvtx.py`) | `policy/marks.py` | It imports torch lazily. `core` sits under the verifier's no-torch contract, so it cannot hold it. The `checker` range opens in the RL reward call, not in `reward/score.py`. |
| coverage (B1.3 `data/coverage.py`) | `data/coverage.py` | B1.3 moves and extends it first. E does not move it again. |
| `verify/store.py` | doctor-store preload and loader | The training reward reads it. |
| `data/store.py` | source store (slices, outlines) | Built offline on the Mac. |
| CPU fork pool (`serve.fork_pool`) | never moved to `verify/`: D7 step 6 removes the last caller and `--procs`, E3b archives it (E R-2), CLEAN16 step 1 checks | No caller is left after D7. |
| advantages (B3.4) | `verify/reward/advantages.py` | numpy, fingerprinted with the reward. `rl/reward.py` only calls it. |
| A, C, D, CLEAN new modules | `eval/{ceiling,select,device}.py -> verify/`, `train/gpu_pixels.py -> policy/`, `train/vllm_{sync,requests}.py -> rl/`, `checker/rings.py -> geom/`, `geometry/box.py -> geom/` | E's move tables must list them. |

Three deep seams carry the design:

| Seam | Interface | What varies behind it |
|---|---|---|
| `geom.polygonize(mask, offset)` (= `geom.rings.polygonize`, D3) | mask in, rings out | One CUDA engine source on every build (CPU build on the Mac, nvcc on the box). B1.4a puts `checker/rings.polygonize` over today's `check_masks` before B1.4, so the B1 targets already use the engine, and moves the numpy code to `tests/oracles/polygonize_oracle.py`, so every ring reference (also D-G3's) stays numpy; D3 adds `trace` (final round 11, fresh-arch-3; final round 12, qa-1). |
| `policy.sampler` | `sample(rows, params) -> list[Sample]` | `VllmSampler`, `HfSampler`. Evaluation only; training generation stays in TRL's `VLLMGeneration`. |
| `rl.trl_adapter` | one module for every private TRL name; `check()` (A7) at start-up, raises `TRLContractError` | TRL version. A change fails in seconds, on the Mac. |

### 2.4 GPU-everywhere data path (after B1, C and D)

```
 Mac, offline, once per data version              box, every step
 +--------------------------------------+        +--------------------------------------------------+
 | CT slices + doctor outlines (LIDC)   |        | B1 rows root (PNG views + manifest, SHA-checked) |
 | -> views (centred/shifted/rescaled)  | HF     | CPU: 32 PNG decodes per step                     |
 | -> targets (polygon text) + hashes   | repo,  |   |                                              |
 | -> B1 rows root (8,320 rows)         | pinned |   v 25.2 MB uint8 H2D (pinned), not 1.61 GB fp32 |
 | -> B data gates B-DG1..B-DG18        | rev.   | C1 patchify (HF/torch ops on GPU; K3a fallback)  |
 +--------------------------------------+------->|   -> vision encoder once per image (C3)          |
                                                 |   |                                              |
                                                 | vLLM: 8 answers per prompt (GPU)                 |
                                                 |   CPU lane: HF preprocess of 32 images,          |
                                                 |   ~201 MB fp32 H2D, own vision encode            |
                                                 |   (removed only if C6b passes)                   |
                                                 |   | text only                                    |
                                                 | CPU: strict parse of polygon text                |
                                                 |   v                                              |
                                                 | GPU checker: legal? IoU / F / area / Betti       |
                                                 | doctor tables resident on GPU                    |
                                                 |   | scores only (a few floats)                   |
                                                 |   v                                              |
                                                 | group-centred advantages (B3) -> shared-prefix   |
                                                 | forward -> update LoRA -> push weights (C5)      |
                                                 +--------------------------------------------------+
```

Sources: C sections 3.1-3.3, D section 3.2, B1.4 step 5 (rows root on HF). The 25.2 MB figure is C1's design
number (uint8 RGB planes). The 1.61 GB fp32 buffer is measured today [measured:
docs/research/notes/cpu_gpu_trace.md]. The 201 MB is an estimate (32 x 1,024 x 1,536 x 4 B) [C.3.3].

A view bank (one parquet of uint8 planes) is **deferred, not in this plan**. No task builds it. Trigger: C1 measures
PNG decode above 0.2 s per step. If it is ever built, it holds pageable host planes loaded before the fork pool, and
copies 32 planes per step into C1's pinned buffer. No PNG is archived until every image passes a full pixel-hash check.

### 2.5 One RL step after all phases (interaction diagram)

```
 trainer            vLLM              parser(CPU)      checker(GPU)     reward          optimiser
    |  32 prompts      |                   |                |               |               |
    |--(32 PIL views)->|                   |                |               |               |
    |                  | 256 single requests (today);       |               |               |
    |                  | 32 x n=8 only in the C6 arm         |               |               |
    |<- 256 answers ---|                   |                |               |               |
    |---------------------- answers ------>|                |               |               |
    |                                      | polygon text -> rings          |               |
    |                                      |--------------->| legal+score   |               |
    |                                      |<-- scores -----|               |               |
    |------------------------------------------------------------------------>| advantages  |
    |<------------------------------------ advantages ------------------------|               |
    |  update forward: logp and IS ratio (no separate old-logp pass:                           |
    |  FastGRPO.skip_old_logps, existing), no-merge LoRA, shared-prefix forward,                |
    |  log-prob in torch (K3b not planned)                                                      |
    |------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------>| update
    |  push to vLLM in one call (C5), by the preset that B2.4 rule 0 picks:                     |
    |    F (after Gate B3): the adapter via add_lora (+ base W, mode B only) -->|               |
    |    B1, B3 and other presets: merged W + BA (all tensors) ----------------->|               |
    |  NVTX ranges: generate, reward, old_logps, update, sync (Phase A6)                        |
```

Sources: C sections 3.1-3.2 and tasks C1-C10, B3 (reward v5), A6 (NVTX names), `skip_old_logps`
[code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:540-547], merged push values `p.data + d.to(p.dtype)` [code:
src/objdel/train/fast.py:696-717]. vLLM LoRA serving (option F) is not adopted for speed. It is the numerics fix
for merge rounding, and ADR 0013 decides it: B2.4 rule 0 picks F when the B2.0 step-100 relative error is >= 0.2.
The seed value is 0.531 [measured: B.1 item 5], so F is the expected preset of the runs after Gate B3. B1 and B3
run `bf16-seqmask` with the merged push (ADR-0013 rule (b), B2.4 "Scope"). Under F in mode B, sleep level 2
frees the base weights, so the base W is pushed again without the delta (B2.2 must follow). The weight push mode
(vLLM awake or asleep) is a measured arm in Phase C. The diagram shows mode A (awake). Feeding vLLM the trainer's
image features is C6b, an investigation, not planned.

## 3. Model decision

Sources: notes M1, M2, M3 (HF API and model cards, 2026-11-08).

**Decision: keep Qwen3-VL-2B (LoRA) for the B1 data-fix run. Change one variable at a time.** Reasons:

1. The cause is data, not size. Found images score 0.722 against a 0.740 ceiling: 0.018 of headroom [measured:
   final_eval.json; BRIEF]. The 0.740 uses the old ceiling definition, which favours the model, and the found subset
   is chosen by the model's own success [to be confirmed by A2]. After A2, recompute on val: the fair gap on found
   images and on all images, with patient CIs. This bounds the gain on found images only. A bigger model could gain
   mainly through fewer misses, which the 4B gate measures.
2. Training closes most of the 2B to 4B gap. EGM: Qwen3-VL RefCOCO-family average 84.2 (2B) vs 87.3 (4B) on the
   Instruct bases; 83.6 vs 87.2 on the Thinking bases. After SFT+RL from the Thinking bases: 89.6 vs 91.0. The gap
   goes from 3.6 to 1.4 [paper: 2601.13633 Tables 4 and 9].
3. Cost. A 4B RL run is about $2.9 by estimate (step 40-55 s against 23.65 s). It also needs its own SFT (step 0
   below), whose cost is unknown [estimate: M3]. It does not fit the $3 budget beside the 2B run.
4. Every FastGRPO patch is written for Qwen3-VL and works unchanged on 2B.

| Rank | Model | Verdict | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Qwen3-VL-2B | Keep | Capacity ceiling (unknown until the B1 result) |
| 2 | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (4.438 B, Apache-2.0) | Conditional upgrade. Same class, same tokenizer, same 0-1000 grid. Same vision blocks (depth 24, width 1024, DeepStack layers 5/11/17); merger output 2,048 (2B) vs 2,560 (4B) [measured: HF config.json] | 2x step time; memory with colocated vLLM unmeasured; cached feature shapes differ |
| 3 | Qwen3.5-4B (4.660 B) | Park. Best small numbers (RefCOCO 88.1) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet breaks shared-prefix forward and the rope assumptions; new vLLM/LoRA issues |
| 4 | Qwen3.5-2B | Park | Same cost, no grounding gain |
| 5 | LFM3-VL-2B | Park | Licence gate ($10M revenue), custom code, vendor-only numbers, new token budget |
| 6 | InternVL3.5-4B, MiniCPM-V, Gemma 4, SmolVLM2, Moondream, PaliGemma 2, Florence-2 | Excluded | Weak grounding, other format, licence, or size |
| - | MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B | Excluded | SLAKE grounding IoU 0.05 and 0.07, below a fixed centre box at 0.10 [paper: 2604.27720 Table II]; Lingshu is 7B; MedGemma is gated |
| - | HuatuoGPT-Vision | Excluded | Size: 7B and 34B only; no grounding output [M3 item 13; not re-read from the model card] |

Size limit. The owner rule is "any model up to 4B". Every 4B candidate is above 4.0 B: Qwen3-VL-4B and
`MBZUAI/MedMO-4B` have 4.438 B, Qwen3.5-4B has 4.660 B [measured: HF API safetensors.total]. The owner decides if
"up to 4B" means the 4B size class or a hard 4.0 B limit (99_back, model decisions). With a hard limit, there is no
4B arm.

Medical pretraining. No paper shows that it helps polygon text. The evidence is for boxes. It says the localisation
data matters, not the label "medical" [paper: 2602.06965, 2512.10691]. We already have LIDC polygons.
`MBZUAI/MedMO-4B` is the only medical model that drops into our stack (Qwen3-VL-4B architecture). Use it only as an
optional SFT-start A/B. The same HF id is used in the owner decisions.

**Gate for the 4B arm (on val, never on test).** The owner sets the numbers before any spend. Suggested: run 4B only
if, after the 2B B runs, val IoU_tc is still below about 0.68 and the val miss share is still above about 7 %.
R5 val is 0.618 / 12.6 % and R5 test is 0.645 / 10.8 % [measured: runs/r5/eval/eval_{val,test}], so test numbers do
not transfer one to one. The owner sees the full 4B cost (SFT step 0 plus the RL probe and run) before the decision.
Test is read once, after the owner closes this gate, on the single final candidate of whichever model wins. So no B
session reads test before the gate is closed (B-S2 ends with the val evals; B must follow).

**If the gate fires** (code changes, not now):

0. SFT the 4B first. RL needs a checkpoint that already writes the polygon text. The 2B RL started from the SFT
   checkpoint e2 (HF revision `r1-qwen3vl2b`) [measured: docs/research/notes/full_rl_2026-11-08.md:3]. This step is
   the only copy of the 4B SFT recipe. 99_back decision 17 points here.
   - Config. Copy `experiments/phase2/configs/r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml` to `experiments/phase2/configs/sft_qwen3vl4b.yaml`.
     Change exactly five lines: `model: qwen3-vl-4b`; `output_dir: sft-qwen3vl4b`; `branches: [2.0]`;
     `stages: [train]`; `vision: {prepared: prepared, reference: vision_ref/qwen3-vl-4b.json}`. All else stays:
     view `lidc-bundle-v3`, the WSD schedule, seed 1, effective batch 32 and LoRA r 16 / alpha 32 [code:
     experiments/phase2/configs/r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml; src/objdel/train/configs.py:90-95].
   - Why `stages: [train]`. With `branches` set and no `stages` key, `policy.chain` adds select and probe, and both
     read val [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:441-450]. With `stages: [train]` only `train_sft` runs, so
     val stays unread.
   - Why a new reference. `train_sft` raises `ValueError` when the reference JSON names another model [code:
     experiments/phase2/train_sft.py:160-166]. `run.sh` refuses the chain while the reference file is missing
     [code: policy.py:456-475]. The 2B file names `qwen3-vl-2b`.
   - Order on the box, in one rental. First `run.sh <run> experiments.phase2.train_sft --config
     experiments/phase2/configs/sft_qwen3vl4b.yaml --vision_reference_only true`. It writes the 4B reference on the
     CPU in float32, as R0 did [code: experiments/phase2/configs/r0.yaml]. Then `run.sh <run>
     experiments/phase2/configs/sft_qwen3vl4b.yaml`.
   - Tests on the Mac, before the rental. `policy.chain(sft_qwen3vl4b.yaml)` returns exactly one stage, the
     `train_sft` stage. A new preflight check refuses a config whose `vision.reference` JSON names another model;
     a test plants the 2B reference and expects the refusal.
   - Why the 2B recipe. SFT on the B1 rows would change the SFT data and the branch too, so a 4B gain would not be a
     size gain. Price: the 2B SFT ledger rows times the 4B/2B step-time ratio of a 50-step timing probe, plus the
     reference step [estimate until measured]. The RL probe and run start from that merged checkpoint.
1. Add `"qwen3-vl-4b": "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct"` to the model map and to `MAX_COMPLETION`, `_LORA`, `_GRAD_CKPT`:
   in `policy/models.py` after E; in `src/objdel/train/configs.py:73-77` before E [code: configs.py:73-77]. CLEAN8
   keeps `_LORA` and `_GRAD_CKPT` (CLEAN must follow).
2. Make `vllm_gpu_memory_utilization` a per-model value: 0.35 now, about 0.55 for 4B [estimate: M3].
3. Run a 15-step RL probe from the step-0 checkpoint (about $0.25 [estimate]).
4. Accept only if peak memory is below 30 GB and the step time is at most 2.2x the 2B step (M1).

**Guard: deferred to a task.** `FastGRPO` must refuse `shared_prefix` when the text config has `linear_attention`
layers (M2 rec 5). Without it, Qwen3.5 gives silent wrong log-probs. Owner: E5 (`rl/trl_adapter.py` or
`FastForward`), with a unit test on a tiny fake config. Until E5, nobody runs a Qwen3.5 model.

## 5. Custom kernels index

Drafts only. They live in `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1`, `K2`, `K3`. They are not built into the package. Each
folder holds `DESIGN.md`, `GPU_RUN.md`, source and CPU tests. The CPU build of each kernel is the same source as the
GPU build, so the CPU result is the oracle.

Before any rental, each `GPU_RUN.md` must use repo paths: `K1=$REPO/docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1` (same for K2,
K3), with `REPO=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`. Work files go to `$REPO/data/k1_bundle/` (git-ignored, LIDC only).
Today the three runbooks still name the session scratchpad [measured: grep, 2026-11-08: K1 GPU_RUN.md:15-18, K2
GPU_RUN.md:33, K3 GPU_RUN.md:15]. The path edit is D1 step 0 (Mac, $0, before V2), not D1 step 5, which comes after
the R-D1 run that needs it (D must follow). The same step adds an R-D1 config that runs the K1 and K2 runbook steps
through `run.sh` (heartbeat and ledger rows), and a preflight check that no file under `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/`
contains `/[p]rivate/tmp`. The `build/` folders hold macOS binaries and stay out of git (DOC1).

How the drafts reach the box. Today the code sync drops all of `docs/` [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:379],
and the bundle holds no `docs/` and no `k1_bundle` [code: experiments/phase2/vast/bundle.py:52-70]. B1.6 adds the
one keep rule of `code_files()` for `docs/reference/frozen_views.json` and `val_halves.json` (before V1; final round 12,
fresh-arch-1; final round 15, data-2), and
D1 step 0 widens it: paths under `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1/`, `K2/` and `K3/` ship, except
their `build/` and `results/` folders. On the box the runbooks use `/workspace/src/docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1`
(same for K2, K3) and `/workspace/src/cuda`, with work files in the run folder. No scp or rsync line is left. K1's

## 6. GPU rentals within the $3 Vast budget

**One source.** This section is the only place that lists rental items, their order, minutes, dollars, caps, skip
rules and the launch configs that `make preflight` stamps. A phase section points here with a short reference (for
example "rental V1 item 3, front 6.2") and holds only its own run steps: commands, flags and output folders. If a
phase number differs from this section, this section wins. DOC4 check 16 reports a rental table outside this
section.

Rules (binding):

- Vast AI only. North America hosts only (US/CA, fixed in `policy.reasons()`, no flag).
- Preflight before every rental. The main agent rents only after the owner says so. No subagent rents.
- Offer limit: `dph_total` <= $0.641/h and `inet_up_cost`, `inet_down_cost` <= $0.0065/GB. A dearer offer needs a
  new plan, because the `BudgetStop` values below assume these limits.
- `--cap-hours` on every launch. Compute it from the picked offer: `floor_to_0.05((approved $ - b) / r_s)`, with b
  and r_s from the table below. Write the result in the launch line.
- Teardown and `sweep_orphans.sh` after every rental, also after an error.

### 6.2 V1: the B1 run, every Gate B1 input, then A3-val (data first)

V1 is the first paid rental. It runs the owner tag `v1-b1` (order rule 2) with `--shared-prefix` and the control
numerics (bf16-seqmask). It holds no C, D or kernel code. Every V1 reward and eval scores on the CUDA build of the
checker (plan step 0 below). V1 has no nsys capture: the A6 capture is the C0 baseline
arm in V2 item 3 (steps 16-17).

**Launch config (the one file that `make preflight` stamps for V1).** `experiments/phase2/configs/b1_launch.yaml`,
a `RunArgs` file. B1.5 creates it; B1.3 adds the `rows_plan` field to `RunArgs`.

```
model: qwen3-vl-2b
view: views/lidc-bundle-v3            # the SFT bundle, as in r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml
seed: 1
output_dir: b1-rows                   # push_hf.sh uses it as the HF revision
rows_plan: experiments/phase2/configs/b1_rows.yaml
```

- No `branches`. Without them `policy.chain` would give only a train stage [code: policy.py:450], and the launch
  config is never given to `run.sh`.
- Why `view` stays the SFT bundle. `preflight.hashes` reads `view_hash` from `<view>/manifest.json`, and
  `view_integrity` and `patients` read `<view>/rows.jsonl` [code: experiments/phase2/preflight.py:59-70, 101-139].
  The B1 rows root has neither: B1.4 writes `lidc/train.jsonl` and a manifest without `view_hash`.
- How the rows root enters the stamp. With `rows_plan` set, preflight reads the plan's `train_rl` stage, requires the
  local rows-root `manifest.json` SHA-256 to equal its `--rows-manifest-sha256`, runs `quality.failures` on the root
  (check "ROWS root"), and adds that SHA-256 to the stamp's data hash. An edited rows root then refuses the launch
  [code: preflight.refusal compares the data hash]. A plan with several `train_rl` stages (V2's `c_speed.yaml`)
  must name the same `--train`, `--rows-revision` and `--rows-manifest-sha256` in each; preflight refuses a plan
  where they differ, then checks the root once.
- Why a new field and not a plan file. `preflight.load` builds `RunArgs(**raw)`, so a `steps:` key raises
  `TypeError` [code: experiments/phase2/preflight.py:49-56; experiments/phase2/train_sft.py:77-101]. `rows_plan` is a
  declared field (beside the runner-only `stages` and `sampler`), so it loads.

**Plan files (run by `run.sh`; never stamped).**

- `b1_rows.yaml` (B1.5 writes the commands): (0) the CUDA build: `bash experiments/cuda_checker/run_box.sh
  --build-only`, then `/opt/venv/bin/python -I -c "import objdel._gpucheck as g; assert g.build() == 'cuda'"`,
  then `tests/test_gpu_scoring.py` (CPU against CUDA scorer parity, the pair that `policy.chain` adds today to a
  chain that scores [code: policy.py:450-452]); (1) `env_check.sh`; (2) B's GPU smoke by node id (B.9.5):
  `[-m, pytest, -m, gpu, tests/test_train_fast.py::test_g02_is_summary_no_sync,
  tests/test_train_fast.py::test_g08a_smoke]`; (3) `train_rl`, item 2, a soft step (first word `~`), with `--out
  {rd}/b1-rows --steps 260 --budget-usd 2.05`; (3b) `train_rl --merge-last`: if the run crashed, it merges the last
  `trainer/checkpoint-N` into `final/` and records `partial: true` (B1.5); (4) one `final_eval` process, item 3:
  the B1 final model on `lidc-val-shifted` and `lidc-val-edge`. Steps 0-2 are inside item 1. Step 3b takes seconds
  when `final/` exists.
- `a3_measure.yaml` (A3 writes the commands): the build-if-missing step (assert the CUDA build; if the assert fails,
  `run_box.sh --build-only`, then assert again; in V1 the assert passes, so no minutes), then one `final_eval` process on
  R5 (`{rd}/ckpt`): `lidc-val-edge` (item 4, `--out {rd}/eval_val_edge`), then `lidc-val-shifted` with saved
  answers, K = 8, seed 11 (item 5, `--out {rd}/eval_val`). No test step: the test half is `a3_test.yaml`, V3 item 3.
- Why step 0. `sync_up` installs the package with `uv pip install ... -e .` [code: policy.py:399]. CMake builds the
  CPU `_gpucheck` unless `OBJDEL_CUDA=ON` [code: CMakeLists.txt:15]. A `steps:` plan runs its steps as written
  [code: policy.py:432-433]. Without step 0, the B1 rewards and every V1 eval score on the CPU build, and the GPU
  smoke skips. The build goes into `/opt/venv`, so `a3_measure.yaml` on the same box uses it. `run_box.sh` swaps 4
  CUDA compiler wheels in the training venv (13.4 to 13.0); the full RL run trained after the same swap [code:
  experiments/phase2/configs/rl_full.yaml:25; measured: runs/k1/checker_gpu.log:12-22]. On a CUDA build
  `final_eval` uses pool size 1, as A2 step 2 does, so no forked worker opens its own CUDA context (A3 adds the
  cap). The eval minutes below were measured on the CPU build.

**Launch lines** (main agent, after the 6.1 step 0 approval; `<run>` = the V1 run id):

```
launch.sh OFFER <run> --config experiments/phase2/configs/b1_launch.yaml --cap-hours <floor_to_0.05((2.40 - b) / r_s)> --owner-approved
sync_up.sh <run> && fetch_hf.sh <run> rl-full-3ep && fetch_hf.sh <run> --rows <rows_revision> lidc-train-b1
sed "s#__REPO__#$PWD#g" experiments/phase2/vast/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist > ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist && launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist   # pull job: checkpoints to the Mac every 20 min
run.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/b1_rows.yaml       # items 2-3; wait for EXIT
run.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/a3_measure.yaml    # items 4-5; start right after the b1_rows EXIT; no spend check in between
pull.sh <run> && push_hf.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/b1_launch.yaml && teardown.sh <run> && sweep_orphans.sh
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist
```

Why the pull job (final round 11, fresh-arch-2). Without it, nothing moves checkpoints off the box during the 2-3 h
run, and a lost host loses every checkpoint. The job runs `pull.sh` every 1,200 s [code:
experiments/phase2/vast/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist:11]; `pull.sh` with no run id pulls every active run [code:
policy.py:502]. Its bandwidth is already in r_s: `UP_GB_PER_H = 6` is "checkpoint pulls of 3-5 GB per 20 min"
[code: policy.py:59-61]. It is not loaded today [measured: `launchctl list | grep objdel` empty, 2026-11-09]. One
side effect: the watchdog destroys an idle box 30 min after a pulled `EXIT` [code: policy.py:603, `--idle-minutes`
default 30], so `a3_measure.yaml` must start within minutes of the `b1_rows` `EXIT`, as today.

At the planning values the cap is 3.35 h = 201 min [estimate: (2.40 - 0.10) / 0.680 = 3.39 h, rounded down].

The launch lines need five code changes on the tag (B1.5 and A3 own them):
- `fetch_hf.sh <run> --rows REV ROOT`. Today `cmd_fetch_hf` pulls only a checkpoint revision into `{rd}/ckpt` [code:
  policy.py:527-536]. The token reaches the box only on ssh stdin, so a plan step cannot fetch the private repo. The
  rows root lands at `{data}/rows/lidc-train-b1/` and the call checks its manifest SHA-256 on the box (B1.5
  "Rows-root download"). B1.5 also adds `--as NAME` for a checkpoint revision (V3 item 0).
- `train_rl --rows-revision HEX40 --rows-manifest-sha256 HEX64`. The rows SHA check reads the flag. E2.1's `to_argv`
  uses these spellings.
- `push_hf.sh` of a `train_rl` output. Today `hf_push` pushes only `<run>/branches/<selected>` of an SFT run [code:
  experiments/phase2/hf_push.py:1-13]. `cmd_push_hf` runs `hf_push` on the box, with the token on ssh stdin, and takes
  the revision from the config's `output_dir` [code: policy.py:511-524]. So it runs before teardown, and its minutes
  are in the pull/push/teardown time after item 5. It writes the B1 final model (`final/`) and the unmerged B1 final
  adapter (`final_adapter/`, saved by `train_rl` before the merge) to revision `b1-rows`. B2.3b's box part and the
  F check comparator (B2.2 F step 4) read the adapter.
- `BudgetStop` on session spend. It computes session spend as `policy.accrued` does for the live run: fixed b plus
  r_s x (now - `started`) [code: policy.py:190-193]. `run.sh` exports, from the active-run record [code:
  policy.py:321-323]: `OBJDEL_SESSION_START` = `started`, `OBJDEL_RATE_USD_PER_H` = `dph` + 6 x `inet_up_cost`, and
  `OBJDEL_FIXED_USD` = 15 x `inet_down_cost`. `train_rl` reads them as the defaults of `--session-start`,
  `--rate-usd-per-h` and `--fixed-usd`. `--budget-usd` without a session start is an argparse error. Why: a clock that
  starts with the process trips 17-31 min late (launch to first sync, plus the downloads). A rate without bandwidth
  trips about $0.10 + $0.039/h late. Either way the cap then ends the box before items 3-5.
- `final_eval --view` may repeat (A3), with one `--out` per view. One store preload and one trainer build per
  checkpoint; one output folder and one `seconds` record per view. A unit test: two views give the same items as two
  separate calls (same seed).

Pull, adapter push and teardown run after item 5, inside the cap or the 600 s `PULL_S` window [code: policy.py:73,
321]. The worst case below counts them.

Notes:

- Why items 3-5 always fit. The eval tail is items 3-5 (20.8 min) plus about 5.2 min for the untimed imports of the
  two eval processes: 26 min [estimate]. `BudgetStop` at $2.05 ends training at session minute
  (2.05 - 0.10) / 0.01133 = 172.3 at the latest, and 172.3 + 26 = 198.3 <= 201. For any offer inside the offer
  limit, $2.40 - $2.05 = $0.35 buys at least 30.9 min, more than the 26 min of the tail plus the 3 min that the
  rounding of the cap can take [estimate: arithmetic].
- Why 260 steps. Step 1 starts at session minute 33-53. Launch to the first `run` row took 17.7, 24.1 and 38.2 min
  (rl, r4, r5) [measured: ledger.csv]. Then come the CUDA build (about 3 min [estimate: D.8]), `env_check` (about
  1 min [measured: runs/r5/r5_shared.log:39]), the smoke (< 5 min) and the `train_rl` start-up (about 6 min,
  section 6 inputs). The rows-root download is not in the measured rows. At 27.5 s and a 53-min start, 260 steps
  end at minute 53 + 119.2 = 172.2, before the stop. 300 steps would end at minute 190.5, so `BudgetStop` would cut
  them at about step 260 [estimate: (172.3 - 53) x 60 / 27.5]. With the 53-min start the stop trips only above
  about 27.5 s per step; with the r4 start (39 min) only above about 30.7 s [estimate: (172.3 - 53) x 60 / 260;
  (172.3 - 39.1) x 60 / 260]. If it trips, the adapter is saved and items 3-5 still run. 300 steps need a higher
  stop and amount: owner decision 2 lists that option.
- Worst case. `run.sh` ends every plan job at the cap [code: policy.py:480], so session spend at the cap is at most
  $2.40 ($2.38 at planning values). The 600 s `PULL_S` window for pull, push and teardown adds at most $0.11. So the
  worst case is $2.49. `launch_refusal` checks exactly this: $16.90 + $2.49 = $19.39 <= $19.90. With the $0.25
  reserve: $2.49 + $0.25 = $2.74 <= $3.00.
- So no V1 item has a skip rule, and no V1 rule reads the ledger total. Owner decision 2 (99_back) has no $2.20 or
  $2.30 option. If the owner keeps $2.20 anyway: the cap is 3.05 h = 183 min, `--budget-usd` is $1.85, and the run
  plans 220 steps (a multiple of 20) [estimate: (1.85 - 0.10) / 0.01133 = 154.6 min; (154.6 - 53) x 60 / 27.5 = 221
  steps]. This plan uses $2.40 and 260 steps.
- Gate B1 has five inputs, all made in V1 or on the Mac: (a) item 3 shifted; (b) item 3 edge; (c) item 4; (d) item
  5; (e) the noise floor from A3 step 7 (two K = 4 halves of item 5, $0). The main rule pairs item 3 with item 5
  (A3's R5 val items: same frozen view, same box). R5's `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl` is a second line.
- Fallback, only if the R5 process (items 4-5) gives no output: Gate B1 pairs with R5's `items.jsonl`. The
  view-identity rule is then "hash only, correlation not run": the frozen `lidc-val-shifted` `target_set_sha256`
  must equal the one in the view manifest that R5's eval scored, and the report says so. `a3_measure.yaml` then runs
  again as V2 item 1b. B.6.2 and U49 follow this rule.
- The edge rule under the fallback. Item 4 is the only R5 edge baseline: `runs/r5/eval/` holds `eval_val` and
  `eval_test` only [measured: ls, 2026-11-09]. If item 4 gave output and item 5 did not, the edge rule pairs with
  item 4, and only the shifted rules use the fallback above. If item 4 gave no output, the edge rule has no
  baseline. Gate B1 is then "open: edge baseline missing" and is never a pass. The other Gate B1 rules are still
  computed and printed. Under a raise, V2 item 1b (with item 1, its launch) runs first and gives the baseline; then
  Gate B1 is decided. Under (b'), or when item 1b fails again, Gate B1 takes row 4 of section 1.1 (stop, owner
  review) with the reason "edge baseline missing". B.6.2 and U49 follow this rule.
- Out of V1: B2.3b's box part (15 min [estimate: B2.3b]) moves to V3. A3's test half (R5 test re-score, 10.6 min =
  634 s; A-G3 and D7's test answers) moves to V3 as `a3_test.yaml`. Every user of A3's answers before V3 reads val
  only.
- B.8.1 (B-S1) and A.8 point to this table and hold no copy.

### 6.3 V2, V3 and V4: only after a budget raise

Money left after V1 (reserve $0.25): at 27.5 s: $3.00 - $2.29 - $0.25 = $0.46, which is 31 min of a rental after
its fixed bandwidth b. At 23.65 s: $3.00 - $2.10 - $0.25 = $0.65, which is 48 min [estimate: arithmetic at r_s].
No V2 subset that gives a gate result fits that money. Item 1 alone costs $0.58. Items 1 + 2 cost $0.73, and items
1 + 1b cost $0.70. The cap formula ends every plan job at the cap [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:480], so
a V2 on $0.46-0.65 ends inside item 1 or item 2 and gives no gate result. V4 ($0.71, below) does not fit
$0.46-0.65 either. Rule: under the default (b') (owner decision 1) no rental follows V1. V2, V3 and V4 each wait for a budget
raise, and the money left stays unspent as a second reserve.

inputs). The check arm continues in the fast arm's process after step 17 (steps 18-32, with
`--check-rope-every 1 --check-meta-every 1 --record-batches` switched on at step 18; step times after step 17 are not
used by C-G-SP1). Every C arm trains on the B1 rows root, and `train_rl` trains only whole 20-step blocks (B1.3), so
the 17-step arms run `--steps 20` and the fast arm `--steps 40` (C0 files; the extra steps are not read).

- One preset for the C arms. The C0 baseline arm and the fast arm run under `bf16-seqmask` with the merged push.

  F arm. The F check is the first 15 steps of the first run after Gate B3 (B2.4 rule 0). That run reports its step
  time against the B3 run as a report line; C-G-SP1 is not re-gated under F.
- One data path. Every C arm (baseline, fast, check, 3c, 3d) trains on the B1 rows root with the B1.5 rows flags

  path; and a C-G-SP1 pass then describes the B3 run, which trains on the same root. `c_speed_check` does not wait
  for A3's answers. The V2 bundle is the default LIDC bundle (no `lidc-train-*` view). The Mac half of C-G-EQ2/3 runs
  on A3's val answers and must pass before V3, not before V2 (C.6; order rule 3).

```
sync_up.sh <run> && fetch_hf.sh <run> rl-full-3ep && fetch_hf.sh <run> --rows <rows_revision> lidc-train-b1   # {rd}/ckpt and the rows root: every C arm reads both

pull.sh <run> && teardown.sh <run> && sweep_orphans.sh     # item 5 (K3), if C1 step 7 fires, runs before this line
```

destroy an idle box 30 min after a pulled `EXIT` [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:603].

  them on the Mac.
- One definition: B-S2 (B.8.1) is V3 items 0 and 4, the only required V3 items. Items 1, 2a, 2b, 3 and 5 are
  optional rows. Each runs only if the owner names it in the V3 approval, and its dollars are then in the amount.
  B.8.1 points here.
- V3 amount rule. The approved amount = the session spend at the end of the 260 B3 steps at 27.5 s (every approved
  item before item 4 included) + $0.35 + item 5's $ when it is planned. 6.4 rule 5 then gives a `BudgetStop` that
  does not cut the 260 steps at 27.5 s. Items 0 + 4: B3 step 1 starts at minute 39 + 14 + 13 = 66 (the 13 min are
  the B1 re-eval of B3.9 step 2) and step 260 ends at minute 185.2, so `BudgetStop` = $0.10 + 185.2 x $0.01133 =
  $2.20 (rounded up) and the amount is $2.55. Items 0, 1, 3 and 4: step 1 starts at minute 39 + 46 + 13.6 + 14 + 13
  = 125.6, step 260 ends at minute 244.8, so `BudgetStop` = $0.10 + 244.8 x $0.01133 = $2.88 (rounded up) and the
  amount is $3.23 [estimate: arithmetic at r_s]. Item 2a adds 15 min ($0.17) to both values,
  item 2b 41.5 min ($0.47). Worst case = amount + $0.11 (`PULL_S`, as in 6.2).

**V3 launch config (the one file that `make preflight` stamps for V3).** `experiments/phase2/configs/b3_launch.yaml`,
a `RunArgs` file. B3.9 creates it beside `b3_v5.yaml`. With `rows_plan` set, the stamp holds the rows-root SHA-256
and the "ROWS root" check of B3's `train_rl` stage (6.2 "How the rows root enters the stamp"). `output_dir` is the
HF revision of the B3 push, and `b3_v5.yaml` writes `--out {rd}/b3-v5`.

```
model: qwen3-vl-2b
view: views/lidc-bundle-v3
seed: 1
output_dir: b3-v5                     # push_hf.sh uses it as the HF revision
rows_plan: experiments/phase2/configs/b3_v5.yaml
```

**V3 launch lines** (`<run>` = the V3 run id; one `run.sh` call per item, in table order; skipped items have no
call; between two calls the main agent applies 6.4 rule 2):

```
launch.sh OFFER <run> --config experiments/phase2/configs/b3_launch.yaml --cap-hours <floor_to_0.05((approved - b) / r_s)> --owner-approved
sync_up.sh <run> && fetch_hf.sh <run> rl-full-3ep && fetch_hf.sh <run> b1-rows --as b1 && fetch_hf.sh <run> --rows <rows_revision> lidc-train-b1
sed "s#__REPO__#$PWD#g" experiments/phase2/vast/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist > ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist && launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist   # pull job, as 6.2
run.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/d_gpu_test.yaml    # item 1, only if approved (R-D2, then A's G02b and G03 as its step 2)
run.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/b2_fp16.yaml       # item 2b, only if approved (item 2a uses the B2.3b box command)
run.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/a3_test.yaml       # item 3, only if approved
run.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/b3_v5.yaml         # item 4; wait for EXIT
pull.sh <run> && push_hf.sh <run> experiments/phase2/configs/b3_launch.yaml && teardown.sh <run> && sweep_orphans.sh
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.objdel.vast.pull.plist
```

The pull job is the one of 6.2 (final round 14, rl-2). Without it a lost host loses every B3 checkpoint, and no later
$0 merge is possible. 6.2 "Why the pull job" gives the reason and the 30-min idle destroy after a pulled `EXIT`. Here
the idle rule also applies between two `run.sh` calls: the main agent starts the next call within minutes of the last
`EXIT`. A `train_rl` crash is covered on the box: `b3_v5.yaml` step 3 is soft and step 3b runs `--merge-last` (B3.9).

After the V3 `pull.sh`, on the Mac ($0): `OBJDEL_V3_RUN=<run> make test-data`. D's S13 reads the D-G14, D-G15 and
D-G17 records from `runs/<run>/` only when `OBJDEL_V3_RUN` is set; without it S13 skips (D.9.6), so `make test-data`
stays green when V3 never runs.

**V4** (optional, after E, owner decision; needs a budget raise: after V1, $0.46-0.65 is left, and V4 costs $0.71):
E-G10 box part (prompt ids and SamplingParams equal; TOST sampler arm on val), E4 deterministic check and E-G13.
Plan file: `specs/e_v4.yaml` (E.8 writes its commands). Step 0 is the CUDA build of
`b1_rows.yaml` step 0 (6.2). Without it `sync_up` leaves the CPU build [code: policy.py:399; CMakeLists.txt:15]: the
A.9 hook then fails GP1-GP4, and the sampler arm scores on the CPU checker. Then come `env_check.sh` (E-G13), the E.9
box test list, and the sampler-arm `final_eval` (pool size 1, as A3). A B run follows E only on the post-E raise
path ("End state under (b')"); there Gate B3 pairs within V3 (B3.9 step 2, the B1 re-eval), so the sampler change
cannot enter Gate B3. V4 is its own rental and still closes E-G10. It is priced on the V2 and V3 basis: launch to first `run` up to 38.2 min (sync and the checkpoint
download included) [measured: ledger.csv r5 launch and first `run` rows] + build 3 + `env_check` 1 + box tests 2 +
sampler eval 7 + untimed eval-process imports 2.6 = about 54 min = $0.71 at r_s [estimate: E.8 for the work
minutes; 6.2 notes for the imports]. Approved amount: $0.75, so the cap is 0.95 h = 57 min at planning values
[estimate: (0.75 - 0.10) / 0.680 = 0.956 h, rounded down]. Worst case with the 600 s `PULL_S` window: $0.86. This
is the one V4 price; E.8, E owner decision 7 and 99_back decision 3b point here.

**V4 launch config.** `e_v4.yaml` itself. After E6 it is a `RunSpec`, and `make preflight` stamps it (E6 step 8b),
so it is both the launch config and the plan file. Before V4: `make preflight CONFIG=specs/e_v4.yaml`.

**V4 launch lines** (`<run>` = the V4 run id):

```
launch.sh OFFER <run> --config specs/e_v4.yaml --cap-hours <floor_to_0.05((0.75 - b) / r_s)> --owner-approved
sync_up.sh <run> && fetch_hf.sh <run> rl-full-3ep          # to {rd}/ckpt: the R5 final model, the TOST trainer arm's checkpoint
run.sh <run> specs/e_v4.yaml                               # steps 0-3 of E.8; wait for EXIT
pull.sh <run> && teardown.sh <run> && sweep_orphans.sh     # no push_hf.sh: V4 trains nothing, and push_target dies on e_v4.yaml (E6 step 8b)
```

After `pull.sh`, the Mac computes the TOST from the pulled sampler-arm items (E.9 GP5). E-G10's box half passes when
GP4 passes on the box and GP5 passes on the Mac. The old samplers (`sample_vllm.py`,
`hf_sample.py`) go to `archive/phase2_samplers/` in the E4 step 3 commit, not after V4, so the (b') end state holds
no old code beside new code. `final_eval` uses the new sampler from that commit on. The old samplers and the old
trainer eval path stay in git history: the owner tags the last commit before E4 step 3 `pre-e4-eval`. If V4 fails,
E4 step 1's V4-failure rule applies: fix forward in the new sampler, no restore (final round 15, arch-1). The trainer
arm of the TOST is already on disk (`runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl`, E4 gate).

**Totals for owner decision 1** (99_back points here) [estimate: sums of the rows above]:
- (b') keep $3: V1 only. V2, V3 and V4 wait for a budget raise. The money left ($0.46-0.65) stays unspent as a
  second reserve. No V2 subset gives a gate result: item 1 alone costs $0.58, and items 1-3 cost $1.21.
- (a) B1 then B3: V1 + B-S2 + reserve = $2.29 + $2.32 + $0.25 = $4.86 at 27.5 s ($2.10 + $2.13 + $0.25 = $4.48 at
  23.65 s); the V3 approved amount is $2.55 (V3 amount rule). With V3 items 1 and 3 (R-D2 and A's test half):
  $2.29 + $2.99 + $0.25 = $5.53 at 27.5 s; the V3 approved amount is $3.23. The V2 items for C adoption add $1.21
  ($6.07 at 27.5 s with B-S2 only). V4 adds $0.71 (approved amount $0.75).
- (c) one merged run (B1 rows and reward v5, V1 shape): costs as V1 ($2.10-2.29); it loses the B1-vs-B3 split.
- Any raise also raises `HARD_STOP` by the same amount (6.1 step 0).

Phase E costs $0 on the Mac. DOC and CLEAN cost $0.

### 6.4 Stop rules (all rentals)

1. Preflight fails: no rental.
2. Session spend reaches 90 % of the amount the owner approved: stop new items that the rental table marks
   skippable, save, teardown. An item whose full cost still fits under the cap is not stopped. Items marked "not
   skippable" run only if the cap still covers their minutes. V1 has no skippable item. `policy.chain` has no
   spend-based skip (a leading `~` only lets a step fail [code: policy.py:424]). So the main agent applies this rule
   on the Mac, between two `run.sh` calls, from `policy.spend()` minus the spend at launch.
3. A launch fails, or the box has no first sync in 35 min (good launches took 17-31 min): tear down at once.
4. A gate fails: stop that item. Do the isolation on the Mac with the CPU build. K1, K2, K3 each have an isolation
   order in their `DESIGN.md`. Do not retry on the box until the Mac shows the cause.
5. `BudgetStop` ends a training run at a session-spend value and saves the adapter. Its clock starts at the launch
   time, and it adds the bandwidth estimate as `policy.accrued` does (6.2). Its value is: approved amount - $0.35
   (the 26-min eval tail plus the cap rounding) - the $ of every later item in the same rental. V1: $2.40 - $0.35 =
   $2.05. The plan's eval steps then run, and the box is torn down.
6. Teardown and `sweep_orphans.sh` after every rental, also after an error.
7. Nothing from `data/` leaves the Mac except LIDC-only artifacts: the B1 rows root, the LIDC eval views named in the rental's
   table, the bundle's `checker_eval/` set (K1's raw masks are built from it on the box, section 5), and the LIDC val
   views that the bundle and the stamp always need
   (`bundle.LIDC_EVAL` and `preflight.EXAMS`: `lidc-val-shifted`, `lidc-val-rescaled`, `lidc-val-rotated`,
   `probe-precision`, `probe-topology`) [code: experiments/phase2/vast/bundle.py:26, 58-60; preflight.py:28]. The
   bundle ships every `data/eval_views/lidc-*` folder [code: bundle.py:53-62]. So only a `lidc-test-*` view is moved
   out before a rental whose table does not name it (6.1 step 4c). RIGA never leaves. The code sync also ships
   `docs/reference/frozen_views.json` (hashes, LIDC item ids, commits) and `docs/reference/val_halves.json` (LIDC
   patient ids, item ids, counts) through the B1.6 keep rule. Neither holds pixels.
8. No rule reads the ledger total ($16.90) as a session amount. "Session spend" (section 0) is the only spend that a
   stop rule, a skip rule or `BudgetStop` reads.

The box toolchain for V2 and V3 is `cuda-toolkit[nvcc,cccl,nvtx]==13.0.3` and `nvidia-cuda-sanitizer-api==13.4.92`.
This is what `experiments/cuda_checker/run_box.sh` installs after D1 adds the `nvtx` extra. Today it installs
`[nvcc,cccl]` only [code: experiments/cuda_checker/run_box.sh:24].

## 7. Risk register

| # | Risk | Likelihood / impact | Mitigation | Owner of the call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR1 | B2, B3 and the C checks do not fit $3 after the B1 run | High / High | Section 6.3 holds the prices: the V2 items for C adoption do not fit at either step time. B1 runs first and whole. V2, V3 and V4 wait for a budget raise | Owner |
| FR2 | Data fix does not close the miss gap | Medium / High | Gate B1 is paired with patient CIs. Section 1.1 names the next step for each Gate B1 result, approved before V1. 4B gate on val (section 3); B3 reward for misses | Owner |
| FR3 | Shifted rows lengthen the decode tail, so the step is above 23.65 s | Medium / Medium | Costs use 27.5 s as the base (section 6); C7 outline limit after the A8 count | Owner |
| FR4 | Trainer-vLLM mismatch (IS ratio min 0 in 98.1 % of 770 steps) stays | Medium / Medium | B2.0 merge-rounding table ($0) and the B1 run's counterfactual stats (B2.1 is on the `v1-b1` tag); preset for the runs after Gate B3 chosen by B2.4 (F, A or E); the F check in the first 15 steps of the first run after Gate B3; optional fp16 arm in V3; no-merge LoRA sync | Main agent |
| FR5 | Private TRL names change (TRL 1.17.1 pinned) | Low / High | `trl_adapter.check()` in A7 (raises `TRLContractError`); single adapter | Main agent |
| FR6 | Kernels pass the CPU but fail on the GPU (first GPU run) | Medium / Low | CPU build is the same source; V2 stops per item; torch-op path for C1 | Main agent |
| FR7 | Moving files (E) changes a result | Low / High | E0 move-invariance goldens; E gates after each commit | Main agent |
| FR8 | Archive removes something still used | Low / Medium | CLEAN0 safety tag; hygiene test; owner runs the git commands | Owner |
| FR9 | Hashed target sets change when the polygonizer switches to CUDA | Low / High | D gate: target hashes byte-identical; K1 parity on 37,093 masks | Main agent |
| FR10 | 4B memory or time estimate is wrong | Medium / Medium | Do not spend before the 15-step probe | Owner |
| FR11 | Data leaks across splits | Low / High | B-DG1, B-DG1b (rows root), B-DG2, B-DG3 (patient, SHA-256, near duplicate) before any spend; B-DG15 frozen test and val-edge views; all 21 B data gates (B-DG1..B-DG18) pass first | Main agent |
| FR12 | Vast host quality (failed launch, slow image pull) | Medium / Low | Reserve $0.25; reliability filter; 35-minute stop rule | Main agent |
| FR13 | Docs drift again, or tracked docs cite the scratchpad | Medium / Low | DOC4 drift tests; one source for headline numbers; a check for `/[p]rivate/tmp`, `/[U]sers/` and scratchpad paths | Main agent |
| FR14 | Trackio or TRL logging breaks FastGRPO timers | Low / Low | Trackio is deferred; Mac CPU smoke with `report_to="trackio"` before any adoption | Main agent |
| FR15 | The code budget guard refuses V1, or its hourly sweep destroys the box mid-run (`HARD_STOP` 17.5 against $16.90 spent) | High / High (if not fixed) | Section 6.1 step 0 (`HARD_STOP` = $19.90 with owner approval, unit test) and step 4b | Owner |
| FR16 | Host lost, or `train_rl` crashes, during the V1 or V3 run | Medium / High | The Mac pull job copies checkpoints off the box every 20 min (6.2 launch lines). `b1_rows.yaml` step 3 is soft, and step 3b (`train_rl --merge-last`) merges the last checkpoint into `final/` with `partial: true`, so the B1 eval still runs after a crash (1.1 row "B1 stopped early"). V3 has the same guards: the pull job in the 6.3 launch lines, and `b3_v5.yaml` steps 3 (soft) and 3b (B3.9). After a host loss, `train_rl --resume` from the pulled checkpoint needs a new rental. Under (b') the money left ($0.46-0.65) does not buy one; the owner hears this before V1 (6.1 step 0) | Main agent |

## 8. How to read the phase sections

Each phase file is one H1 section, "Phase X: ...". Its headings carry the phase letter: `A.1`, `B.4`, `E.9.1`. The
unnumbered parts are `X.0` (skills used) and, in CLEAN, `CLEAN.Q`. The same parts appear in each:

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| Skills used | Which skill changed what |
| 1 Goal and why | Measured problem, target, gate |
| 2 Research basis | Papers and notes, one line each |
| 3 Design | Box diagram, data flow, GPU versus CPU |
| 4 Tasks | Numbered tasks (A1..., B1..., C0..., D1..., E0..., DOC1..., CLEAN0...) with steps and files |
| 5 Custom kernels used | Which of K1-K3 the phase uses |
| 6 Acceptance gates | Measurable pass rules, with the id prefix of section 0 |
| 7 Risks and rollback | What can fail, how to undo |
| 8 Cost, time, dependencies | A pointer to the rental items of section 6 (no copy of a rental table), the phase's own work breakdown and Mac time; what each phase needs from others |
| 9 Tests | Test list by level, with pytest sketches (not run: the code under test does not exist yet) |

**Review log.** Each phase source keeps its review logs (`X.R`, `X.Rn` and every "Review log ..." section). The
assembler moves all of them, in phase order, into `docs/implementation2.0/review-log.md`. So this plan shows no review
log, and a "Review log" reference in a phase points to that file.

A reference like "section 3.1" inside a phase means that phase's section. Tags mean the same everywhere (section 0).
The doc order is: A, B, C, D, E, DOC, CLEAN, then the owner decisions, open questions and sources.

# Phase A: measure fairly

Paths are relative to the repo root. No path points at the session scratchpad.
- The test writers' contract is `docs/implementation2.0/specs/A.spec.md`. DOC copies it there from the session.
- Where `A.spec.md` and this phase section differ, this phase section is the rule. Known differences that
  `phases/A.spec.md` must take before DOC1 step 0 copies it (final r11 data-1): §3.2 takes the A1 "Output keys"
  list (`paired` and `iou_found` carry `ci95_patient` as the gate CI, `ci95_nodule` as the second line; plus
  `gate_ci`, `signal.cluster_t` and `view_content_sha256`); §5 item 7 takes A-G3 (TOST: the 90 % patient CI of the
  paired difference inside ±0.01, view identity, the frozen-view hash); §5 item 8 takes A-G4 (Gate A on the lower end
  of the paired patient CI); its revision line names this file's latest review round.
- `notes/X.md` means `docs/research/notes/impl_2026-11-08/X.md`. DOC copies each cited session note there.
- The kernel designs are `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1/DESIGN.md` and `.../K2/DESIGN.md` (already in the repo tree).

Tags: [measured: file or command, 2026-11-08 unless dated], [code: file:line], [paper: arXiv id], [web: URL],
[estimate], [unverified] (a claim not yet checked; none is load-bearing).

Words (one word for each thing; the code name is given once):
- **doctor**: one radiologist outline. Code name: `rater`. A **voting doctor** has a topology vote (`cache.voters`).
- **answer**: one model output text. Code name: `sample`; TRL name: `completion`. K = 8 answers per image.
- **view**: the window the model sees (code: `view`, B1 code: `window`). **image**: the pixels of one view.
- **miss** (the K-mean rule): an image whose mean IoU_tc over its K = 8 answers is below 0.1. **found image**: not a
  miss. **missed answer**: one answer with IoU_tc below 0.1. Every miss number in this phase uses the K-mean rule.
- **gate CI**: the 95 % patient-cluster bootstrap CI (key `group_id`). The nodule and item CIs are second lines.
- **R5 step**: 23.65 s (mean over all steps) [measured: runs/r5/shared_rl.json `timing_s.per_step`].

## A.1. Goal and why

**Goal.** Every number that steers Phases B to E must be fair and repeatable. Before we spend on training, we need:
honest intervals, a fair human ceiling, all answers saved, a label-free answer choice, the standard metrics, time marks
in each step, a guard on TRL internals, and a true count of outline lengths.

Evidence:

1. **The intervals are too narrow.** `final_eval.summarize` resamples single images
   [code: experiments/phase2/final_eval.py:33-43]. About 5.5 images come from each nodule. The test set has 2,200
   items, 401 nodules, 160 CT series and 158 patients [measured: runs/r5/eval/eval_test/items.jsonl with `group_id`
   from data/store/lidc/test.parquet]. Bootstrap of the R5 test items (B = 2,000, seed 0):
   - item: IoU_tc 0.6448, CI [0.6334, 0.6562], width 0.023 [measured: final_eval.json];
   - nodule (`signal.draws`): CI [0.6279, 0.6621], width 0.034 [measured: `signal.ci` on the R5 test items, 2026-11-08];
   - patient (`group_id`, the key A1 uses): CI [0.6252288200704239, 0.6644106494958667], width 0.039
     [measured: 2026-11-08].
   The repo already has the nodule bootstrap. Only `final_eval` does not use it [code: src/objdel/eval/signal.py:98-119].
   The patient is the independent unit. All nodules of one scan share its reading sessions, scanner and
   reconstruction, and reader 1 in one XML is not the same radiologist as reader 1 in another (final r1 data
   review, item 2). So the patient CI is the gate CI. Val has 1,084 items from 78 patients; test has 2,200 items from
   158 patients [measured: R5 items.jsonl joined with `group_id` of data/store/lidc/{val,test}.parquet].
   Every CI here covers data variance only. It excludes training-seed variance: all runs so far use seed 0.
   Training-seed variance is not measured, so a gain is a single-run result. A3 step 7 reports the K = 8
   sampling noise; the paired patient CI of every gate already contains it. It is not a seed-noise measure.
2. **The ceiling favours the model, and no committed script makes it.** 0.732 (test) and 0.734 (val) appear only in prose
   (0.734 is the found-image value on val; the whole-val legacy value is 0.723 [measured: notes/r8data/legacy.py
   and legacy_found.py, 2026-11-08])
   [code: docs/research/notes/rl_plateau_diagnosis_2026-11-08.md:42; Direction.md:327]. Each doctor is compared with
   k - 1 doctors, and the model with all k doctors. Also, the doctor uses best IoU with no topology rule, while the model
   uses IoU_tc [code: docs/glossary.md:59 per notes/A1.md F3].
3. **The answers are lost.** `final_eval` keeps only K-sample means of 7 numbers. It never writes the 8 texts, and it
   writes every file only after scoring [code: final_eval.py:26-30,65-84]. So best-of-8, the medoid and the pixel
   vote cannot be computed afterwards, and a crash in scoring loses the 17.5 min of sampling.
4. **The metrics are computed but hidden.** `metrics()` already returns GED, HM-IoU, soft Dice and NSD per item
   [code: src/objdel/eval/metrics.py:322-324]. `final_eval.per_item` drops them. Boundary IoU does not exist
   (grep: no match).
5. **No time marks on the GPU.** There is no NVTX range in `src/`, `cuda/` or `experiments/phase2/*.py` [measured: grep].
   The R5 step is 23.65 s [measured: runs/r5/shared_rl.json] and the GPU idles about 40 % of it [BRIEF §2]. Phase C needs a trace before it changes speed.
   `experiments/phase2/profile.py` already computes the GPU busy share and host-wait counts from a torch.profiler
   trace (`busy`, `GPU_CATS`, `SYNCS`) [code: profile.py:43-44,77-99]. A6 reuses that code.
6. **TRL internals are unguarded.** FastGRPO overrides 6 private GRPOTrainer methods, swaps 1 module global, assigns
   1 private VLLMGeneration method and reads 2 private attributes [code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:501-503,524,549,
   561,567,575,618,638,650]. It also reads 13 undocumented attributes (`use_vllm`, `loss_type`, `num_iterations`,
   the 4 `vllm_importance_sampling_*` settings, `vllm_generation.{llm, model, sync_weights}`, ...) and 4 input keys,
   and it copies TRL's ratio code [code: fast.py:351-363,540-603,652-690]. TRL is pinned at 1.17.1
   [code: pyproject.toml:21], but no check runs at start-up.
7. **The outline limit needs a true count.** On centred LIDC train targets the longest doctor outline is 1,182 tokens
   (0 of 23,469 above 1,200) [measured: notes/A1.md F9, Qwen3-VL-2B tokenizer]. Every outline length in A counts the
   end token (the `sft_rows` rule, A8 step 2). Without the end token the same outline is 1,181 tokens
   [measured: notes/B1.md:90]. The shifted and rescaled train views
   already exist on the Mac: `data/views/lidc-train-{shifted,rescaled}`, 7,341 records each, built 2026-11-08
   [measured: `wc -l`, manifest.json]. They are not counted yet. The model's own answer lengths (38 % of R5 steps hit
   1,536 [BRIEF §2]) are not counted either.

## A.2. Research basis

| Source | Id | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| Kohl et al., Probabilistic U-Net (GED, App. B) | [paper: arXiv 1806.05034] | GED = 2E d(S,Y) - E d(S,S') - E d(Y,Y'), d = 1 - IoU; already in `metrics._ged` |
| Kohl et al., HPU-Net (HM-IoU) | [paper: arXiv 1905.13077] | Hungarian-matched IoU of samples to raters |
| CAR (HM-IoU16 protocol) | [paper: arXiv 2006.13144] | K = 16 in the published protocol; we have K = 8, so we label the key HM-IoU8 |
| Cheng et al., Boundary IoU | [paper: arXiv 2103.16562] | IoU of the inner d-px bands; official `mask_to_boundary`: 1-px zero pad, 3x3 ones kernel, `cv2.erode` d iterations, mask minus eroded [web: github.com/bowenc0221/boundary-iou-api] |
| Nikolov et al., NSD; Metrics Reloaded | [paper: arXiv 1809.04430; 2206.01653] | NSD@tau is the default boundary metric; already in `metrics.nsd` |
| Navigating Uncertainty in Medical Image Segmentation | [paper: arXiv 2407.16367] | GED mixes detection and shape. So report the miss rate and IoU on found images beside it (abstract read; full text not read) |
| QUBIQ soft Dice | [paper: arXiv 2405.18435] | Thresholded soft Dice; ours uses 5 thresholds [code: metrics.py:44-46] |
| Field and Welsh, cluster bootstrap (JRSS-B 2007) | [web: via arXiv 2607.02394 citation; not read] | Resample whole clusters; keep all images of each cluster |
| Bertsch et al., MBR / self-consistency | [paper: arXiv 2310.01387] | Sample-based MBR picks the medoid in utility space. Our utility is IoU between samples |
| PyTorch NVTX and profiler | [code: .venv torch/cuda/nvtx.py:115 `range`; torch/cuda/profiler.py:20-26 `start` calls `cudaProfilerStart`] | No new dependency for ranges and capture windows |
| Nsight Systems capture range | [web: dev-discuss.pytorch.org/t/using-nsight-systems-to-profile-gpu-workload/59] | `nsys profile -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=stop` |
| Nsight Systems stats reports | [web: docs.nvidia.com/nsight-systems/AnalysisGuide; forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/nvtx-with-gpu-timing/268356] | `cuda_api_trace`, `cuda_gpu_trace`, `nvtx_pushpop_trace` give per-event rows. `nvtx_sum` has no nesting and no per-step split. NVTX ranges are CPU times; GPU work runs later (`nvtx_gpu_proj_trace` projects it) |
| verl Nsight profiling | [web: verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/perf/nsight_profiling.html] | Profile chosen steps only, with named role ranges |

Per item, inside `final_eval` (the same code on the box and the Mac):

```
 answer text x8 --> parse --> checker (GPU on box): legal, iou_tc, f5, g_area, topology   (scores only return)
                         \--> to_masks (the checker's raster, check_polygons; masks copied to the host)
                                 --> metrics(): pairwise IoU (8+k+1)^2, GED, HM-IoU8, soft Dice, NSD,
                                     boundary IoU, Dice/prec/recall vs vote
 per-item record --> per_item() --> summarize(): mean + CI by patient (gate CI), by nodule, by item
 sample_iou (8x8) --> select.medoid() --> chosen index --> its iou_tc (no doctor mask is read)
```

### A.3.2 GPU versus CPU

| Work | Where | Why (every CPU item justified) |
|---|---|---|
| Sampling 8 answers per item (vLLM) | GPU | the main cost: 415 s val, 630 s test [measured: runs/r5/eval/*/final_eval.json] |
| Text -> mask, legality, IoU_tc, F5, g_area, topology | GPU (`_gpucheck.score_polygons`) | already on the device; only scores return [code: src/objdel/reward/score.py:1-14,106-124] |
| Text -> mask for the set metrics | GPU raster (`_gpucheck.check_polygons` inside `to_masks`), then a host copy | it is the same checker raster, not a second rasterizer [code: src/objdel/geometry/shape.py:136-148]; equality with the archived CPU checker is tested [code: tests/test_gpu_scoring.py:51-57]. The pixels reach the host only in the test-evaluation path, never in a training step |
| Leave-one-out ceiling scores (A2) | GPU on the box; CPU build of the same source on the Mac | the checker is one source for CPU and nvcc, and the bits are identical [code: score.py:12-13]. The Mac is free and runs offline, so CPU there is the cheaper choice. The box is billed by the minute |
| Leave-one-out `ExpertCache.build` (tau, T5, EDT) | CPU, offline | the cache EDT is OpenCV and is hashed into the reward fingerprint [code: src/objdel/reward/cache.py:130,210-216]. K2's device EDT replaces it in Phase D, with the same bits [docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K2/DESIGN.md §7 item 6]. It never runs inside a training step |
| Set metrics: pairwise IoU, GED, HM-IoU, soft Dice, NSD, boundary IoU, Dice/precision/recall vs vote | CPU (numpy/scipy/OpenCV) in A | (1) it is the test oracle for K2's device kernels (`set_terms`, `surface_words`), which are not yet verified on a GPU [docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K2/DESIGN.md §8 risk 1]; (2) scoring is about 3 s of a 634 s test run [measured: final_eval.json seconds: total - load_and_sample]; (3) it reruns offline from saved answers. Phase D moves the arithmetic to the GPU on the masks `check_polygons` already makes, and must show equality with this code |
| Medoid choice | host argmax over an 8x8 float matrix | only scores, as the owner rule allows; 64 floats |
| Bootstrap CIs | host, numpy | its inputs are per-item scalars (2,200 numbers), which are already on the host by design. `signal.draws` gives exact B2 reproduction [code: signal.py:17-18] |
| NVTX ranges, profiler start/stop | host API calls | they mark GPU time; they launch no GPU work |
| nsys trace analysis (`nsys_baseline.py`) | host numpy and `sqlite3`, offline on the Mac | it reads CSV and SQLite rows of a finished trace; there is no GPU work to do |
| TRL start-up check | host, at trainer start | it inspects Python objects only |
| Token count (A8) | host tokenizer | text-to-id is a host string operation on about 100,000 short strings [estimate: 3 x 23,469 LIDC train targets, plus val, RIGA and 26,272 answers]. It is offline and is the one step with no GPU form |
