#### B1.4a Polygonizer seam over today's engine (before B1.4; final round 11, fresh-arch-3)

The owner rule says the polygonizer must be CUDA. Today's engine already gives the numpy polygonizer's rings:
`check_masks` is IDENTICAL to K1's dump, and K1's dump has 0 mismatches against `objdel.checker.polygonize` on all
37,093 LIDC masks (ring count, every corner, signed area) [measured:
docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1/results/cross_numpy_m3.txt; code: K1/cross_numpy.py:1-8]. It also has 0 mismatches
on an RTX 5090 [measured: docs/research/notes/issues_solved_2026-11-07.md:37]. The binding already returns rings
(`pts`, `ring_start`, `pts_start`, `ring_area`) [code: cuda/gpucheck_py.cpp:140-158]. So the seam lands now, with
today's engine behind it, and D2 later swaps K1 in behind the same seam.
- Create `src/objdel/checker/rings.py` with `polygonize(mask, offset=(0, 0))`: pack the mask, call
  `_gpucheck.check_masks` once, build today's `Ring` objects (same order, corners and signed area), add the offset on
  the host. `Ring` moves from `polygonize.py` to `rings.py`. This is the first part of D3's deep module (D.spec.md
  §3.1); D3 adds `trace` and `MaskRings`.

  `.rings`. `targets/build.py:53` imports it from `objdel.checker`, so it follows with no edit; the cv2 hole grouping

#### B1.4 Build the rows root (script)

- Create `experiments/phase2/build_rl_rows.py`:
  `--store data/store --target-law train-shifted --out data/views/lidc-train-b1 --steps <budgeted, multiple of 20>
  --per-step 32 --draws <n> --shares 0.15 0.75 0.10 --seed 0 --procs 6
  --exclude docs/reference/train_exclusions.json`. `--exclude` is required (no default); a list with no entry is
  the file `{}`. B1.4 runs after B1.7: DG17 must pass first, and its drops are in that file.
- Steps:
  1. `ids = frozenset(json.loads(Path(a.exclude).read_text()))`; `pool(train items, draws=n, exclude=ids)`. Target
     = `cell_shares` of the pool's draw-0 shifted windows (the train shifted law; geometry from the train store
     only; no val data and no model output), so the target is computed without the excluded items. This target equals the test view's
     generator law by choice; the guard views of B1.6 check that the model did not fit only this law.
  2. Choose `draws`: simulate `draws` in (1, 2, 4, 8) with `schedule` + `cell_coverage`; take the smallest value that
     passes DG7-DG9 on every block prefix, does not raise, and uses no disagreement window more than once. If no
     value meets the last condition, take the smallest value that passes the rest (reuse <= 4, B1.2 step 4). Print the
     table with the largest disagreement reuse per value, and record the chosen value's largest reuse in
     `manifest.schedule.disagreement_max_reuse`. (Today one draw fails [measured: SD3
     s5]; the value that passes is not yet measured.)
  3. Materialize only scheduled windows with a public `objdel.train.dataset.window_record(out, item, window)`. It
     calls `_prepare` with **`window.window_id` as the item id** [code: src/objdel/train/dataset.py:102,110: the PNG
     is `images/<id>.png` and the caches `caches/<id>/`]. Passing the source `item_id` would make windows overwrite
     each other's image and caches. Run in a `multiprocessing.Pool(procs)`. Record `item_id = window_id`, plus
     `source_item_id`, `cell`, and `view = {kind, draw, offset: [dx, dy], side, fallback: false, kept_side: false,
     op: "id"}` (same keys as today's view records).
  4. Write `lidc/train.jsonl` in schedule order (NOT sorted by id; the order is the schedule). Run
     `quality.rows_leakage` and all other gates. Write the manifest only after `quality.failures(...)` is empty: the
     usual `files`, `sets`, `reward_fingerprint`, `versions` fields (copy `build_eval_views.build`), plus
     `schedule = {steps, planned_steps, block_steps, per_step, seed, draws, shares, target_law: "train-shifted",
     target_sha256, ids_sha256 (SHA-256 of the newline-joined ordered window ids), dropped,
     disagreement_weight, disagreement_max_reuse, exclusions_sha256 (SHA-256 of the `--exclude` file's bytes),
     excluded_ids (sorted list of its keys), gates}`. `quality.rows_leakage` gets the same `ids`.
  5. Upload the rows root before any rental, so the host downloads it instead of the Mac uploading 1.2-1.6 GB during
     paid time. One place only, set by owner decision B.8.3 item 6 (front-matter owner decision 10): default the
     private model repo `svenk029/objdel-sft` under `rows/lidc-train-b1/`. Upload with one
     `HfApi.upload_folder(...)` call. It commits a large folder in several batches, with " (part N)" commit messages
     [code: .venv huggingface_hub/hf_api.py:5779-5784], and the root holds about 16,640 files (one image and one
     cache per window; today's 7,341-window train view holds 14,684 files [measured: find
     data/views/lidc-train-shifted -type f | wc -l, 2026-11-08]). So record `CommitInfo.oid` of the call's return
     value (the last commit, which holds every file), never a part commit, as `rows_revision`. The manifest's
     `schedule` also gets `files_count` and `files_sha256` (SHA-256 of the newline-joined sorted relative paths of
     the root, without `manifest.json`). Record the SHA-256 of `manifest.json` as `rows_manifest_sha256` in
     `experiments/phase2/configs/b1_rows.yaml`, as
     the `train_rl` flags `--rows-revision <40 hex>` and `--rows-manifest-sha256 <64 hex>` (B1.5). The
     rows root is LIDC only (CC BY 3.0, attribution in the repo README [web:
     https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/lidc-idri/]); RIGA stays on the Mac.
- `build_eval_views._record` also calls `window_record` (the code comment already asks for a public helper: "S1-2:
  needs a public helper (FX-T)" [code: experiments/phase2/build_eval_views.py:63]).
- Tests `tests/test_p2_rows.py`: `--limit`-style run on the fixture; manifest present only when gates pass; rows
  order equals the schedule; every window's PNG path and cache folder is unique; caches load through
  `cache_loader`; image hashes match records; `--steps 30` with `block_steps` 20 is refused.

#### B1.5 Train on the ordered rows

- `experiments/phase2/configs/b1_launch.yaml` (the V1 launch config; B1.3 explains why): a RunArgs file with the
  same `model`, `view` and `seed` keys as `r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml`, `output_dir: b1-rows`, no `branches`, and
  `rows_plan: experiments/phase2/configs/b1_rows.yaml`. `make preflight CONFIG=` names this file only.
- `experiments/phase2/configs/b1_rows.yaml` (a `steps:` plan, run by `run.sh`; rental V1 items 2-3, front 6.2), in
  this step order:
  0. The CUDA build, one `bash -c` step: `bash experiments/cuda_checker/run_box.sh --build-only && /opt/venv/bin/python
     -I -c "import objdel._gpucheck as g; assert g.build() == 'cuda'" && /opt/venv/bin/python -I -m pytest -q -p
     no:cacheprovider tests/test_gpu_scoring.py`. Front 6.2 ("Why step 0") gives the reason: without it the box
     scores on the CPU build.
  1. `bash experiments/phase2/docker/env_check.sh {rd}/ckpt {rd}/env_check.json`.
  2. The GPU smoke by node id: `[-m, pytest, -m, gpu, tests/test_train_fast.py::test_g02_is_summary_no_sync,
     tests/test_train_fast.py::test_g08a_smoke]` (< 5 min; its minutes are in front item 1). `cmd_run` runs a step
     that does not start with `bash` as `/opt/venv/bin/python -I <argv>` [code: policy.py:484-487], so the step
     starts with `-m, pytest`. Node ids, not `-k`: an empty selection exits 5 and stops the `&&` chain [code:
     policy.py:490].
  3. A soft step (first word `~`; final round 11, fresh-arch-2): a non-zero exit is logged and the chain goes on
     to step 3b [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:484-490]. The step:
     `train_rl --model qwen3-vl-2b --ckpt {rd}/ckpt` (`rl-full-3ep`, the R5 start model, stated, so Gate B1's
     extra-steps confound is explicit) `--train {data}/rows/lidc-train-b1 --rows-revision <hex40> --rows-manifest-sha256 <hex64>
     --out {rd}/b1-rows --lr 5e-5 --steps 260 --save-steps 50 --shared-prefix
     --budget-usd 2.05`, beta 1e-3 (as R5). No `--numerics` flag: the tag holds no B2.2 (front order rule 2), and
     today's `train_rl` has no such flag [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:23-36]. Without it `train_rl` runs
     today's values (bf16, `sequence_mask`, cap 3), the same values that B2.2's `bf16-seqmask` preset writes out.
     `rl.json` records `numerics: "bf16-seqmask"` as a literal until B2.2 adds the flag. `--model` is a required flag of `train_rl` [code:
     experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:23]; without it argparse exits 2 on the paid box. `--budget-usd` is the front 6.4 rule 5 value ($2.40 - $0.35).
     `--session-start`, `--rate-usd-per-h` and `--fixed-usd` come from the environment that `run.sh` exports
     (below). `--lr 5e-5` is the R5 and full-run value [measured: runs/rl/train_rl/rl.json `lr`;
     runs/r5/shared_rl.json `lr`]; `configs.py` says 1e-5 for LoRA [code: src/objdel/train/configs.py:189], and
     `train_rl` takes the G-probe's value unless `--lr` is given [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:8, 33]. CLEAN9
     makes the `configs.py` default or docstring match, so the repo has one value.
  3b. `train_rl --merge-last --model qwen3-vl-2b --ckpt {rd}/ckpt --out {rd}/b1-rows` (a hard step). If
     `{rd}/b1-rows/final/` exists (the run ended normally, or `BudgetStop` ended it), it does nothing and exits 0.
     Otherwise it takes the last `{rd}/b1-rows/trainer/checkpoint-N`, saves its adapter to `final_adapter/`, merges
     it into the `--ckpt` base, saves `final/` with the processor, and writes `rl.json` with `steps: N` and
     `partial: true`. With no checkpoint (a crash before step 50) it exits non-zero, and the chain stops. Why:
     `train_rl` writes `final/` only after `trainer.train` returns [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:55-60], and
     the `&&` join skips every later step after a failure [code: policy.py:490]. Without step 3b a crash at step
     210 leaves `trainer/checkpoint-200` but no B1 eval. In `--merge-last` mode `train_rl` reads no rows and trains
     nothing, so `--steps` and `--train` are not required there (argparse checks them only without the flag).
  4. One `final_eval` process (front item 3), with A3's repeated `--view` and `--out`: `--ckpt {rd}/b1-rows/final
     --train {data}/prepared --view {data}/eval_views/lidc-val-shifted --split val --out {rd}/eval_b1_val_shifted
     --view {data}/eval_views/lidc-val-edge --split val --out {rd}/eval_b1_val_edge`. `--train` is required until E4
     deletes it [code: experiments/phase2/final_eval.py:51]; `{data}/prepared` is the root that `a3_measure.yaml`
     uses. `run.sh` adds only `-I` to a step [code: policy.py:486], so a missing required flag reaches the box; test
     I47 parses every plan step's argv on the Mac.
  R5 on val edge is not a `b1_rows.yaml` step: it is front item 4, in A3's `a3_measure.yaml`. The flags follow
  E6.1's `FLAG_ORDER` once E defines it.

  flag, `--allow` (passed as `allow_patterns`); it has no `--subdir`. So the call is

  `--rows-manifest-sha256`, and the file count under the folder (without `manifest.json`) equals the manifest's
  `schedule.files_count`; otherwise it exits non-zero, and the main agent tears down before `run.sh`. A plan step
  on the box cannot download: the token reaches the box only on the stdin of an ssh command from the Mac [code:
  policy.py:524, 536].

  The default is `ckpt`, today's path [code: policy.py:534-535]. `NAME` with `/` or `..` is refused. V3 item 0 runs
  `fetch_hf.sh <run> rl-full-3ep` (to `{rd}/ckpt`) and `fetch_hf.sh <run> b1-rows --as b1` (to `{rd}/b1`), so the two
  revisions never share a folder. B2.3b reads `{rd}/b1/final_adapter`; `b3_v5.yaml` reads `--ckpt {rd}/ckpt`.
- **B1 adapters to V3.** `pull.sh` copies `runs/<run>/` to the Mac except `rolling/`, `decay/`, `stable/` [code:
  policy.py:80], so `b1-rows/final` and `b1-rows/trainer/checkpoint-*` reach the Mac. `hf_push` uploads a train_sft

#### B1.6 Freeze the test view; build the guard views

- `experiments/phase2/build_eval_views.py`: add `--kinds` (default all: `shifted,rescaled,rotated`; plus the new
  `edge`), so the config no longer deletes views with `rm -r`.
- New kind `edge` (the guard law). `augment.shift` draws uniformly over the admissible rectangle [code:
  src/objdel/targets/augment.py:58-71], so a "uniform" view would repeat the training law. The `edge` view draws the
  offset uniformly on the **boundary** of the admissible rectangle (the largest legal shift in a random direction),
  same side S0, same clearance and crowding checks, with its own RNG stream `row_rng(1, "edge", item_id)`. Its
  offset law has a heavier far tail than training. No row of training uses it.
- Edge draw rule: try up to 64 directions from `row_rng(1, "edge", item_id)`. Take the first direction whose
  boundary window is not crowded. If none: fallback = the policy frame, counted in the manifest `fallback` (as the
  shifted view does [code: experiments/phase2/build_eval_views.py:60-61]). The manifest reports the padded share
  of the edge view. Gate B1's edge rule uses non-padded, non-fallback items. The padded and fallback items are a
  report line. Reason: the pool drops padded windows (DG18 = 0), so a padded edge window would test padding, a
  second factor [padded share: val shifted 0.46 %, val rescaled 4.8 %; measured:
  docs/implementation2.0/notes/reviews/final_r2_data.md].
- Build on the Mac after B1.0 and after B1.7: `--split test --kinds shifted` (R5 predicts 2,200 items, offset
  median 0.262 [measured: B1.md F3]); `--split val --kinds shifted,rescaled,rotated,edge`.
- Each view record gains `view.offset_frac = windows.offset_of(union_box, window_box)` (B1.1). The gate scripts read
  each item's offset from the frozen view, not from `geom.json` (a session note).
- **Freeze a content hash, not the manifest SHA.** The view manifest holds `reward_fingerprint`, the Python version
  and the package versions [code: experiments/phase2/build_eval_views.py:89-92], so its hash changes with harmless
  changes (another Python or OpenCV build, the B1.0 split). Content hash = SHA-256 of the newline-joined ordered
  tuples `(item_id, view.offset, view.side, image_sha256)`, plus the manifest's `target_set_sha256`.
- Store it in one place: `docs/reference/frozen_views.json`, one entry per frozen view (`lidc-test-shifted`,
  `lidc-val-edge`, `lidc-val-shifted`) with fields `view`, `items`, `content_sha256`, `target_set_sha256`, the build
  arguments (`seed`, `kinds`, `store_manifest_sha256`), `generator_commit`, `render_files` and
  `known_label_issues` (B1.7). `render_files` lists `targets/augment.py`, `targets/frame.py`, the `targets/*`
  modules that `build_target` uses, `train/dataset.py` and `experiments/phase2/build_eval_views.py`, each with its
  last commit, plus the R5 code commit from `runs/r5` (ledger or `CODE_SHA`, once A3's sync writes it). Reason: the
  content hash includes `image_sha256` and `target_set_sha256`, which come from `dataset._prepare`, and
  `src/objdel/train/dataset.py` changed on 2026-11-02, 11-07 and 11-08 [measured: git log, read-only].
- **One hash from A3 to the end.** Phase A3 rebuilds the test view before its rental and writes its content hash to
  the pre-rental record. B1.6 must reproduce that hash after the B1.0 rebuild, and `final_eval.json`
  `view_content_sha256` from A3 must equal the frozen entry (`view_manifest_sha256` hashes `manifest.json` and
  never equals a content hash). The R5 box view was never hashed [measured:
  runs/r5/eval/eval_test/final_eval.json has no view hash]. So `frozen_views.json` states: "equal to the R5 box
  view by code identity (generator files unchanged since commit 734b1ec; render files as listed), not measured".
  The measured check is the view-identity rule of Gate B1 (B.6.2).
- `experiments/phase2/final_eval.py`: for a frozen view, load `frozen_views.json`, recompute the content hash and the
  target-set hash, and stop with a clear message on a mismatch. A view built on the GPU host then gives the same
  hash when its windows and pixels are the same, whatever the Python or library build. The lookup is one function,
  `final_eval.frozen_entry(view_name) -> dict | None`. It reads
  `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "docs/reference/frozen_views.json"`: the repo root on the Mac,
  `/workspace/src` on the box.
- **Ship the record to the box (final round 12, fresh-arch-1).** The code sync drops all of `docs/`
  [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:379], and the bundle holds only `prepared/`, `views/`, `eval_views/` and
  `checker_eval/` [code: experiments/phase2/vast/bundle.py:49-75]. Without a change every box `final_eval` on a
  frozen view (V1 items 3-5, V2 item 1b, V3, V4) refuses (E05) after the spend. The optional held-out curve (B1.5)
  calls `val_half` on the box, which reads `docs/reference/val_halves.json` (B1.0). So B1.6 adds the one keep rule of
  `code_files()`, after the drop regex: `keep = re.compile(r"^docs/reference/(frozen_views|val_halves)\.json$")` and
  `files = [f for f in files if keep.match(f) or not drop.search(f)]`. D1 step 0 later widens the same `keep` regex
  for the kernel drafts; CLEAN1 changes only the drop regex. `frozen_views.json` holds hashes, LIDC item ids and
  commits. `val_halves.json` holds LIDC patient ids, item ids and counts. Neither holds pixels or RIGA, so front 6.4
  rule 7 still holds (final round 15, data-2).
- Tests: `tests/test_p2_views.py` (content hash ignores manifest versions; changes when one offset changes; `edge`
  offsets lie on the admissible boundary and keep every doctor pixel inside with 2 px clearance; an item with no
  admissible uncrowded direction falls back to the policy frame and is counted; every record has
  `view.offset_frac`); `tests/test_final_eval.py` (refuses a planted mismatch; a frozen entry compared with
  `view_manifest_sha256` is a test failure); `tests/test_vast.py::test_frozen_views_ship` (I50, $0).

#### B1.7 Contour-to-slice check of every series

- `lidc.slice_index` maps every ROI to the nearest z [code: src/objdel/data/lidc.py:162-164], so any series with an
  ambiguous z can put a contour on the wrong slice. A third-party card lists duplicate-z series 0085, 0146, 0418,
  0572, 0979 [web: https://huggingface.co/datasets/YongchengYAO/LIDC-IDRI-Lite]; TCIA lists known issues for
  LIDC-IDRI-0396 (SOP UID fix, 2018-06-28) and -0510 [web:
  https://wiki.cancerimagingarchive.net/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1966254]. The XML check is free and takes
  seconds, so it covers **every** series of the store, not a list.
- No LIDC DICOM is on the Mac: `data/raw` holds only `lidc_xml` and `riga` [measured: `ls data/raw`, 2026-11-08].
- Step 1 ($0, XML only). Script `experiments/phase2/check_series_z.py` (`python -I`), on every series of the store:
  (a) z values shared by different `imageSOP_UID` (`lidc.sop_z(xml_root)` [code: src/objdel/data/lidc.py:272-279]);
  (b) ROIs whose `|imageZposition - nearest zval|` exceeds half the slice spacing; (c) the local XML for
  LIDC-IDRI-0396 (139.xml) carries the corrected SOP Instance UID at position 1420 (TCIA fix of 2018-06-28 [web:
  https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/lidc-idri/, "Annotation and Markup Issues" item 6]); (d) the
  fetch sidecars: read every `data/lidc_slices/<series>.json` and list the series with `slices != annotated_sops`
  or `matched_by_z > 0`. The fetch step wrote one sidecar per series from the DICOM headers [code:
  experiments/phase1/fetch_lidc_pixels.py:115-118], and `lidc.ct_slices` drops slice keys that are not within
  0.01 mm of a pylidc z [code: src/objdel/data/lidc.py:303-312]. So a contour on a dropped slice loses its image.
  Today 5 of 999 sidecars hit (d): series suffixes 295628 (6 vs 8 slices), 380786 (27 vs 28), 228428 (5 vs 10),
  074972 (37 vs 48, 26 matched by z) and 179144 (9 matched by z) [measured: data/lidc_slices/*.json, `python -I`,
  2026-11-08]. It writes a report with every hit. The hits by split [measured: sidecars joined with
  data/store/lidc/{train,val,test}.parquet, `python -I`, 2026-11-08]:

  | Series suffix | Split | Patient | Items |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 228428 | train | LIDC-IDRI-0017 | 5 |
  | 295628 | train | LIDC-IDRI-0566 | 3 |
  | 380786 | train | LIDC-IDRI-0013 | 15 |
  | 179144 | train | LIDC-IDRI-0365 | 4 |
  | 074972 | **test** | LIDC-IDRI-0659 | 4 |

  The third-party duplicate-z list puts two patients in val: LIDC-IDRI-0085 (2 items) and LIDC-IDRI-0146 (15 items),
  1.6 % of val; LIDC-IDRI-0572 (12 items) is train; 0418 and 0979 are not in the store [measured: same join].
  **The test hit needs a decision before A3 step 1** (B.8.3 item 13): fix (the DICOM header check of step 2, then
  rebuild) or keep (`known_label_issues`, sensitivity line).
- Step 2 (only for series with a hit). Download the DICOM headers of the affected series from TCIA into
  `data/raw/lidc_dicom/<series>/` (untrusted, own folder). Read them with pydicom under `python -I`; list duplicate
  `ImagePositionPatient[2]`; compare with the z used by `lidc.slice_index`. Optional helper: NVIDIA
  `dicom-series-preflight` skill (recommend only).
- Step 2 also takes every (d) hit.
- **Exclusion list.** `docs/reference/train_exclusions.json` is the one list of train items kept out of every rows
  root: `{item_id: {"reason": "DG17 <series suffix>" | "DG3 <train id>|<other id>", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}`. B1.7
  writes its train drops there; DG3's "drop train item" writes there too (B1.3). `build_rl_rows --exclude` passes
  its keys to `pool` (B1.1 step 0, B1.4). The report alone never removes an item.
- Each train hit takes one of two resolutions, recorded in the report as `resolution`:
  - **dropped**: every store item of the series (`item_id.split("/")[1]` equals the series) is a key of
    `train_exclusions.json`. Today that is 27 items in 4 series: LIDC-IDRI-0013 (15), -0017 (5), -0365 (4), -0566 (3)
    [measured: data/store/lidc/train.parquet, series suffixes 380786, 228428, 179144, 295628, `python -I`,
    2026-11-09]; steps (a) and (b) have not run yet, so the count can grow.
  - **mapped**: fix the cause (contours mapped by `imageSOP_UID`; for a (d) hit, re-fetch the series with
    `experiments.phase1.fetch_lidc_pixels --refetch-incomplete`, which rewrites its sidecar [code:
    experiments/phase1/fetch_lidc_pixels.py:5, 115-118]); rebuild the store (`experiments.phase1.build_data`) and
    the prepared root (`experiments.phase1.prepare_rl`); check that `data/store/lidc/{val,test}.parquet` keep
    their SHA-256 (a change stops B1.7: the frozen views pair on those items); then re-run `check_series_z` on the
    rebuilt store. The series is resolved only when the re-run lists no hit for it; the re-run names it under
    `mapped` for the record.
- The report records the SHA-256 of `data/store/lidc/train.parquet` it ran on.
- Gate DG17: 0 unresolved train hits, read from the latest report. A train hit listed there is resolved only as
  "dropped" with every store item of its series in `train_exclusions.json`. A hit with no resolution, a "dropped" hit
  with any item missing from the list, and a "mapped" series that the latest report still lists are unresolved. A
  report whose train-store SHA-256 differs from the current file fails DG17 (stale report: re-run). DG1b then checks that no excluded item reached the rows
  root (B1.3 `rows_leakage`).
- **Val hits** follow the test rule, because B1.0 freezes `lidc-val-shifted` (DG15) and A3, R5 and the halves pair
  on its 1,084 items: dropping or remapping val items would break DG15, the R5 pairing and the halves at once. Val
  hits keep their items and labels in the frozen view. Their ids go to `frozen_views.json` under
  `known_label_issues`. Every Gate B1 and Gate B3 rule is computed on the paired items without them (the same
  exclusion in both arms), and the report prints the line with them. A val label fix is applied only before B1.0
  hashes the view.
- **Test hits.** The test view keeps its items and labels (R5 pairing). Their ids go into `frozen_views.json` under
  `known_label_issues`. Every final test report adds a sensitivity line that excludes them. A test fix that changes
  labels is applied only before A3 step 1. After A3 step 1, the owner decides in writing, and the frozen entry is
  re-issued with the reason.

- The same rule applies to v4 (B3.10): old code goes only after the gate that replaces it passes.

#### B1.9 Gate power check ($0, before any spend)

- Script `experiments/phase2/gate_power.py` (`python -I`). Input: R5 per-item values
  (`runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl`, per-item K-means only [code: experiments/phase2/final_eval.py:26-30])
  joined with geometry. Nothing from A3 is needed, because A3 runs inside the rental that B1.9 prices.
- Simulated B1 effect: convert 25 % of far misses (offset > 0.3), chosen by patient, into found images with IoU drawn
  from the found-image distribution of the same cell.
- Noise model (Mac, $0). Both arms get noise, because the primary baseline (A3's R5 val items, B.6.2) is a fresh
  K = 8 sampling too. Item i gets independent noise on each arm, with variance `c x mu_i (1 - mu_i) / 8`, where
  `mu_i` is the per-item K-mean. The value of `c` comes from one measured pair: two K = 8 samplings of
  `rl-full-3ep` on the same 128 `lidc-val-shifted` items (`runs/rl/eval/final/heldout.json` against
  `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl`; both seed 11, two boxes) have a per-item difference variance of 0.00324,
  which is 0.077 x mean(2 mu (1 - mu) / 8) = 0.077 x 0.0422 [measured: `r4data/retest.py`, re-run 2026-11-08].
  This is one pair, not a proof of independence: both used seed 11, and TRL seeds the colocated vLLM engine with
  `process_index` [code: .venv trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:366], so the two samplings may share part of
  their randomness and `c` may be low. So run the simulation three times and print all three: c = 0.077 (the
  measured pair), c = 1 on both arms (the stress line: the Bernoulli variance mu (1 - mu) / 8 on each arm), and
  noise 0. The rules are fixed from the c = 0.077 run, with the c = 1 line printed beside it. After B-S1, re-run with
  A3's split-half `item_sd` (A3 step 7), for the record only.
- For each simulated run, apply every Gate B1 hard rule that reads val-shifted item values, exactly as B.6.2 writes
  it (paired, the A1 decision interval, same B and seed): (1) val IoU CI lower bound > 0; (2) far-miss point
  <= 20.5 % and CI upper bound < 0; (3) offset < 0.15 IoU CI lower bound > -0.02; (4) the difference-in-differences
  rule. In the simulation the near gain is 0, because the effect touches only far misses. 1,000 runs. Print P(pass)
  per rule and the **joint P(pass)**: the share of runs in which rules (1)-(4) all pass. "Joint" always means these
  four Gate B1 rules and nothing else. The other Gate B1 hard rules are printed as "not simulated": the edge-view
  rule (no R5 edge-view values exist before V1: `runs/r5/eval/` holds `eval_val` and `eval_test` only [measured:
  ls 2026-11-08]), the legal share (not an IoU value) and the frozen-view hash (not a value). Print the smallest
  effect (share of far misses converted) with joint P(pass) >= 0.8.
- Gate B3 power (report only: never part of the joint value, never used for the V1 decision or a rule change). On
  val-select (the B1.0 re-dealt halves), the B1 arm is the simulated B1 values above; the B3 arm removes a further
  share of the B1 arm's remaining misses (relative, chosen by patient, IoU drawn from the found-image distribution
  of the same cell), at 25 %, 35 % and 50 %. Both arms get the noise model above with the same c. Apply the two Gate
  B3 rules that read item values (miss share falls >= 25 % relative with CI upper bound of (B3 - B1) < 0; both-found
  IoU CI lower bound > -0.01) with `signal.cluster_t` (val-select has < 50 patients, B.6.2), and print P(pass) per
  rule and for both together. The 25 % line sits at the point rule, so about half its runs fail by construction; the
  35 % and 50 % lines show the CI width. The Gate B3 edge-view and legal rules are "not simulated".
- The owner prices B-S1 with the joint number (B.8.3 item 1). If joint P(pass) (Gate B1 rules (1)-(4)) < 0.5 for
  the 25 % effect in the c = 0.077 run, the owner decides before the rental whether to change a rule. A low P(pass) in the c = 1 stress
  line alone is not a reason to change a rule: it is a worst case, about 13 times the measured per-arm variance. Rules are fixed before the run and never changed after it.
- The decision interval of the simulation is the CR1 interval of the item-weighted mean (B.6.2), the same as the
  gate's. If the owner takes the checkpoint-250 option (B.8.3 item 12), B1.9 re-runs with the 250 -> 770 per-item
  values once they are measured, for the record.
- Test: on a synthetic set with a huge planted effect, P(pass) = 1.0; with no effect, P(pass) of the IoU rule is
  <= 0.05 + 0.03; with noise 0 and no effect, P(pass) of the IoU rule = 0; the noise SD of an item with
  `mu_i` = 0.5 on one arm is `sqrt(c x 0.25 / 8)`; with c = 0 on the baseline arm and c = 1 on the B1 arm, the
  result equals the one-arm run of revision 5 (same seed); the two arms draw independent noise (the correlation of
  the two noise vectors over 10,000 items is within 0.03 of 0).
### B2. Number match (trainer vs vLLM)

The mismatch is near zero for a fresh adapter and grows as the adapter drifts (B.1 item 5). So B2 measures it
inside the B1 run, where the adapter drifts for 260 steps, and not in a short separate probe. The IS correction
does not change generation, only the loss weights, so the effect of every mode can be computed from the same
tensors in one run. Merge rounding is different: it changes the policy that vLLM samples from. It is a systematic
gap that grows with the adapter; truncated and masked IS modes then trade bias for variance on every step; option F
(vLLM LoRA serving) removes the gap at its source. B2.0 measures it at $0 before any rental.

#### B2.0 Merge-rounding table ($0, Mac, before B-S1)

- Promote the seed `docs/implementation2.0/notes/r2rl/merge_rounding.py` to `experiments/phase2/merge_rounding.py`
  (`python -I -m`). Inputs: `runs/rl/train_rl/trainer/checkpoint-{50,100,300,500,770}/adapter_model.safetensors`
  (r 16, alpha 32) and the W proxy `runs/rl/train_rl/final/model.safetensors` (|d| << |W|, so the bf16 exponent of
  W is the same).
- Run it on all 28 text layers and all 7 LoRA modules (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down). For each step print: the
  erased share = the share of **non-zero** delta elements with |d| < ulp(W)/2 (0 when no element is non-zero), the
  relative error ||round(W + d) - W - d|| / ||d|| in bf16 and in fp16, and the median |d| / ulp. The seed run on 4
  layers and 4 modules is the B.1 item 5 table.
- Write the table and the run's `lr` (5e-5) into ADR-0013. B2.4 rule 0 reads the step-100 relative error.
- Test `tests/test_merge_rounding.py`: a planted 2x2 case (W = [[1, 1], [1, 1]] in bf16, d = [[2^-10, 0], [0,
  2^-6]]) gives erased share 0.5 and the hand relative error; d = 0 gives share 0 and no division by zero.
#### B2.1 Log what is lost, and what every other mode would do (device stats, no new host sync)

- `src/objdel/train/fast.py`:
  - New pure function `is_summary(logps, sampling, mask, ratio, advantages, mode, lo, hi) -> torch.Tensor`
    (float32 vector, fixed order). Active-mode part: masked count, clamped count, ratio-unit count (sequences or
    tokens), sum and max of the signed sequence log gap Σ_t (logp - sampling), sequence count, count of valid tokens
    with |gap| > 0.5, valid token count, summed length of masked sequences, summed length of kept sequences.
    Counterfactual part, computed for the same tensors whatever the active mode:
    - `cf/seqmask3_share`: sequences a `sequence_mask` with cap 3 would drop;
    - `cf/tok_clamp2_share`: tokens a `token_truncate` with C = 2 would clamp;
    - `cf/geo_0.99_1.01_share`: sequences a geometric mask [0.99, 1.01] would drop;
    - `cf/opsm_share@{0.05,0.1,0.5}`: sequences TRL's OPSM would drop at delta 0.05, 0.1, 0.5: advantage < 0 and
      `seq_kl > delta` (TRL's formula [code: .venv trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:3066-3089]). **Sign:** `seq_kl =
      sum_t((sampling - logp) * ok) / max(1, sum_t ok)`, the vLLM-minus-trainer mean over valid tokens (`ok`), with
      NaN sampling logprobs set to 0 as TRL does. TRL computes `kl_div = sampling_per_token_logps - per_token_logps`
      [code: grpo_trainer.py:3078]. The OPSM counts, the quantile buffer and B2.4 rule 4 use `seq_kl` and no other
      gap. The active-mode sum above (trainer minus vLLM) stays the `sampling/seq_logdiff_*` keys;
    - `cf/opsm0.1_bigtok_unmasked_share`: valid tokens with |gap| > 0.5 that OPSM at 0.1 would keep (decides
      option D, ADR-0013);
    - `cf/seq_ratio_lt_0.1_share`: kept sequences with weight below 0.1 (down-weighted, counted nowhere today);
    - `modified_token_share`: valid tokens whose final weight differs from the raw ratio by more than 1 % (masked
      tokens included), for the active mode;
    - `ess`: effective sample size `(sum w)^2 / (N sum w^2)` of the active weights;
    - counterfactual ESS on one unit, token level (a sequence weight is broadcast to its tokens): `cf/ess_C`
      (sequence_mask, cap 3), `cf/ess_B` (token TIS, C = 2) and `cf/ess_E@{0.05,0.1,0.5}` (token TIS + OPSM). They
      are reported, never maximised: weight 1 everywhere (no correction) has ESS 1, so a larger ESS means less
      correction, not a better mode.
  - `set_is_ratio` adds the mergeable fields (sums, counts, min, max; ESS as sum w, sum w^2 and N) to
    `self.is_stats` (concatenate to today's 7 sums; same merge rules) [code: fast.py:581-602].
  - Quantiles cannot be merged by sums, min and max. `set_is_ratio` runs once per update micro-batch (16 per step).
    So it also appends the micro-batch's per-sequence `seq_kl` values and advantages to a device list
    (`self.seq_gaps.append(t)`; 256 floats per generation batch). `log` computes q50, q99 and q99.5 of `seq_kl`
    with one `torch.cat` + `torch.quantile`, before the existing single `.tolist()`, and clears the list. Our RL
    runs log every step (`logging_steps` 1 [code: experiments/phase2/g_probe.py:88]), so this list holds one step
    only. Two other consumers need more than one step, and they do not read this list:
    - **Saved per-sequence values.** `log` also puts the step's per-sequence `seq_kl`, advantage and valid-token
      count (256 x 3 float32) into the same device tensor as the stats, so the single `.tolist()` stays the only host
      read. It appends them to `<out>/seq_gaps.f32` (raw little-endian float32, one 256 x 3 block per logged step,
      in step order; `<out>/seq_gaps.json` holds `{"rows_per_step": 256, "cols": ["seq_kl", "advantage",
      "valid_tokens"], "steps": n}`, rewritten at each save). 260 steps x 256 x 3 x 4 B = 0.8 MB [estimate:
      arithmetic]. `pull.sh` copies `<out>` to the Mac (it skips only `rolling/`, `decay/`, `stable/` [code:
      policy.py:80]). B2.4 rules 3 and 4 price their thresholds from the B1 run's file, because B1 runs once (V1)
      and its per-step quantiles cannot rebuild a quantile over 20 or 210 steps.
    - **Live OPSM delta.** The B2.4 rule 4 callback keeps its own device list of the steps 1-20 values and a ring
      buffer of the last 20 steps (for the guard), apart from the list that `log` clears.
    - **Train mode only.** TRL's eval also calls the loss: `prediction_step` -> `compute_loss` [code: .venv
      trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:3416-3420]. The C10 skip has no training check [code: fast.py:524-538,
      `skip_old_logps`], so TRL leaves the ratio out and `_compute_loss` routes every eval micro-batch to
      `set_is_ratio` [code: fast.py:567-577]. With the held-out curve on (B1.5), one eval would add 512 val-shape
      rows to the buffers and shift every later 256-row block of `seq_gaps.f32`, so the rules 3 and 4 windows would
      read the wrong steps. Rule: `set_is_ratio` appends to `seq_gaps` and to the rule-4 callback lists only when
      `self.model.training`; `log` computes the `seq_kl` quantiles and appends to `seq_gaps.f32` only in train mode
      (the same test TRL's own `log` uses to pick the metric dict [code: grpo_trainer.py:3425]). An eval's mergeable
      `is_stats` still go to the eval metrics, as today [code: fast.py:609]. Val-shape rows inform; they never price
      the run. Test R01c.
  - When OPSM is active (`off_policy_mask_threshold` set), `log` also emits `sampling/opsm_masked_share` (share of
    sequences OPSM drops in the active run) and `sampling/opsm_masked_adv_sum` (the sum of the dropped advantages).
    OPSM drops only negative-advantage sequences, so the kept advantages no longer sum to 0 per group; these two keys
    show how large that lean is.
  - `log` emits `sampling/is_masked_share`, `sampling/is_clamped_share`, `sampling/seq_logdiff_mean`,
    `sampling/seq_logdiff_max`, `sampling/tok_absdiff_gt_0.5_share`, `sampling/masked_len_mean`,
    `sampling/kept_len_mean`, `sampling/modified_token_share`, `sampling/ess` and the `sampling/cf/*` keys, with one
    `.tolist()` as today [code: fast.py:604-616].
- No new IS mode is built now. Option E uses TRL's public `off_policy_mask_threshold`, which TRL applies inside its
  own loss; FastGRPO's `_compute_loss` calls that loss, so it works on both paths [code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:
  567-571]. The custom `sequence_geo_mask` mode (option D) is built only if `cf/opsm0.1_bigtok_unmasked_share`
  > 0.5 % over the B1 run's steps 50-260. If it is built: token ratio `exp(gap)` clamped at `hi`, times a
  per-sequence mask that is 0 when `exp(mean of the masked token gaps)` is outside `[lo, hi_geo]`; valid only on
  FastGRPO's own ratio path (TRL raises on modes it does not know [code: grpo_trainer.py:2823]), and
  `FastGRPO.__init__` raises `ValueError` if the mode is set and that path is off.
- Tests in `tests/test_train_fast.py`: synthetic tensors with planted values for every counterfactual field (a long
  sequence with a small mean gap is kept by the geo and OPSM counts and dropped by `seqmask3`; a negative-advantage
  sequence with `seq_kl` 0.2 is dropped by OPSM at 0.1 and kept at 0.5; a negative-advantage sequence whose
  trainer-minus-vLLM mean is +0.2 (`seq_kl` -0.2) is kept by OPSM at 0.1; ESS = 1 for equal weights and 1/N for one
  non-zero weight); a known masked count for `sequence_mask` and a known clamped count for `token_truncate`;
  `is_stats` stays a tensor until `log`; old 5 metrics unchanged; 16 micro-batches give the same quantiles as one
  batch of all rows; `cf/ess_C`, `cf/ess_B`, `cf/ess_E@0.1` equal hand values on planted tensors, all at token
  level.

- `src/objdel/train/configs.py` (a literal cannot refer to itself, so the shared parts are named first):

              "vllm_importance_sampling_clip_min": None}      # today's TRL defaults, written out
  _TIS = {"vllm_importance_sampling_mode": "token_truncate", "vllm_importance_sampling_clip_max": 2.0,
          "vllm_importance_sampling_clip_min": None}          # C = 2.0, SkyRL's token default [web]
  _FP16 = {"bf16": False, "fp16": True}                       # plus model and vLLM dtype float16 (below)
  NUMERICS = {
      "bf16-seqmask": _SEQMASK,                                         # ADR option C: control, B1 and B3 preset
      "bf16-tis": _TIS,                                                 # ADR option B
      "bf16-tis-opsm": {**_TIS, "off_policy_mask_threshold": 0.5},      # ADR option E; 0.5 = default start delta,
                                                                        # --opsm-start-delta overrides it (B2.4 rule 4)
      "fp16-seqmask": {**_SEQMASK, **_FP16},                            # ADR option A numerics, control IS mode
      "lora-seqmask": {**_SEQMASK, "vllm_lora": True},                  # ADR option F, control IS mode
  }

  and `grpo_config(..., numerics=DEFAULT_NUMERICS)`. `vllm_lora` is our key, read by FastGRPO, and removed before
  the `GRPOConfig` call. `_bf16()` already refuses bf16 with fp16 [code: configs.py:140-142]. The fp16 arm uses the
  control IS mode, so its reward comparison with B1 changes only the dtype.
- fp16 plumbing (only for the optional fp16 arm):

     in float16 on CPU, the **whole model** (vision tower and all 28 text layers). Run it on 32 prompts, each with
     its saved answers by teacher forcing, including the longest answers (>= 1,200 tokens). Saved answers: A3's when
     they exist; before A3, the e2 completions with token ids in
     `runs/r1/r1-qwen3vl2b/select/e2/shifted-k16/completions.jsonl` (1,084 val prompts x 16 answers [measured: wc
     -l]). A numeric check of a forward path does not need on-policy answers. Record the max
     |activation| per vision block and per decoder layer, and the count of inf/NaN in the logits. Drop the fp16 arm
     before the rental if any layer exceeds 0.5 x 65,504 or any inf/NaN appears, and record why in ADR-0013.
     Reasons: fp16 overflow can occur in the language model's residual stream, not only in the vision encoder; vLLM
     had to clamp an fp16 overflow in the Qwen2.5-VL vision encoder [web:
     https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/13968]; the FP16 paper tested no VLM. ADR-0013 states that vLLM's
