     `lora_request=None` on base W (no adapter, so no merge error) and keeps (f_base). (iii) The trainer scores the
     three answer sets with way (b) of B2.3b: (i) and (ii) with `"b1"` active, (0) under
     `with model.disable_adapter():`. f0 = mean |f_base - b_base| is the bf16 engine-vs-trainer floor at d = 0.
     Why a floor: the gap does not reach 0 when merge rounding is gone. At step 1 the adapter delta is exactly 0,
     and the logp difference is still 0.00956 (R5 base arm), 0.00952 (R5 shared arm) and 0.00956 (full run); the
     full run's median at a 260-step drift is 0.0176 (steps 240-280), 0.0236 (101-300), 0.0185 (301-500)
     [measured: `sampling/sampling_logp_difference/mean` in runs/r5/base/rl.json, runs/r5/shared_rl.json,
     runs/rl/train_rl/rl.json, 2026-11-08]. A bar on raw gaps would score a perfect F at 0.0096 / 0.0176 = 0.54,
     so the gate result would follow the drift range, not F. Pass: (mean |f_lora - b| - f0) <= 0.5 x
     (mean |f_merged - b| - f0). If mean |f_merged - b| - f0 < 0.002 [estimate threshold], the comparator cannot
     tell F from no F: `f_check.json` records `informative: false`, the output-level check passes, and the tensor,
     NaN, load-count, base-hash and timing checks decide. This is the number F exists to fix. Cost: three
     generations and three scoring passes plus the fixed-length timing of step 4b.4 (14 generations of about
     7.8 s each [estimate: 5.61 s + 4.3 ms x 512 tokens, the R5 fit in docs/implementation2.0/notes/B_gpu_audit.md:40]), about 5 min inside
     the run [estimate]. The comparator does not depend on B2.3b's box part. Phase C's G-EQ5 under F uses the same
     check.
  4b. **Comparator plumbing (the one rule; C5 points here).** It runs before step 1, so step 1 must see the same
     engine state as a run without `--f-check`.
     1. Base. The comparator runs on the run's own `--ckpt`. The first run after Gate B3 starts from `rl-full-3ep`
        (`--ckpt {rd}/ckpt`, as B1 and B3). If its `--ckpt` is another model, the output-level check is skipped and
        `f_check.json` records the reason. Its launch lines fetch the B1 adapter with `fetch_hf.sh <run> b1-rows
        --as b1` (B1.5).
     2. Adapter. The training process holds the run's own fresh adapter `"default"`. B1 loads beside it:
        `model.load_adapter("{rd}/b1/final_adapter", adapter_name="b1")`, then `model.set_adapter("b1")`.
        `lora_merged_params` merges the active adapters [code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:703-707], so arm (i) merges
        B1. `sync_lora` gains `adapter_name="default"` and `slot=1`; the comparator passes `adapter_name="b1"` and
        `slot=2`, so its folder comes from `get_peft_model_state_dict(model, adapter_name="b1")` and
        `peft_config["b1"]` (the default `adapter_name` reads `"default"` [code: .venv
        peft/utils/save_and_load.py:148-151]), and it loads as `LoRARequest("b1", 2, <b1 dir>)`.
     3. Engine state. Before each comparator generation: wake the weights if asleep, only through `sync_lora` /
        `push_weights` (they clear the flag, C5 "Sleep state"); never a raw `wake_up(tags=["weights"])`. Then
        `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])`. In mode B, TRL sleeps the engine at start-up and wakes the KV cache only
        inside its own generate [code: .venv trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:376-377, 718-719]. Prompts. The
        comparator runs before step 1, and the `patch_vllm_prompts` wrapper goes in only at the first `_generate`
        [code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:618-622]. So at that time `llm.generate` is vLLM's own. TRL's prompts are
        processor-expanded ids [code: .venv trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:720-743]; sent raw, vLLM expands the
        image a second time (N pads become 2N-1). The wrapper is today the only code that cuts each pad run to one
        pad (`one_pad_per_image` [code: fast.py:407-415]) and checks that vLLM's expansion gives the trainer's ids
        [code: fast.py:680-688]. So move the body of the wrapper's inner `one_pad` into one shared helper,
        `fast.vllm_generate_checked(generate, prompts, pad, **kw)`: it calls `generate(one_pad_per_image(prompts,
        pad), **kw)`, then raises the same "vLLM expanded the image to n pads" error on any mismatch. The wrapper
        and the comparator both call it, with vLLM's own `generate`. Only `lora_request` differs: the wrapper
        passes `"policy"` under F; the comparator passes `LoRARequest("b1", 2, <b1 dir>)` in arm (ii) and
        `lora_request=None` in arms (0) and (i) and the base timing arm. An expansion error in the comparator
        writes `f_check.json` with `prompt_expansion: false` and fails the F check.
     4. Order. Arm (ii) runs first, on the start-up base W. The floor arm (0) runs next, on the same base W. The
        B2.4 rule 0 timing runs after them, on slot 2 and on `lora_request=None`, with the KV cache awake. Arm (i)
        runs last: its merged push writes `W + d_B1` into vLLM's base tensors [code: fast.py:716-717], so every
        arm that needs base W runs before it. Timing at a fixed length: the LoRA kernel cost depends on rank and
        shapes, not on the adapter values, but the answers do. The two arms sample from W + d_B1 and from W, so
        their longest answers differ, and generate time grows 4.3 ms per token of the longest answer (5.61 s +
        4.3 ms x longest answer, r = 0.92 [measured: docs/implementation2.0/notes/B_gpu_audit.md:40]). A 736-token gap (1,536 against 800)
        moves the ratio by about 0.29 on an 11 s generate, twice the 0.15 margin. So both timed arms use
        `SamplingParams(max_tokens=512, min_tokens=512, ignore_eos=True, seed=s)` and the run's other sampling
        fields; every row then decodes exactly 512 tokens in both arms (the check asserts
        `len(out.outputs[0].token_ids) == 512` for every row, else the timing check fails). One untimed warm-up
        generate per arm comes first (it fills the image and prefix caches of both arms alike). Then, for each
        seed s = 0, 1, 2, the order is A B A B (A = slot 2, B = `lora_request=None`); the timing value is the
        median of the 6 ratios t_A / t_B (`lora_over_base` in `f_check.json`). Arms (0), (i) and (ii) keep the
        run's normal `SamplingParams`. Limit: a full-batch 512-token decode measures the kernel cost at batch 256;
        the decode tail at 1-2 rows is seen only in the run's s/step report line.
     5. Restore, in both modes, in this order, while the engine is still awake: `push_weights(vg, model,
        values="base")`; then hash every vLLM base tensor on the host against `p.data`, one tensor at a time (the
        C5 step 5(b) method); then `remove_lora(2)`, `model.set_adapter("default")`, `model.delete_adapter("b1")`,
        `reset_prefix_cache()`; then, in mode B only, `sleep(level=2)` last and set `vg._llm_weights_sleeping = True`
        (as TRL does [code: vllm_generation.py:771-773]; C5 "Sleep state"), so step 1's sync wakes the weights before
        it pushes `p.data`. A mismatch fails the F check before
        step 1. Why the hash comes before the sleep: level 2 discards the weights ("Sleep level 2 discards the
        weights" [code: .venv trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:378]), so a host read after it reads freed memory.
        In mode B the sleep discards the restored base anyway; step 1's own `sync_lora` pushes `p.data` again after
        the wake (F sync step 2.2), and the C5 step 5(c) mode-B base hash checks that push.
  5. **Where the check runs: inside `train_rl`.** `train_rl --f-check` (on by default under `lora-seqmask` and
     `fp16-seqmask`; setting it under another preset is an argparse error) runs every check of the first run that
     uses the preset in the training process, on that run's own vLLM engine. Why not a separate pytest: a second
     engine cannot start beside the run (vLLM takes `vllm_gpu_memory_utilization` 0.35 of the 32 GB [code:
     src/objdel/train/configs.py:192] beside a trainer peak of about 17 GB, C5), and a pytest before the run would
     check another engine and cost one more start-up. Under `lora-seqmask`: the comparator before step 1 (step 4,
     floor-subtracted); the restore base hash (step 4b.5); the packed-layout equality after sync 1 and again after
     the first sleep/wake cycle (step 4); the LoRA load count per RL step is 1 (`add_lora` calls, steps 1-15); the
     fixed-length ABAB timing inside the comparator (step 4b.4, B2.4 rule 0); NaN/inf = 0 over steps 1-15. Under
     `fp16-seqmask`: the engine dtype assertion (fp16 step 3) and NaN/inf = 0 over steps 1-15. After step 15, or at
     the first failure, it writes `<out>/f_check.json`: `preset` (the preset the run started under), each check's
     value and pass flag, and `passed`, the AND of every pass flag of that preset. Fields under `lora-seqmask`:
     `nan`, `comparator` (`f_merged`, `f_lora`, `f0`, `ratio` = (f_lora - f0) / (f_merged - f0), `informative`,
     `ok`), `base_hash_ok`, `lora_equal`, `load_count`, `lora_over_base` (median of the 6 fixed-length ratios),
     `passed`; under `fp16-seqmask`: `nan`, `engine_dtype_ok`, `passed`. `restart_preset` (B2.4 rule 0) reads only
     `preset` and `passed`. On a failure it raises after writing the file, so the plan step fails and the run
     restarts under the B2.4 rule 0 fallback. G05's box part is a record check of that file (B.9.5); the Mac
     twin with fakes is U76.
- `train_rl --numerics {bf16-seqmask,bf16-tis,bf16-tis-opsm,fp16-seqmask,lora-seqmask}`; `rl.json` records it.
- `train_rl --opsm-start-delta X` (float > 0; valid only with `--numerics bf16-tis-opsm`, an argparse error under
  any other preset) sets `off_policy_mask_threshold` = X after the preset is applied, so X is the delta of steps
  1-20 (TRL copies the threshold once at init [code: .venv trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:882] and reads the attribute
  at each loss call [code: .venv trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:3190-3203]). Absent, the preset's 0.5 stays. This is the
  only path for the start delta: a `--grpo` JSON (today's override flag [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:36])
  holding `off_policy_mask_threshold` is an argparse error. The run plan writes the ADR-0013 `start_delta` (B2.4
  rule 4) as this flag's value; `rl.json` records `opsm_start_delta` (0.5 when the flag is absent).
- Note: colocate vLLM already returns processed logprobs (`logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` [code: .venv
  trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:370]), and sampling is T = 1, top_k 0 [code: configs.py sampling()]. So the
  gap is numeric, not a sampling-mode gap.
- Tests: `tests/test_train_configs.py` (each preset builds a GRPOConfig; fp16 never with bf16; `bf16-tis-opsm` sets
  the public OPSM key; `vllm_lora` never reaches `GRPOConfig`); a CPU test that the `vllm_kwargs` patch passes
  `dtype` or the LoRA kwargs and restores the name; the dtype assertion test above; a fake-engine test (U70) of the
  F sync order: `add_lora` once per sync with `load_inplace=True`, every `generate` with `load_inplace=False`, the
  unmerged base push in mode B only, `reset_prefix_cache` once per sync.

#### B2.3 Optional fp16 arm (paid, B-S2, owner decision B.8.3 item 8)

- Only if the Mac check passed and the owner funds it. Config `experiments/phase2/configs/b2_fp16.yaml`: start
  `rl-full-3ep`, the B1 rows root, seed 0, `--numerics fp16-seqmask --lr 5e-5 --steps 60 --save-steps 60
  --shared-prefix`. No eval. 60 steps, because the mismatch appears only after about 20 steps (B.1 item 5).
  Step 0 of `b2_fp16.yaml` is the CUDA build of `b1_rows.yaml` step 0 (B1.5). Why: V3 item 1 is skippable, so no
  earlier V3 item is sure to build, and `sync_up` leaves the CPU build [code: policy.py:398-399; CMakeLists.txt:15];
  without step 0 the arm would score every reward on the CPU checker (final round 8, qa-5). Step 1 is G08b's fp16
  part: `[-m, pytest, -q, -p, no:cacheprovider, -m, gpu, tests/test_train_fast.py::test_g08b_fp16_dtype]`. Its model
  is `os.environ["OBJDEL_RUN_DIR"] + "/ckpt"`, the folder that `fetch_hf.sh <run> rl-full-3ep` fills (front 6.3 V3
  item 0); a missing folder fails, never skips. The arm
  trains on reward v4 (the B1 control), so it needs no `sum_x`/`sum_y` check. The IS
  mode is the control's, so the (fp16 - B1) reward bound changes only the dtype.
- Script `experiments/phase2/b2_summary.py`: reads the fp16 arm's `rl.json` and the B1 run's `rl.json`. It prints,
  over steps 41-60 of each: the means of the B2.1 metrics, `importance_sampling_ratio/mean`,
  `sampling_logp_difference/mean`, `rewards/iou_tc/mean`, NaN/inf count (`logging_nan_inf_filter` is off [code:
  configs.py NO_SYNC], so NaN shows in the log) and s/step. Decision number for the reward: the paired bootstrap
  over the 640 prompts of steps 41-60 (same prompts, same order in both runs), resampling prompts, 95 % lower bound
  of the mean (fp16 - B1) `rewards/iou_tc` difference. The one-sided t bound over the 20 per-step differences is a
  second line only (per-step differences of two trajectories are autocorrelated).

#### B2.3b Attribution of the gap (Mac part $0 before B-S1; box part in V3 (B-S2) only if B2.4 needs it)

- Script `experiments/phase2/b2_attribution.py` (no training). Adapters: `checkpoint-100` and `checkpoint-770` of
  the full run (both drifted; they exist today [measured: ls runs/rl/train_rl/trainer]). Sequences: 32 prompts x 8
  saved answers (A3's when they exist, else the e2 completions named in B2.2 step 0).
- **Mac part ($0, CPU).** Score the same 256 prompt+answer sequences four ways under `torch.no_grad()`:
  - (a) the FastGRPO default (packed shared-prefix forward, vision cache, RopeCache);
  - (b) the plain TRL forward (FastGRPO patches off);
  - (c) the trainer forward with the LoRA delta merged into the bf16 base weights (`lora_merged_params` values
    [code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:696-708]), which is what vLLM receives;
  - (d) the plain trainer forward in fp32 (no autocast, base cast to fp32): the reference.
- **Box part (rental V3 item 2a, front 6.3; about 15 min [estimate: one vLLM batch and two scoring passes plus
  process start-up]; only if the B2.0 step-100 relative error is < 0.2, so rule 0 does not fire).** It is
  attribution for ADR-0013; the F check does not need it (B2.2 F step 4). The B1 final adapter reaches the box by
  `fetch_hf.sh <run> b1-rows --as b1` (B1.5). Load `{rd}/b1/final_adapter/` on `rl-full-3ep` (`{rd}/ckpt`), so way (c) has a real LoRA delta to
  merge. Generate one batch (32 prompts x 8) with vLLM in bf16 from that adapter (the only B1 adapter this part
  reads) and keep:
  - (f) the generation-time `sampling_per_token_logps` of those 256 answers: this is the quantity that enters the
    IS ratio, so it is the "vLLM-bf16" line of every reading;
  - (e)-bf16, vLLM teacher-forced scoring of the same sequences (`SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=0)`):
    a separate "prefill vs decode" line, because prefill and decode use different attention kernels and batch
    shapes;
  - (e)-fp32, only in a fresh process after the trainer is freed, with `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` named. The fp32
    attention backend is untested for Qwen3-VL. If it fails, record the failure and do not retry.
  - (a)-(d) again on the same 256 answers, so the box and Mac lines share one batch.
- Print, for each pair against (d) and for (f) against HF-bf16 (b): the signed mean gap, the mean |gap| and the gap
  by token position (bins of 64). Readings:
  - (b) << (a): the packed forward causes the gap (fix in FastGRPO, not by dtype).
  - (f) vs (b) much larger than each one's gap to fp32: the engine kernels cause it.
  - (e)-bf16 far from (f): prefill and decode differ; (e) is then not a proxy for the IS ratio.
  - both close to fp32 only in fp16 or fp32: the dtype causes it.
  - (c) >> (b) on a drifted adapter: merge rounding causes it (B2.0 predicts this), and option F applies.
- Record the table in ADR-0013.

#### B2.4 Decide (rules 2-4 after V1, $0; rule 1 after the optional fp16 arm; rule 0 inside the first run under F)

- **Scope (ADR-0013 rule (b)).** The B3 run keeps B1's preset `bf16-seqmask`. So the B3 A/B changes the reward and
  the truncation mask only, and B3.10 can credit them. B2.4 picks the preset for the runs after Gate B3. Why not
  for B3: the step-100 relative error is 0.531 [measured: B.1 item 5], so rule 0 would almost surely pick
  `lora-seqmask`, and B3 would then change four things at once (reward, truncation mask, serving path, beta). F
  alone can move the miss share, so Gate B3 could not tell them apart.
- No code edit inside a rental. A run picks its preset with `train_rl --numerics <name>`. The preset deletion and
  the `grpo_config` default change land in the first commit after the session that used the decision.
- Decision rule (ADR-0013). Rule 0 uses the B2.0 table; rules 2-3 use the B1 run's counterfactual stats over
  steps 50-260 (the adapter has drifted there):
  0. Two stages, because the F check can only run inside a `lora-seqmask` run (today `train_rl` has no
     `--numerics` or `--f-check` flag [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:23-36]; B2.2 F step 5 adds them).
     **Start choice (before the run, `start_preset`):** if B2.0 shows a bf16 relative error >= 0.2 at step 100 (the
     seed run gives 0.531), the first run after Gate B3 starts under `lora-seqmask` (`--f-check` is on by default
     there). This stage reads only the B2.0 error; no F result exists yet and none is needed. If the error is < 0.2,
     rules 1-3 give the start preset. **Restart choice (inside the run, `restart_preset`):** the F check result in
     `<out>/f_check.json` keeps `lora-seqmask` (passed) or picks the restart preset (failed). The F check is the
     first 15 steps of that run itself, in one process on one host, run by `train_rl --f-check` in the training process (B2.2 F step 5; no separate pytest): NaN/inf = 0; the LoRA tensors equal the trainer's under vLLM's layout (B2.2 F step 4); the
     LoRA load count per RL step is 1; the restore base hash (B2.2 F step 4b.5); the output-level check against the
     comparator that the run measures before step 1, minus the measured d = 0 floor f0 (B2.2 F step 4); and the
     timing rule. Timing rule: inside the comparator before step 1 (B2.2 F step 4b.4 holds the plumbing), generate
     the same 32 x 8 batch with the comparator's `lora_request` and with `lora_request=None` (the base, same
     engine) at a fixed length (`max_tokens=512, min_tokens=512, ignore_eos=True`), so answer length cannot move
     the ratio; order A B A B for each seed s = 0, 1, 2; pass if the median of the 6 LoRA / base
     generate-time ratios is <= 1.15 [estimate threshold]. A cross-run s/step ratio is a report line only: the host
     moves the CPU phase (3.0-3.2 s of the R5 step, BRIEF section 2), and two runs sample different answers, so the
     decode tail differs too. If the F check fails, `train_rl` raises after writing `f_check.json`, and the run
     restarts under `fp16-seqmask` (if rule 1 passed) or else the rules 2-3 preset (`bf16-tis-opsm`, or
     `bf16-seqmask` by the rule 3 veto); the restart costs one process start-up (about 6 min) plus the 15 steps.
     A failed check in a run that started under `fp16-seqmask` (error < 0.2, rule 1) restarts under the rules 2-3
     preset. **`restart_preset(cf, f_check, fp16, b1)`** encodes this: it reads `f_check["preset"]` (the start
     preset) and `f_check["passed"]` (the AND of every check, B2.2 F step 5) and never recomputes the pass from
     some of the fields. `passed` -> keep the start preset. Failed, start `lora-seqmask`, and fp16 passed rule 1 ->
     `fp16-seqmask`. Failed otherwise (start `fp16-seqmask`, or no fp16 arm, or fp16 above half) -> the rules 2-3
     preset. So a restart never returns the preset that just failed: a comparator-only failure (NaN 0, equal
     tensors, ratio <= 1.15) still restarts away from `lora-seqmask`. Both the start preset and the restart preset are computed before the run from inputs that exist then (B2.0
     table, B1 counterfactual stats, the fp16 arm if it ran); `f_check.json` only says which one applies.
  1. `fp16-seqmask` passes if it passed Gate B2's fp16 rules AND its mean `sampling_logp_difference/mean` over steps
     41-60 is at most half of the B1 run's over the same steps [estimate threshold: the paper reports a much larger
     cut, so half is a low bar]. No speed bar: the fp16 arm (V3 item 2b) and the B1 run (V1) are two rentals, and
     rule 0's reason applies (the host moves the CPU phase; different answers move the decode tail). An in-process
     speed bar is not possible either, because one vLLM engine holds one dtype (fp16 step 5). The s/step of both runs
     is a report line (`b2_summary.py` prints it, B2.3).
  2. Default IS mode when rule 0 does not apply: `bf16-tis-opsm` (token TIS C = 2 + OPSM). The ESS values are
     reported, not maximised (B2.1).
  3. Vetoes on `bf16-tis-opsm`, over B1 steps 50-260: if `cf/opsm_share@0.5` > 2 % of sequences, raise the starting
     delta to the q99.9 of `seq_kl` over the per-sequence values of B1 steps 50-260 (read from the B1 run's
     `seq_gaps.f32`, B2.1; this number is `start_delta`, rule 4); if `cf/tok_clamp2_share` > 1 % of tokens, record it and keep the preset; fall
     back to `bf16-seqmask` only if the median `cf/ess_E@0.1` < 0.5 [estimate thresholds].
  4. OPSM delta: delta = q99.5 of `seq_kl` (B2.1) over the per-sequence values of the first 20 steps (20 x 256) of
     the run that uses OPSM, under its own preset, then frozen. The values come from the callback's own steps 1-20
     device list (B2.1), not from the list that `log` clears each step. Until step 20, delta = `start_delta`: 0.5 (the example value of TRL's
     `off_policy_mask_threshold` docstring [code: .venv trl/trainer/grpo_config.py:348-352]) when rule 3's first veto
     did not fire, else the rule-3 q99.9 value. `start_preset` and `restart_preset` return `start_delta` as a number
     (the q99.9 computed from the B1 `seq_gaps.f32`, or 0.5), never the string "q99.9", and `None` for any other
     preset; ADR-0013 records it and the run plan passes it as `train_rl --opsm-start-delta` (B2.2). Reason the
     frozen step-20 delta is not taken from B1: a delta taken
     from the B1 run is measured under bf16 merge rounding; under F or fp16 the gap shrinks, so it would be too
     loose. Patch point: a `TrainerCallback.on_step_end` at step 20 sets `trainer.off_policy_mask_threshold = delta`
     (TRL reads that attribute at each loss call [code: .venv trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:882, 3190]) and writes
     `delta` to `<out>/opsm_delta.json` beside the step-20 checkpoint. A resume reads that file (`rl.json` is written
     only at the end of a run). The attribute name joins the A7 start-up check. Guard: if
     `sampling/opsm_masked_share` exceeds 2 % in 20 consecutive steps, recompute delta once as the q99.5 of the last
     20 steps (the callback's ring buffer, 20 x 256 values), log the change, and never change it again. Why: a fresh adapter has the smallest gap in steps 1-20
     (median logp diff 0.011 against 0.028 in steps 21-100 [measured: B.1 item 5]), so a delta frozen there can mask
     a growing share later. Priced at $0 on the B1 run: take the q99.5 of the B1 run's steps 1-20 per-sequence `seq_kl` from
     its `seq_gaps.f32`, apply it to steps 50-260 of the same file as a counterfactual (advantage < 0 and `seq_kl` >
     delta), and report the share it would mask.
  5. Build option D only under the B2.1 trigger.
  Missing inputs: when the fp16 arm did not run, rule 1 is skipped (in the start choice and in the restart choice).
  The F check is never a missing input: the start choice reads only the B2.0 error, and the F result is read only
  by the restart choice, after the run writes `f_check.json`. With error < 0.2 and no fp16 arm, the start preset is
  `bf16-tis-opsm` (or `bf16-seqmask` by the rule 3 veto).
- The B1 run used `bf16-seqmask`, so Gate B1 has no numerics confound; under rule (b) Gate B3 has none either.
- Write ADR-0013 with the B2.0 table, the counterfactual table, the veto values, the B2.3b attribution, the start
  preset and the restart preset for the runs after Gate B3 (both written before the run; the run's `rl.json`
  `numerics` and `f_check.json` record which one ran).
- **Eval of a run trained under `lora-seqmask` (the one rule; ADR-0013, 99_back RL settings 16 point here).** Such a
  run is evaluated unmerged, with vLLM LoRA serving, as it was sampled in training. Why: `train_rl` merges before it
  saves `final/` (`merge_and_unload()` then `save_pretrained` [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:58-59]), and the
  merge is the bf16 `round(W + d)` of B2.0 (relative error 0.531 at step 100 [measured: B2.0 seed run]). Today
  `final_eval` takes only `--ckpt` [code: experiments/phase2/final_eval.py:48], and no code starts vLLM with
  `enable_lora` [measured: grep src experiments, 0 hits, 2026-11-09]. So B adds `final_eval --adapter DIR`: the
  command is `final_eval --ckpt <the run's --ckpt base> --adapter <out>/final_adapter ...`. With `--adapter`,
  `final_eval` builds the engine with `fast.vllm_kwargs(enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16)` (B2.2 F step 1) and
  passes `LoRARequest("eval", 1, <dir>)` to every generate, through `fast.vllm_generate_checked` (B2.2 F step 4b.3).
  It refuses a folder without `adapter_config.json` and `adapter_model.safetensors` (exit 2, names the file), and
  writes `"adapter": <dir>` and its SHA-256 into `final_eval.json`. `final/` is still saved, for a merged report
  line only. The comparator's (f_merged - f_lora) on the B1 adapter is the expected merged-eval loss; ADR-0013
  records it. Runs under the merged presets (B1, B3) keep `--ckpt <out>/final`, because they sampled
  `round(W + d)` in training too. Test: I48.
- **KL weight (beta).** Owner decision B.8.3 item 5. B1 keeps beta 1e-3 (as R5), so Gate B1 tests data only. For
  B3, the default is `beta = 1e-3 / r`, where r = median |A_v4| / median |A_v5| from B3.7 rule 6. That keeps v4's
  policy-to-KL balance, so the B3 A/B changes only the reward in effect. The B3 config also sets
  `adam_epsilon = 1e-8 / r` from the same r (ADR-0014): Adam with (g / r, eps / r) takes the steps of (g, eps), so
  the smaller v5 gradients do not lower the effective learning rate unevenly. Option: beta 0.0 (Phase C's C8; with LoRA,
  TRL needs no reference copy at any beta [code: .venv trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:1029-1036], so beta can be raised
  later). ADR-0013 records the value. Phase C's G-C step-time gate is then computed for the chosen beta.
- KL spike: one logged KL value of 398,284 at step 746 left grad_norm at 0.0041 (run median 0.0048); median KL 0.32
  [measured: runs/rl/train_rl/rl.json]. It is a diagnostic, not a driver.
### B3. Reward v5

#### B3.1 Centroid sums in the CUDA scorer

- `cuda/gpucheck.cpp`:
  - `kPart` 5 -> 7 [code: gpucheck.cpp:1187]. `ScoreRows` writes two more row partials: `sx` = sum of column
    indices of mask pixels in the row, `sy` = y x (pixels in the row) [code: gpucheck.cpp:1409-1441].
  - Exact integer column sum per 32-bit word w: `32*w*popc(m) + popc(m & 0xAAAAAAAA) + 2*popc(m & 0xCCCCCCCC) +
    4*popc(m & 0xF0F0F0F0) + 8*popc(m & 0xFF00FF00) + 16*popc(m & 0xFFFF0000)` (LSB = leftmost pixel, as the planes
    are packed [code: gpucheck.cpp:1144]). No per-bit loop.
  - `ObjTerms` sums the two partials over rows into `ObjOut` (new `i64 sum_x, sum_y`) [code: gpucheck.cpp:1199,
    1476-1523].
  - `cuda/gpucheck_py.cpp`: return `sum_x`, `sum_y` (int64 per object) from `score_polygons` and `score_masks`.
  - All existing outputs stay bit-identical (golden test).
- Tests: `tests/test_gpu_scoring.py` and `tests/test_cuda_checker_gpu.py` (GPU), `tests/test_checker_host.py` (CPU
  build): sums equal numpy `np.nonzero` sums on 200 random masks and on all fixture masks (each scored against
  `b_tables(m)`, the B.9.5 G01 tables rule: `score_masks` needs one table handle per object in its own frame); CPU build == CUDA build;
  old terms unchanged. `compute-sanitizer` runs in R-D2's `make gpu-check` sanitize step on the small subset test
  `test_g07_sanitize_sums` only (B.9.5 G07; markers `gpu` and `sanitizer`). `test_g01_golden` carries `gpu` only.

#### B3.2 Location term in the scorer adapter

- `src/objdel/reward/cache.py` `ExpertCache`: cached properties `ref_sum = (sum_x, sum_y, n)` of the vote mask if
  `n_vote > 0`, else of the union; `radius2 = |U| / pi` (union area over pi). Host arrays, once per cache.
- `src/objdel/reward/score.py`:
  - `location(sum_x, sum_y, area, ref_sum, radius2, width=1.0) -> float`: 0.0 if `area == 0`; else
    `exp(-d2 / (2 * width^2 * radius2))`, `d2 = (sum_x/area - rx/n)^2 + (sum_y/area - ry/n)^2` (pixel indices on
    both sides, so the half-pixel centres cancel). `width` is a spec constant set in B3.7 (1.0 = v1's kernel). If
    B3.7 picks the heavy-tailed kernel instead, the formula is `1 / (1 + d2 / (width^2 * radius2))`; the choice is
    one function, recorded in ADR-0014.
  - `ObjectTerms` gains `sum_x, sum_y, loc_raw`.
  - Completion term `loc` = mean over objects of the gated per-object value (non-zero only for a missed answer)
    `1[iou_tc < miss_iou] * max(0, 1 - iou_tc / miss_iou) * g_area * 1[topo_freq > 0] * loc_raw`; 0 for an
    unparseable or truncated completion. Add `"loc"` to `NUMERIC`.
  - Why each gate: the ramp makes R continuous at IoU = miss_iou and non-decreasing in IoU for equal f5 and g_area
    (with alpha <= miss_iou); g_area removes specks and huge outlines (zero outside the doctors' area range [code:
    gpucheck.cpp:1515-1520]); `topo_freq > 0` removes shapes whose topology no doctor drew (two blobs whose mean
    centroid sits on the nodule).

#### B3.3 Reward spec v5

- `src/objdel/reward/spec.py`: add `@dataclass(frozen=True) class RewardV5` with `name = "reward_v5"`,
  `alpha_loc = 0.1`, `miss_iou = 0.1` (H2 / Direction s5), `w_f5 = 0.1`, `w_area = 0.1` (H2: <= 0.25 of IoU's
  weight), `c_topo` (set by B3.7; no default until then: the constructor needs it; no `adv_scale`, ADR-0014),
  `loc_width = 1.0`, `area_gate = False` (B3.7 rule), `lam = 0.5`, `eps = 0.1`, `group = 8`, `drop_spread = 0.01`,
  `iou_gate = 0.5` (v4 values [code: spec.py:28-39]). The cache table constants come from `CacheSpec` (B1.0).
- The constructor raises `ValueError` when `alpha_loc > miss_iou`. That order keeps a hit above a miss **for equal
  f5 and g_area** (test T11). It does not hold across different g_area: a miss with g_area = 1 and full location
  scores about 0.1 + 0.1 x 1 = 0.2 against a hit at IoU 0.1 with g_area = 0 at 0.1 [estimate: arithmetic]. B3.7
  measures how often that happens.
- `topology_valid` / `_topology` read `lam, eps, iou_gate` from the active spec, not from `REWARD_V4` directly.

#### B3.4 Advantages v5 (RLOO)

- `src/objdel/reward/advantages.py`: `advantages_v5(terms, group=8, spec=REWARD_V5) -> np.ndarray` (B*G,). It stays
  in this module (numpy, fingerprinted with `REWARD_V5`); Phase E moves the module to `verify/reward/advantages.py`,
  and `rl/` only calls it.
  ```
  area = w_area * g_area * (min(1, iou_tc / miss_iou) if spec.area_gate else 1)
  R = legal * (iou_tc + alpha_loc*loc + w_f5*f5 + area) + c_topo * r_topo
  A_i = R_i - (sum_g R - R_i) / (G - 1)      # RLOO = G/(G-1) x (R_i - mean_g R); group mean of A is exactly 0
  flat = (np.ptp(np.stack([legal, iou_tc, f5, g_area, loc, r_topo], -1), axis=1).max(-1) < spec.drop_spread) \
         & (sig_id == sig_id[:, :1]).all(1)
  A[flat] = 0
  ```
  `r_topo` = today's `_topology` (unchanged maths). `loc` here is the gated term of B3.2 (ramp x g_area x topo x
  loc_raw) **before** `alpha_loc`. Because A has group mean 0, TRL's `sum_then_normalize` with
  `scale_rewards="none"` leaves it unchanged (same reasoning as v4 [code: rewards.py docstring]).
- Why `legal` is in the span test: a parsed but illegal answer keeps its raw terms for logging [code:
  src/objdel/reward/score.py:25-27]. Take 6 legal and 2 illegal answers that draw almost the same ring at IoU_tc
  0.3. The `iou_tc`, `f5`, `g_area` and `loc` spans are below 0.01, and r_topo is 0 for all (IoU < `iou_gate`).
  Without `legal` the group is flat and gets A = 0, although R is 0.3 + 0.1 f5 + area for the legal answers and 0
  for the illegal ones. v4 tests the span of `TERMS`, which includes `legal` [code: src/objdel/reward/spec.py:26;
  advantages.py:98-103]. Test T15.
- Why the drop rule tests each unweighted term: v4 tests the span of each raw term [code:
  src/objdel/reward/advantages.py:103]. A test on the weighted R would drop exactly the far-miss groups the location
  term is for. Example: an all-miss group whose `loc_raw` values span less than 0.1 (every answer more than about 2
  radii away: exp(-2) = 0.135, exp(-4.5) = 0.011 at 3 radii) and whose g_area and F5 are equal has ptp(R) < 0.01
  after `alpha_loc` = 0.1 and the ramp, so it would get A = 0 [estimate: arithmetic].
- Why no scale constant: the optimiser is AdamW, built by the HF Trainer from GRPOConfig, with `max_grad_norm` 1.0.
  The grad norm never comes near the clip (0.0018-0.022, median 0.0048 over 770 steps [measured:
  runs/rl/train_rl/rl.json]). AdamW's step does not depend on a constant gradient scale, except through `eps`
  = 1e-8. Under v4 the per-element RMS gradient is about 1.15e-6, 115 eps [estimate: 0.0048 / sqrt(17,432,576)]. v5
  advantages are about r times smaller (B3.7 rule 6), so at r = 10 the RMS falls to about 11.5 eps, and an element
  at 0.1 x RMS would get about half its step. So the B3 config sets `adam_epsilon = 1e-8 / r` with
  `beta = 1e-3 / r` (B2.4). Then a scale on A changes nothing, and no reward constant is needed.
- Worked check (Direction s5 example, radius 7 px, IoU 0.02 for all, ramp factor 0.8): loc terms 0.62, 0.29,
  0.014 x 6. RLOO for answer 1: 0.1 x (0.62 - (0.29 + 6 x 0.014)/7) = +0.057. Without the ramp the plan's value was
  +0.07; the ramp keeps the sign and order. The drop rule keeps this group: the `loc` span is 0.606 > 0.01.

#### B3.5 Wire v5 into the TRL adapter

- `src/objdel/train/rewards.py`: `TRLReward(caches, stop_ids, spec=REWARD_V5)`; `LOGGED` adds `"loc"`; aggregator
  name `f"advantage_{spec.name.split('_')[1]}"`; `GATED` adds `"loc"`; group checks use `spec.group`. `TRLReward`
  logs `kind/<k>/loc` for every kind: the mean of the gated term before `alpha_loc`. LocGuard (B3.5b) reads it.
- Truncated rows: the B3 config sets `mask_truncated_completions=False` (B.1 item 8). A truncated row keeps R = 0,
  its eval score, and gets A = -b (minus the group baseline). B1 keeps `True`, so Gate B1 stays a data-only test.
  ADR-0014 records it. Every B run report prints the least-squares slope of `completions/clipped_ratio` over the
  steps. Gate B3 reports whether the B3 clipped share is at most B1's.
- Token weight of truncated rows. dr_grpo divides by a constant (`size(0) x max_completion_length` [code: .venv
  trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:3286]), so a 1,536-token truncated row gets about 12 times the gradient mass of a mean
  131-token answer [measured lengths: runs/r5/shared_rl.json]. B3.5 logs `completions/truncated_grad_share` = sum
  over truncated rows of |A| x tokens / sum over all rows of |A| x tokens. The run report prints its median and max.
  If the median exceeds 10 % over steps 50-260, the owner may switch on C11's option "mask the first min(len, T_i)
  tokens" for truncated rows too.
- `src/objdel/train/configs.py`: `grpo_config(..., reward=REWARD_V5)`; `num_generations` check uses
  `reward.group`; `reward_weights` length follows `len(LOGGED) + 1`.
- `train_rl --reward {v4,v5}` (v4 only until B3.10); `rl.json` records `reward = {name, fingerprint, c_topo,
  loc_width, area_gate}` and `beta`.

#### B3.5b Location guard (run guard)

- `callbacks.LocGuard(window=50)` in `src/objdel/train/callbacks.py`. It watches whether the model learns to move
  outlines toward the nodule without hitting it. Active only with `--reward v5`.
- Inputs: per-step means over the off-centre rows only (`kind/shifted/loc`, `kind/rescaled/loc`,
  `kind/shifted/iou_tc` and `kind/rescaled/iou_tc`, B3.5 and B1.5) of the location term and of IoU_tc. Batch means are noisy, because the cell mix changes every step, so a sign test
  would stop a healthy run.
- Rule: stop (and save) only when, in **two disjoint consecutive windows** of 50 logged steps, both hold: (a) the
  least-squares slope of the location mean has t-statistic > 3; (b) the upper 95 % bound of the IoU_tc slope is
  < 0. Both slopes use a Newey-West standard error with lag 5: per-step means of a real run are autocorrelated (the
  policy moves slowly, and the 20-step blocks repeat the cell mix), so an OLS slope t-statistic over 50 steps would
  be too large and the false-stop rate would not hold.
- Unit tests with synthetic logs: seeded noise with flat true trends (per-step sd as in R5) stops in < 1 % of
  300-step runs; a rising location term with a flat-to-falling IoU stops within 100 steps; rising both does not stop;
  fewer than 100 steps never stops. Autocorrelation test: fit AR(1) to the full run's per-step `rewards/iou_tc`
  [measured source: runs/rl/train_rl/rl.json], simulate flat series with that coefficient, and assert < 1 % stops in
  300-step runs.
#### B3.6 Anti-gaming tests (before any spend)

`tests/test_reward_v5.py`, using `tests/oracles/score_numpy.py` and the break-it style of
`tests/test_breakit_reward.py`. List in `docs/implementation2.0/specs/B.spec.md` (T1-T12, T14; T13 is removed with
`adv_scale`; T15 is new in revision 4). The key ones: a huge outline centred on the nodule gets `loc = 0` (g_area); a speck at the centroid
gets `loc = 0`; two blobs around the centroid get `loc = 0`; R is continuous at IoU = 0.1 and non-decreasing in IoU
for equal f5 and g_area; illegal answers get R = 0; RLOO sums to 0 per group and scales linearly with rewards.
**T14:** an all-miss group with `loc_raw` = (0.05, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01) and equal other
terms keeps a non-zero A (the drop rule tests unweighted terms).
**T15 (revision 4):** a group of 6 legal and 2 illegal answers with equal raw terms at IoU_tc 0.3 keeps a non-zero
A, and the 2 illegal answers get A < 0 (the drop rule tests `legal` too).

#### B3.7 Lab round (offline, $0)

- Script `experiments/phase2/reward_lab_v5.py --answers <A3 saved eval answers, K = 8 per item> --view
  data/eval_views/lidc-val-shifted --half shape`. Val-shape only, so val-select stays clean for Gate B3.
- Needs saved answers with text (Phase A3: final_eval saves every answer). Re-score them on the Mac (CPU build of
  gpucheck) and compute v4 and v5 advantages per group.
- Report and rules:
  1. **Location signal in all-miss groups** (a group whose 8 answers are all missed answers). For each all-miss
     group with >= 3 distinct values of d, compute the Spearman correlation of A_i and -d_i / r over its 8 answers,
     where d = centroid distance and r = sqrt(radius2). The value is the mean over groups, with a paired patient
     (group_id) bootstrap 95 % CI (A1). Groups with constant A count as 0 (not excluded), so a rule that zeroes
     groups cannot raise the mean. Gate: v5 mean > 0.3, its CI lower bound > 0, and (v5 - v4) mean > 0 paired by
     group [estimate thresholds]. This replaces v1's "share of all-miss groups with non-zero advantage", which v4
     already has through g_area and F5 (section 1 item 6).
  2. **Drop share:** share of all-miss groups dropped (A = 0 for the whole group), v4 vs v5. Gate: v5 <= v4.
  3. **Variance share:** share of the variance of A in all-miss groups from `w_area * g_area` versus `alpha_loc *
     loc`. If the area term dominates, the location signal is weak; report it.
  4. **Miss beats hit:** share of groups where a missed answer has a higher R than a hit in the same group. If > 1 %,
     set `area_gate = True` (the area term then scales by `min(1, iou_tc / miss_iou)`) and re-measure.
  5. **Distance law:** distribution of d / r for missed answers. If its median is > 3 (the Gaussian kernel is almost
     0 there), set `loc_width` so that the median missed answer gets a location value of at least 0.1, or switch to
     the heavy-tailed kernel; record the choice in ADR-0014. Option to check first: the scorer already sums the
     exact distance to the doctors' union of every spill pixel (`spill`, `spill_n` in `ScoreRows` [code:
     cuda/gpucheck.cpp:1430-1440]), and the distance table is a full-frame EDT [code:
     src/objdel/reward/cache.py:130-135]. So the mean spill distance is available with no new row partial. If it
     predicts IoU gain as well as the centroid term on val-shape, it can replace B3.1 (fewer kernel changes); record
     the comparison.
  6. **Advantage size and KL balance:** median |A| for v4 and for v5 on non-dropped groups; r = median |A_v4| /
     median |A_v5|; the implied effective beta of v5 at beta 1e-3 is 1e-3 x r. The B3 config sets `beta = 1e-3 / r`
     unless the owner chose 0.0 (B.8.3 item 5), and `adam_epsilon = 1e-8 / r` in every case (ADR-0014). Config
     values, not reward constants. Record both in ADR-0014.
  7. **Agreement on hits:** Spearman of A_v4 and A_v5 on groups with all IoU >= 0.1; advantage sd per cell.
  8. **Topology fallback:** margin q95 of (IoU vs vote - best same-signature IoU) over legal answers whose signature
     no doctor drew. Set `c_topo` by rule: the smallest c with `c * eps >= that q95` (so the fallback never beats a
     valid topology, the H1 hack in docs/implementation2.0/notes/H2_rl_math.md s3.4). This rule gives a lower bound
     only. For a valid answer r_topo is about 1, so R jumps by about c at IoU_min = 0.5. Report the jump (c x median
     r_topo of valid answers) and the share of the variance of A in hit groups that comes from `c_topo * r_topo`.
     Gate (pre-run, Gate B3): share <= 0.5 [estimate threshold]. If the lower bound forces a larger share, the owner
     decides between a smaller `eps` and accepting the share; ADR-0014 records the choice.
  9. **Runaway answers:** share of answers that hit the length limit, and their mean v5 R. Today
     `mask_truncated_completions` is True [code: src/objdel/train/configs.py:188]. Masked truncated rows bias the
     update by -b grad P(not truncated) (b = group baseline > 0); runaways rose from 0.00059 to 0.00373 of answers
     over the full run [measured: rl.json, B.1 item 8]. B3 sets it False (B3.5). Option O (DAPO's soft overlong
     penalty) is dropped: unmasking gives the runaway its eval score, 0, as a direct signal. TRL's penalty is
     ((L - cache) - |y|) / cache for L - cache < |y| <= L [code: .venv trl/rewards/other_rewards.py:89-95]. At
     L = 1,200 and cache 200 it starts at 1,000 tokens, but doctor outlines reach 1,181 tokens (header), so a
     correct long outline would lose about its whole IoU reward. If option O is ever revived, a config check must
     require `L - soft_punish_cache >= 1,182 + 32` (end token counted, because the answer cap counts it; header),
     with a unit test.
  10. **Gradient share of all-miss groups.** v4 z-scored each term with floors 0.05, so all-miss groups got
     unit-scale advantages. v5 is mean-centred only, so in an all-miss group A comes from `0.1 loc` and small area
     terms (the B3.4 worked check gives +0.057), against about +-0.3 to 0.6 in a group with hits and misses
     [estimate]. AdamW's shared second moments do not undo a relative scale between groups. Measure
     `S = sum over all-miss groups of sum_i |A_i| / sum over all groups of sum_i |A_i|` for v4 and v5 on val-shape
     answers, beside the all-miss group share. Gate (pre-run, Gate B3): S_v5 >= 0.5 S_v4 [estimate threshold]. If
     it fails, raise `alpha_loc` and `miss_iou` together (keep `alpha_loc <= miss_iou`), or set `loc_width` by
     rule 5, and measure again. ADR-0014 records S.
- Write all values and the evidence into ADR-0014.
#### B3.8 Neyman tilt: removed from Phase B

- v1 tilted cells by `cell/<ij>/group_sd`. Removed, for three reasons. (a) Under v4, all-miss groups have the
  smallest spread, so the tilt would down-weight the miss-heavy off-centre cells, the opposite of the goal. (b) The
  spread would be measured under v4 and used for a v5 run. (c) A tilted mix with factors 0.5-2.0 cannot meet DG7 or
  DG8 against the untilted target, and it would make the B3 A/B change both reward and data.
- 16 answers for hard images (Direction B3): NOT in Phase B. TRL 1.17.1 has one fixed `num_generations`; pooling two
  groups per key breaks the "one item per step" rule and the group checks. Revisit in Phase F.

#### B3.9 B3 run

- Config `experiments/phase2/configs/b3_v5.yaml`: the same start checkpoint as B1 (`rl-full-3ep`), the same B1 rows
  root and `rows_revision` (untilted), B1's numerics preset `--numerics bf16-seqmask` (ADR-0013 rule (b)),
  `--reward v5`, `--lr 5e-5` (as B1), `mask_truncated_completions: false`, `beta` and `adam_epsilon` from B2.4 /
  B3.7 rule 6, the same `--steps` as the B1 run (260, front 6.2), LocGuard and BudgetStop (session spend) on, val
  eval (shifted and edge views). `train_rl --budget-usd` = the front 6.4 rule 5 value for the approved V3 amount
  (front 6.3 "V3 amount rule" holds the values), written in `b3_v5.yaml` before preflight. A lower value cuts the 260 steps, and Gate B3 then compares unequal runs. Step 0 of `b3_v5.yaml` is the CUDA build of `b1_rows.yaml` step 0 (B1.5). Step 1 is
  the G08b smoke, before `train_rl`, so the reward v5 sums are checked on the box before they train anything (final
  round 8, qa-4). It is a `bash -c` step, because a `-m` step cannot set an environment variable (only
  `OBJDEL_RUN_DIR` is exported [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:486, 492]) and the test must find the data
  root: `[bash, -c, "OBJDEL_DATA_ROOT={data} /opt/venv/bin/python -I -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m gpu
  tests/test_train_fast.py::test_g08b_smoke"]` (the D8 form of `d_gpu_test.yaml`). Its 1,000 real windows are the
  first 1,000 crops of `checker_eval/masks.npz` under the data root, which the LIDC bundle of every V3 sync holds
  (D8 payload item 1). The test opens it only through `box_input("checker_eval/masks.npz")` (D8 rule), and
  `tests/test_train_fast.py` defines `BOX_INPUTS = ("checker_eval/masks.npz",)`. Without the variable the default
  root `data` resolves to `/workspace/src/data`, which the code sync drops [code: policy.py:379], so the test fails
  (never skips). The D-G14, D-G15 and D-G17 records need no step or flag here: D7 step 5 writes
  them in code on a CUDA build (final round 8, cuda-2 and qa-3). Step 2 is the B1 re-eval (final
  round 11, fresh-arch-1): one `final_eval` process in the B1 form (B1.5 step 4) on `--ckpt {rd}/b1/final` (the
  merged B1 model, fetched by front 6.3 item 0 with `fetch_hf.sh <run> b1-rows --as b1`), with `--out
  {rd}/eval_b1v3_val_shifted` and `--out {rd}/eval_b1v3_val_edge`. It runs before `train_rl`, so the eval tail
  after `BudgetStop` stays the 26 min of front 6.2. Why: Gate B3 pairs B3 with B1 on the same code, box and
  sampler, as Gate B1 does with R5 (B.6.2). Between V1 and V3 the eval path changes (D7 moves eval pixel work into
  the engine; after E4 `final_eval` uses `VllmSampler`, not the trainer path). V1's `eval_b1_val_*` would carry
  those changes into the B3 - B1 difference. No test
  eval here: test is read once, after the 4B gate (B.4 step 6). Step 3, the `train_rl` step, writes `--out
  {rd}/b3-v5` with `--save-steps 50` (as B1.5 step 3). It is a soft step (first word `~`), as B1.5 step 3. Step 3b is
  the hard step `train_rl --merge-last --model qwen3-vl-2b --ckpt {rd}/ckpt --out {rd}/b3-v5`, the B1.5 step 3b rule
  on the B3 folder (final round 14, rl-2). Why: `train_rl` writes `final/` only after `trainer.train` returns [code:
  experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:55-60], and the `&&` join skips every later step after a hard failure [code:
  policy.py:484-490]. Without steps 3 (soft) and 3b, a crash late in the 260 steps leaves no B3 val eval and no Gate
  B3 result. With them, the val eval runs on the last checkpoint, and `rl.json` holds `steps: N` and `partial: true`.
  A lost host is covered by the pull job of the V3 launch lines (front 6.3; front 6.2 "Why the pull job"). The val
  eval is one `final_eval` step in the B1 form (B1.5 step 4) on `--ckpt {rd}/b3-v5/final`, with `--out
  {rd}/eval_b3_val_shifted` and `--out {rd}/eval_b3_val_edge`; D's S13 reads `eval_b3_val_shifted`. The
  last step is C's G-RC0 box check by node id, a soft step (final round 12, qa-2):
  `[~, -m, pytest, -q, -p, no:cacheprovider, -m, gpu, tests/test_c_gpu.py::test_g_rc0_per_row_caps]`. A failure is
  logged and the chain ends normally [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:484-487]. It blocks only C11's arm,
  never B3: C11 applies from the first run after Gate B3 (last paragraph below). It runs after the B3 val eval, so it
  can never delay `train_rl` or the evals (C.9.4 holds the test and its model; front 6.3 item 0 prices it). A node
  id, not `-k`: B.9.5 never runs `pytest -m gpu` without a file list on a box. So the order of `b3_v5.yaml` is:
  0 CUDA build, 1 G08b smoke, 2 B1 re-eval, 3 `train_rl` (soft), 3b `train_rl --merge-last`, 4 B3 val eval,
  5 G-RC0 (soft).
- Launch config `experiments/phase2/configs/b3_launch.yaml` (created in the same commit; front 6.3 "V3 launch
  config" holds its text): a `RunArgs` file with `output_dir: b3-v5` (the HF revision of the B3 push) and
  `rows_plan: experiments/phase2/configs/b3_v5.yaml`, so the V3 stamp holds the rows-root SHA-256 and the "ROWS
  root" and "ROWS revision" checks of B3's `train_rl` stage.
  Against B1, the reward changes, plus the truncation mask (part of v5, ADR-0014), plus `beta` and `adam_epsilon`
  scaled by the same r (which keeps v4's balance and Adam's step). The serving path and the IS mode do not change.
  B3 keeps `max_completion_length` 1,536 and `--runaway-cap 0`, as B1. The outline limit L (C7) and the runaway cap
  (C11) apply from the first run after Gate B3. Why: an L below 1,536 turns naturally ended long answers into
  truncated rows with R = 0, and dr_grpo rescales the loss by 1,536 / L [code: grpo_trainer.py:3286]. That would be a
  fifth change that B3.10 would credit to v5.

#### B3.10 Clean after gate B3

B3.10 runs only after Gate B3, so only after a raise funds V3. Under the default (b'), B2.2-B2.4 and B3 code wait on
the owner branch `after-raise`, `main` keeps reward v4 only, and no v5 code sits beside it (front section 1 "End
state under (b')" holds the rule).

- What is credited: "v5 + unmasked truncation on the B1 preset `bf16-seqmask`". ADR-0014 writes this sentence.
- Pass: v5 becomes the only reward. Move `RewardV4`, `advantages_v4`, their tests and the v4 TRL wiring to
  `archive/reward_v4/` with a README row (what, replaced by, restore command). Remove `--reward`. Update
  `docs/reference/reward.md`, `docs/glossary.md` (RLOO, location term, miss, missed answer),
  `src/objdel/eval/signal.py` weights if they mirror v4 (E1 Q5).
- Fail: keep v4, archive v5 code to `archive/reward_v5_try/`, record why in ADR-0014.

## B.5. Custom kernels used

- **No new kernel file in Phase B.** B3.1 extends the existing `ScoreRows` / `ObjTerms` functors in
  `cuda/gpucheck.cpp` (single source, CPU and nvcc builds) with two integer partials. If B3.7 rule 5 shows that the
  existing spill-distance sum serves as the location signal, B3.1 is skipped.
- Related kernel designs, used later or optionally:
  - K2 `edt_tables` (GPU EDT for the cache tables): `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K2/DESIGN.md` (s7 item 6). When
    Phase D lands it, B1.4 materialization calls it instead of scipy; bits are identical (K2 s5), so no fingerprint
    change.
  - K1 polygonizer (certified targets on the GPU): `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1/DESIGN.md`. Same role for targets
    in B1.4 after Phase D: D2 swaps K1 in behind the B1.4a seam, under D3 step 3's hash check.
  - K3 `is_ratio` (fused ratio + stats): `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K3/DESIGN.md` (s4 (b)). Optional: if adopted
    in Phase C, it must also emit the B2.1 fields (including the counterfactual stats) and support the chosen B2
    preset.

### B.6.2 Run gates

Common rules for Gates B1 and B3:
- **Value.** Every run gate uses the per-item mean of IoU_tc over the K = 8 answers (`sel_mean_of_k`), whatever
  Gate A picks. The Gate A answer-choice method is reported as a second line. A miss uses the K-mean rule.
- **Pairing and CI.** Paired on the same items, patient level (all items of a patient move together), 95 %. The
  decision interval is the A1 gate CI: the percentile patient interval when the gate set has >= 50 patients (Gate
  B1, whole val, 78 patients), and `signal.cluster_t` when it has < 50 (Gate B3, val-select, about 39 patients).
  `signal.cluster_t` is the CR1 cluster-robust t interval of the **item-weighted** mean difference (A1 step 5):
  with per-patient sums S_p, counts N_p and P patients, m = sum S_p / sum N_p, se^2 = P / (P - 1) x sum_p (S_p -
  m N_p)^2 / (sum N_p)^2, interval m +- t(P - 1, 0.975) se [web: Cameron and Miller 2015, J. Human Resources
  50(2):317-372]. Why item-weighted: every point rule uses the item mean, and on val the two means differ by 0.029
  (0.618 item-weighted, 0.647 patient-weighted; 2-78 items per patient; the 5 largest patients hold 24.9 % of the
  items) [measured: runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl joined with group_id]. A t interval of the per-patient means
  would not be centred on the reported gain. The other interval is printed beside it, with the cluster count. For a
  subset rule (far misses, near IoU, found by both), apply the same choice to the per-item differences of the
  subset, with P = the patients that have items in it, and print that count (far subset: 35 patients on the
  revision-2 val-select [measured: final_r1_data.md]; B1.0 re-measures it on the re-dealt halves). Reason for
  patient level: nodules of one patient share the reading sessions, the scanner and the reconstruction, and on R5
  val-select the patient CI is 23 % wider than the nodule CI (0.085 vs 0.069) [measured:
  docs/implementation2.0/notes/b_final/cluster_ci.json, B = 4,000, seed 0, script cluster_ci.py beside it].
- **Noise floor.** Reported beside each gain: `noise_floor.mean_sd` from A3 step 7 (the two K = 4 halves of one
  val sampling, scaled by 1/sqrt 2). It is K = 8 sampling noise, and the paired patient CI of every gate already
  contains it. Pre-V1 reference: two K = 8 samplings of `rl-full-3ep` on the same 128 `lidc-val-shifted` items
  differ with a per-item SD of 0.0569 (Pearson 0.971, mean difference -0.0076), so the per-arm variance is about
  0.00162, against 0.0211 for the Bernoulli bound mu (1 - mu) / 8 [measured: `r4data/retest.py` on
  `runs/rl/eval/final/heldout.json` and `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl`]. B1.9 uses this pair.
  Training-seed variance is not measured; a gain is a single-run result (also in DOC11 Known issues).
- **Paired baseline (one rule, fixed before any B1 number is read).**
  - Primary: A3's R5 val items (front 6.2 item 5: `rl-full-3ep` on the frozen `lidc-val-shifted` view, the same
    code and the same box as the B1 eval). Then a view or host difference cannot enter the B1 - baseline
    difference. R5's `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl` is a report line.
  - When V1's R5 process (front items 4-5) gave no output (front 6.2 fallback): R5's `eval_val/items.jsonl` is
    the baseline. Its view identity is then the measured hash chain of B1.0 (the R5 launch stamp's data hash equals
    the recomputed one, and it covers the `lidc-val-shifted` manifest that pins `val.jsonl` and
    `target_set_sha256`), recorded in `runs/a3/val_pre_rebuild.json`. The report marks the rule "hash only,
    correlation not run". If that chain is broken, Gate B1 waits for A3-val in V2 item 1b (front 6.3).
  - Edge baseline (front 6.2 "The edge rule under the fallback"): item 4 is the only R5 edge baseline. If item 4 ran
    and item 5 did not, the edge rule pairs with item 4 and only the shifted rules use the fallback. If item 4 gave
    no output, Gate B1 is "open: edge baseline missing", never a pass; the other rules are computed and printed.
    V2 item 1b then gives the baseline under a raise. Under (b'), or when item 1b fails again, Gate B1 takes front
    1.1 row 4 (stop, owner review) with the reason "edge baseline missing".
  - When B1.0's rebuild changed the content hash: item 5 is the only baseline (B1.0 step 2).
  - Which case applies depends only on whether item 5 ran and on B1.0's record. It never depends on a B1 result.
    The report names the baseline used.
- **View identity (from A-G3).** When item 5 ran: the Pearson correlation of per-item IoU_tc between A3 and R5 must
  be at least the 95 % patient-bootstrap lower bound of `r_sh = 2 r_h / (1 + r_h)`, where `r_h` is the correlation
  of the answer 0-3 and 4-7 means (A3 step 7). If this correlation rule fails, Gate B1 still pairs with A3's items
  (same frozen view, same box); only the R5 report line is dropped. If A-G3's TOST fails, Gate B1 is still decided
  on A3's items, and the report states the A3 - R5 difference. So the correlation is not a Gate B1 hard rule. The
  frozen-view hash is one (Gate B1 list below).
- **Known label issues.** Val items listed under `known_label_issues` (B1.7) are excluded from every Gate B1 and
  Gate B3 rule, the same in both arms; the report prints the line with them.
- "Pass" needs every point rule and every CI rule. Rules are fixed before the run (B1.9 prices them). No near-miss is
  accepted after the run.
- R5's per-item values come from `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl` (1,084 items) [measured]. Each item's offset
  comes from the frozen view's `view.offset_frac` (B1.6).
- **Val-select stays clean** (ADR-0015): any change to the B1 rows after Gate B1 is decided on val-shape numbers
  and training logs only.
- **Limitations** (also in DOC11): the test split informed the diagnosis (R5's per-offset test results, B.1 item 2);
  from 2026-11-08 every design number uses train or val only. The target law is a synthetic shift law; the guard
  views check other laws. Val already chose R5: 128 val shifted items (51 of the 78 val patients) chose the final
  model over checkpoint-250 and served the G-probe [docs/research/notes/full_rl_2026-11-08.md:31, 49; measured:
  runs/rl/eval/final/heldout.json joined with group_id]. R5's val numbers are slightly optimistic on them, so Gate B1
  is conservative; Gate B3 (B3 vs B1) is not affected. Gate B1 prints a sensitivity line without these 128 items
  (ids in `docs/reference/val_halves.json` under `r5_selection_items`).

- **Gate B1** (the whole val: 78 patients, 200 nodules, 1,084 items; baselines in section 1; "R5" below means the
  paired baseline of the common rules: A3's value, with R5's 0.618 for reference):
  - val IoU: CI lower bound of (B1 - R5) > 0 (R5 0.618). The target 0.66 is reported, not gated. Decomposition: a
    25 % cut of far misses turns about 0.25 x 0.273 x 406 = 28 misses into found images; at the found IoU 0.706 that
    adds about 28 x 0.706 / 1,084 = +0.018 [estimate: arithmetic on measured values]. Reaching 0.66 needs gains on
    found images too.
  - val misses at offset > 0.3: point <= 20.5 % (25 % below R5's 27.3 %) and CI upper bound of (B1 - R5) < 0;
  - val IoU at offset < 0.15: CI lower bound of (B1 - R5) > -0.02 (R5 0.751; no regression on centred images);
  - extra-steps control (hard, difference in differences): with the same patient draws, the CI lower bound of
    (far gain - near gain) > 0. Far gain = mean (B1 - R5) over items with offset > 0.3; near gain = the same over
    offset < 0.15. Extra centred training lifts both subsets; the data fix lifts mostly the far one (ADR-0015
    confound). B1.9 prices this rule. Informative check (ADR-0015): if A2's near-subset headroom upper bound is
    below 0.013, the report calls this rule uninformative and states the result as "B1 vs R5", not "data effect".
    With the owner's checkpoint-250 option (B.8.3 item 12), the rule becomes the CI lower bound of [far gain -
    (260/520) x far gain(250 -> 770)] > 0 on the same patient draws;
  - guard law: val IoU on the `edge` view, non-padded and non-fallback items: CI lower bound of (B1 - R5) > -0.02
    (R5 on the edge view is front 6.2 item 4; without it, see the "Edge baseline" bullet above). Padded and
    fallback edge items are a report line;
  - legal share on val >= 0.99 (R5 0.995);
  - frozen-view hash: each B1 and A3 `final_eval.json` `view_content_sha256` equals its `frozen_views.json` entry
    (DG15). A mismatch fails Gate B1 (front 1.1: stop, owner review), because the pair would not score the same
    images;
  - report only: paired patient-CI difference vs R5 on `lidc-val-rescaled` and `lidc-val-rotated`, with a
    non-inferiority note at -0.02 (only if the owner adds these evals to a rental; they are not in the front V1 list);
  - report only: the near and far gains themselves; the sensitivity line without the 128 `r5_selection_items`; the
    held-out 128-item points at steps 250 and 770 (0.634, 0.659; `rl.json` of the full run has no eval key in its
    771 log entries [measured]), plus the B1 run's own val-shape curve when the owner turns on `--heldout` (B1.5);
    if it stays off, the report says so, and the B-S2 step count stays an owner choice;
  - test is not read here (test once, final candidate only).
- **Gate B2** (preset for the runs after Gate B3; B2.4):
  - B1 run: NaN/inf count = 0 over all steps; the counterfactual stats are present for steps 50-260;
  - the chosen preset (B2.4 rule 0, else `bf16-tis-opsm` with its vetoes) and its veto values are recorded in
    ADR-0013; under `lora-seqmask`, the F check of B2.4 rule 0 passed in the first 15 steps of the run that uses it
    (`f_check.json` `passed`: NaN/inf = 0, LoRA tensors equal under vLLM's layout, load count 1, restore base hash
    equal, floor-subtracted comparator ratio <= 0.5 or `informative: false`, median of the 6 fixed-length LoRA /
    base generate-time ratios <= 1.15 in the same process; B2.2 F steps 4-5);
  - optional fp16 arm (`fp16-seqmask`, steps 41-60): NaN/inf = 0; the vLLM dtype assertion passed; the paired
    prompt bootstrap 95 % lower bound of (fp16 - B1) `rewards/iou_tc` > -0.02 [estimate threshold].
- **Gate B3:**
  - before the run: T1-T12, T14 and T15 pass (`B.spec.md`); lab round (B3.7, val-shape): location Spearman mean
    > 0.3 under v5, CI lower bound > 0, and higher than v4 paired by group; drop share v5 <= v4; miss-beats-hit
    share <= 1 % (after `area_gate` if needed); gradient share of all-miss groups S_v5 >= 0.5 S_v4 (rule 10);
    topology share of the advantage variance in hit groups <= 0.5 (rule 8);
  - the B3 run used B1's preset `bf16-seqmask` (ADR-0013 rule (b)), so the gate credits "v5 + unmasked truncation";
  - after the run, on val-select (re-dealt halves, B1.0), paired against the B1 re-eval of the same rental (B3.9
    step 2, `eval_b1v3_val_shifted` and `eval_b1v3_val_edge`: same code, box and sampler as the B3 eval). V1's
    `eval_b1_val_*` is a report line only, as R5's `items.jsonl` is for Gate B1. Rules: miss share falls by >= 25 %
    relative (point) and the CI upper bound of (B3 - B1) miss share < 0; IoU on images found by **both** runs: CI
    lower bound of (B3 - B1) > -0.01 (the paired set avoids the composition bias of new, harder hits); `edge` view
    IoU: CI lower bound of (B3 - B1) > -0.02; legal share >= 0.99;
  - report only: the B3 clipped share against B1's, and the slope of `completions/clipped_ratio` in each run.

## B.7. Risks and rollback

| Risk | Sign | Mitigation / rollback |
|---|---|---|
| Val shapes the training mix and also judges the gates | val gains more than test | Fixed: the target is the train shifted law (B1.4). No val data reaches training. Test is read once. |
| The model fits the one synthetic shift law of the test view | shifted val gains, `edge` / rescaled / rotated views fall | Guard views (B1.6) with a hard floor on `edge` (Gate B1). |
| Small gate sets (78 patients for B1, 38 for B3) | wide patient CIs; a real gain fails | B1.9 power check before the rental (joint P(pass) of Gate B1 rules (1)-(4); Gate B3 power is a report line); paired comparisons; fixed rules, no written near-miss acceptance. |
| Gains are seed noise | a single-run gain | Stated as a limitation (B.6.2, DOC11). A second-seed B1 run is the only measurement; owner decision, not in $3. The A3 split-half `mean_sd` is sampling noise, already inside the paired CI; it is not the mitigation. |
| Gain comes from 300 more steps, not data | near-centre gain as large as far gain | Hard difference-in-differences rule in Gate B1 (far gain - near gain > 0); ADR-0015 states the confound with the held-out numbers (0.634 -> 0.659 from step 250 to 770). |
| `draws` needed for DG7 is large; disk grows | B1.4 table | Only scheduled windows are materialized, so disk stays near 1.2-1.6 GB [estimate from 7,341 windows = 1.2 GB]. |
| A budget cut trains a prefix that misses the target | DG7-DG9 fail on a prefix | 20-step blocks; only whole blocks are trained (B1.2, B1.5). |
| Noisy doctor references give a near-random reward | DG14b share of low agreement | Report before B1.4; owner rule B.8.3 item 4. |
| Rescaled share hurts the shifted test view (Q5 in B1.md) | per-kind logs: rescaled reward rises, shifted flat | Shares are config; set rescaled 0 in a rebuild ($0). The rebuild is decided on val-shape numbers and training logs only; val-select numbers from the B1 run are reported, not used (ADR-0015). |
| Rescaled slots reuse a few large-nodule items | DG14 distinct items per (rescaled, cell), largest reuse | ADR-0015 trade-off; owner picks option (i) or (ii) (B.8.3 item 3b). |
| Merge rounding erases the LoRA delta in vLLM | B2.0 table (46-69 % of delta elements erased on the full run's adapters) | It is a systematic gap that grows with the adapter; truncated and masked IS modes trade bias for variance. B2.4 rule 0 picks `lora-seqmask` (vLLM serves the adapter unmerged), else `fp16-seqmask`, for the runs after Gate B3; B1 and B3 both run on `bf16-seqmask`, so their A/B has no numerics change (ADR-0013 rule (b)). |
| Gate B1 fails | B.6.2 rule fails | The decision table B.4.1, approved before V1, names the next step for each failing rule. |
| B3 credits a serving change to v5 | B3 preset differs from B1's | Not possible under ADR-0013 rule (b): B3 keeps `bf16-seqmask`; B3.10 credits "v5 + unmasked truncation". |
| F plumbing bug rejects F for a non-numerics reason | NaN or reward collapse after the first sleep/wake; slow generate | B2.2 F step 2: the unmerged base push in mode B, `add_lora` once per sync, `load_inplace=False` on generate, `reset_prefix_cache`; the LoRA equality check runs after a sleep/wake cycle; timing inside one process (B2.4 rule 0). |
| v5's smaller gradients meet Adam's `eps` | per-element RMS near eps | `adam_epsilon = 1e-8 / r` with `beta = 1e-3 / r` (ADR-0014; U71). |
| A test label issue appears after the test hash is frozen | B1.7 hit on a test series (one exists today: LIDC-IDRI-0659, 4 items) | Test keeps its items and labels; ids in `known_label_issues`; sensitivity line in every test report; the owner decides fix or keep before A3 step 1 (B.8.3 item 13); a label fix after A3 step 1 needs the owner's written decision (B1.7). |
| A val label issue breaks the frozen val view | B1.7 hit on a val series (the duplicate-z list names LIDC-IDRI-0085 and -0146) | Val hits stay in the frozen view; ids in `known_label_issues`; excluded from every gate rule in both arms (B1.7, B.6.2). |
| fp16 overflow (no VLM in the paper; known Qwen2.5-VL case) | inf/NaN or large activations in the Mac check | Full-model Mac check before the optional arm; on failure the arm is dropped. |
| vLLM LoRA serving (F) is slow or wrong | in-process LoRA / base generate-time ratio > 1.15, or LoRA tensors differ under vLLM's layout | B2.4 rule 0 falls back to `fp16-seqmask`, then `bf16-tis-opsm`; the F patch points are in the A7 start-up check. |
| New private TRL patch (`LLM` kwargs: dtype or LoRA) breaks on a TRL update or silently does nothing | A7 start-up check fails; dtype or LoRA-tensor assertion fails | TRL stays pinned 1.17.1; both checks stop the run with a message. Needed only for options A and F. |
| The preset after Gate B3 differs from B1's | B2.4 picks `bf16-tis` or `bf16-tis-opsm` | ADR-0013 notes it; the counterfactual stats show the size of the weight change. |
| token_truncate is biased for long answers (secondary sources) | `cf/tok_clamp2_share` high | Option E (OPSM) is the length-fair option; D only under its trigger. |
| KL spike (398,284 once) | `kl` max in log | It left grad_norm at 0.0041 (median 0.0048); a diagnostic, not a driver. |
| Location term gamed | T1-T14; `loc` rises while IoU stays flat | Gates in B3.2; LocGuard (B3.5b) stops the run on two windows of clear evidence. |
| Location kernel too short for real misses | B3.7 d / r median > 3 | `loc_width` or the heavy-tailed kernel, chosen from data. |
| KL balance differs between v4 and v5 | B3.7 median |A| ratio r | `beta = 1e-3 / r` in the B3 config (or 0.0 by owner decision). Adam needs no scale constant. |
| Masked truncated rows raise the runaway share | `completions/clipped_ratio` slope; B3.7 rule 9 | B3 unmasks truncated rows (R = 0, A = -b); B1 keeps the mask for a clean data test. Option O dropped (it would penalise correct long outlines). |
| All-miss groups get too small a share of the update | B3.7 rule 10: S_v5 < 0.5 S_v4 | Raise `alpha_loc` with `miss_iou`, or set `loc_width`; measure again before the run (Gate B3). |
| c_topo too large: topology dominates IoU | topology share of the A variance in hit groups > 0.5 (B3.7 rule 8) | Gate B3 pre-run rule; owner picks a smaller `eps` or accepts the share (ADR-0014). |
| Fingerprint split makes all caches stale | `StaleCacheError` | Done once in B1.0, before any build; the error names the file. |
| Kernel change alters old terms | golden test | Outputs are additive; revert the commit if goldens change. |
| Rows dropped, reordered or a different upload loaded | manifest hash, count or ids hash assertion | `train_rl` refuses to start (B1.5). |
| Resume replays a different order | `ids_sha256` / step index | Order is the file; HF resume skips consumed batches; resume test on a 4-step stub (B1.5). |
| B1 training crashes before step 260 | `train_rl` exits non-zero; no `final/` | `b1_rows.yaml` step 3 is soft; step 3b (`--merge-last`) merges the last checkpoint into `final/` with `partial: true`, so the B1 eval still runs; front 1.1 row "B1 stopped early" decides what the result may be used for (I49). |
| B3 training crashes before step 260 | `train_rl` exits non-zero; no `final/` | `b3_v5.yaml` step 3 is soft; step 3b (`--merge-last`) merges the last checkpoint, so the B3 val eval still runs, and the V3 pull job keeps checkpoints off the box (B3.9; front 6.3) (I22b, I49). |
| Budget overrun | session spend; BudgetStop | B.8 plan; preflight refuses over cap; BudgetStop measures session spend from the launch time (B1.5), so it trips before the `--cap-hours` deadline and the Gate B1 evals still run. |

Rollback is per task: an old prepared root still loads until B1.8 (no `schedule` = old path); numerics are a preset;
reward v4 stays until gate B3; the kernel change is one commit.

## B.8. Cost and time, dependencies

### B.8.1 Money and GPU minutes

Front section 6 is the only place for rental items, minutes, dollars, caps, skip rules and the stamped launch config.
B holds no copy of a rental table. DOC4 check 16 reports one. B's sessions map to the front rentals:

- **B-S1 = rental V1, front 6.2.** Item 2 is the B1 run (`b1_rows.yaml` step 3, `--budget-usd 2.05`); item 3 is the
  B1 val evals (`b1_rows.yaml` step 4); items 4-5 are A3's R5 process (`a3_measure.yaml`). The launch config is
  `b1_launch.yaml` (B1.5). No V1 item is skippable, and no V1 rule reads the ledger total. V1 has no nsys capture.
- **B-S2 = rental V3 items 0 and 4, front 6.3** (the B3 run). Items 2a, 2b and 5 (the test eval, when the owner has
  closed the 4B gate) are optional V3 rows, approved by name; front 6.3 holds the one definition and the "V3 amount
  rule". It runs only after the owner's budget decision (B.8.3 item 1) and only on a B.4.1 row that funds it.
- V1 plus B-S2 does not fit the $3 (front 6.3). Direction.md already says Phase B needs more than $3 and an owner
  decision.

Phase-local notes (no rental numbers):

- Step time 27.5 s is the pessimistic base; 23.65 s comes from a short R5 test on centred rows, so it is
  optimistic for shifted rows; 20.0 s applies only after Phase C's C-G-SP1 passes, so never to V1 (front 6 inputs).
- Options that are not in the front lists (each needs a front change before it can run): one eval of
  `runs/rl/train_rl/trainer/checkpoint-250` on `lidc-val-shifted` (B.8.3 item 12); B1 on `lidc-val-rescaled` and
  `lidc-val-rotated`; the held-out curve (B.8.3 item 15). An option added to V1 also lowers `--budget-usd` by its
  cost (front 6.4 rule 5).
- The F check (B2.4 rule 0) in the first run after Gate B3 is the first 15 steps of that run (0 extra minutes). If it
  fails, the run restarts under the fallback preset: 6 min of start-up plus the 15 lost steps. The front prices it
  when that rental is planned.
- The merged fallback (B.8.3 item 1, option c) is one run with the B1 rows and reward v5. It has the V1 shape, so it
  costs what V1 costs (front 6.2).
- `BudgetStop` sets the session-spend stop per run in the plan file, so an overrun stops and saves instead of
  billing on.

### B.8.2 Mac time

Pool + schedule simulation for 4 values of `draws`, minutes [estimate from "about 1 minute" per full audit];
materialization of 9,600 windows about 1 min with 2 processes [estimate scaled from 22,023 windows in 2 min 11 s];
the DG13 re-render of every scheduled window about 1 min [estimate: same scale]; the B1.0 rebuild of prepared roots
and views: same order; the all-series z check: seconds [estimate]; B1.9 power check: minutes [estimate]; fp16 full
model check: minutes [estimate]; B2.0 merge-rounding table on all layers: minutes [estimate];
the Mac part of B2.3b (four forwards of 256 sequences on CPU, two adapters): hours [estimate].
$0.

### B.8.3 Owner decisions needed

1. Budget. Default (b'): keep $3 and run B-S1 first (rental V1, B1 260 steps; front 6.2 prices it); B-S2 waits for
   a budget decision. Option (a): raise the cap for B1-then-B3 attribution (front 6.3 prices B-S2; 99_back decision
   1 has the total). Option (c): the merged run (V1 shape, front 6.2), which loses the B1-vs-B3 split (the lab round B3.7 and the per-cell logs are then the only evidence
   for v5's own effect). The B1.9 power number is shown with this decision. A shorter B1 must be a multiple of 20
   steps.
2. (Removed in final round 11, fresh-arch-3: no polygonizer exception is needed. B1.4a puts the engine behind the
   seam before B1.4. The number is kept so later items keep theirs.)
3. Kind shares (15 / 75 / 10), the val-half rule (B1.0) and the disagreement weight (4, default, or 1).
3b. Rescaled kind target (ADR-0015 trade-off): (i) one target for both off-centre kinds (default; DG14 reports
   item reuse) or (ii) the rescaled kind's own draw-0 apparent law, with DG7-DG9 per kind.
4. Label noise (DG14b): keep all (default: honest test), or drop items with doctor LOO IoU_tc < X, or weight them
   0.5. Decided before B1.4 runs.
5. KL weight: B1 beta 1e-3 (fixed, as R5). B3: `1e-3 / r` (default) or 0.0 (Phase C's C8).
6. Rows-root storage: the private model repo under `rows/` (default) or a separate private HF dataset repo
   (front-matter owner decision 10). One place; the config pins `rows_revision`.
7. Truncated rows in B3: unmasked (default, B3.5; option O dropped). Phase C's C11 decides its own capped-row rule
   with the same bias argument (B.1 item 8).
8. Optional fp16 arm in B-S2 (`fp16-seqmask`, 60 steps plus its process start-up; rental V3 item 2b, front 6.3). Default off unless
   the full-model Mac check passes and the budget allows. Under ADR-0013 rule (b) it informs only the runs after
   Gate B3.
9. Option F (vLLM LoRA serving) and the B3 preset. Default, rule (b): B3 keeps B1's preset `bf16-seqmask`; B2.4
   rule 0 picks `lora-seqmask` for the runs after Gate B3 when the B2.0 step-100 relative error is >= 0.2 (the seed
   run gives 0.531). Its F check is the first 15 steps of that run (0 extra minutes; a failed check costs a restart,
   B.8.1). Rule (a), F joins B1 in V1, is not offered: the front V1 list has no minutes for it.
10. The behaviours pinned in B.9.12 (defaults listed there).
11. V1 amount: $2.40 with `--budget-usd 2.05` (front 6.2; the owner approves it in front 6.1 step 0). Keeping the
    older $2.20 means a 260-step B1 run (front 6.2 notes).
12. V1 option: evaluate `runs/rl/train_rl/trainer/checkpoint-250` on `lidc-val-shifted` ($0.07) to measure the
    gain of 520 centred steps per subset and sharpen Gate B1's control rule (ADR-0015). Default off (not in the front V1
    list; adding it needs a front change).
13. The test-series hit LIDC-IDRI-0659 (4 test items, B1.7): fix (DICOM header check, rebuild) or keep
    (`known_label_issues`, sensitivity line). Due before A3 step 1.
14. The decision table B.4.1 (what each Gate B1 result leads to). Approved before V1, so it cannot be bent after the
    result.
15. Held-out curve in the B1 run (`--heldout`, val-shape, 64 items x 8 answers, every 50 steps; about 2 min = $0.02). Default
    off, because the front V1 table has no minutes for it.
