- **G-PX1 CUDA equals CPU equals HF (G-EQ1)** [s1: PX18, PX19; s2: T11]. 2,000 or more views (centred, shifted and rescaled
  rows of the B1 rows root) plus all 32 images of each of the 5 `c_speed_check` batches (C1); batches of 1, 8, 64, 256; backends `hf`, `torch`, `k3` where

- **G-PX3 speed** [s1: PX21; s2: T142]. 32 images 512 x 512: `patchify` (torch, cuda) under 5 ms median of 50; ImageMemo pass-2 call under 10 ms; 256 rows
  under 20 ms warm; at least 5x faster than the CPU processor (baseline recorded). Soft gate (skip on shared CI). Covers C1, G-SP3.
- **G-PX4 H2D bytes** [s2: T144]. H2D of the pixel pass is at most 32 x 512 x 512 x 3 + 1 MB = 25.2 MB (no 256-row upload).
  Covers C1, G-SP5.
- **G-PX5 OOM leaves no damage** [s2: T127]. A 4,096-image `patchify` OOM propagates; the next normal ImageMemo call equals HF;
  memory returns to the pre-call level (+ 1 MB) after `gc.collect()` + `empty_cache()`. Covers C1.
- **G-IM1 placement** [s1: IM10; s2: T24]. `pixel_values.is_cuda`, `image_grid_thw` on CPU, in both `per_image` modes and in the
  fallback path; values equal HF after `.cpu()`. Covers C1, G-SP4.
- **G-IM2 memory** [s1: EN10; s2: T29, T66]. The memo holds at most 201 MB (+10 %) after the call; on the encoder-once path the
  `max_memory_allocated` increase attributable to pixels is under 100 MB (under 400 MB measured for the whole call); no CUDA tensor
  of shape `(256*1024, 1536)` exists (scan `gc` or the memory snapshot); peak at most 30 GB. Covers C1, C3, G-MEM.
- **G-RP1 rope on device** [s1: RP9 GPU, RP12; s2: T44 box]. `count_syncs()` is 0 and `set_sync_debug_mode("error")` raises
  nothing around `rope_positions`; CPU template with CUDA inputs and the reverse work without a sync; < 5 ms for 256 rows. Covers C2, G-SP4.

At least 50 batches (at least 15 from the box: the check-arm files in the adopted fast arm's folder, `c_check/arm_batches_b` when item 3c ran, else `c_check/arm_batches` (C.6), and the 5 `c_speed_check` batches in `c_check/batches`) x
  256 rows: every row `torch.equal` HF, 0 `bad` rows on LIDC, including 1,536-token truncated and 0-token answers. Covers C2, G-EQ2.

  least 15 box, read as G-RP2 reads them, with the same `OBJDEL_V2_RUN` skip rule); `count_syncs()` is 0 across the four host functions; each function under 1 ms (`row_meta` under 3 ms). Covers C4, G-EQ3, G-SP4.
- **G-EN1 encoder-once equality (G-EQ4)** [s1: EN11]. Reference pass and 16 update chunks of `c_speed_check` batch 0 of the real
  model, with its seeded group-centred advantages: logprobs and entropies `torch.equal`, one micro-batch's LoRA grads equal, tower called once; first run the
  `pixel_values` path twice to prove determinism (else mark non-deterministic and report). Covers C3, G-EQ4.
- **G-SY1 push equals TRL's (G-EQ5)** [s1: SY7; s2: T94]. Merged presets: after one `push_weights` every vLLM parameter equals the state
  after TRL's per-parameter push of the same adapter state (per-tensor SHA-256 of the int16 view, hashed on the host one
  tensor at a time; `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated` rises by less than 100 MB during the check): awake with 3 pushes on 3 perturbed states, sleep after a
  sleep/wake cycle; includes fused `qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj` and the tied embedding; temperature-0 generation of 16 prompts
  gives equal token ids in both arms. Under F (`lora-seqmask`, C5 step 5(c)): after the first sync and after one sleep/wake
  cycle with a second sync (mode B), or after 3 syncs (mode A), each packed `lora_a` slice `torch.equal` `A.to(bf16)` and each
  `lora_b` slice `torch.equal` `2 * B.to(bf16)` (q/k/v -> `qkv_proj` 0/1/2, gate/up -> `gate_up_proj` 0/1); in mode B each
  base tensor hashes equal to `p.data`; the vLLM adapter load count is 1 per sync. Covers C5, G-EQ5.
- **G-SY2 push speed** [s1: SY8; s2: T141]. `PushStats.seconds <= 0.2` (median of 20 pushes); awake: no `time/wake_*` or sleep keys;
  sleep: `time/sync_s <= PushStats.seconds + baseline wake_weights_s + 0.1`; the one-call full push is timed against the
  per-parameter loop and a 196-tensor push (5 repeats, `c_speed_check --sync`) and the >= 50 ms delta re-add rule is evaluated. Covers C5, G-SP2.
- **G-SY3 no leak** [s2: T95]. 50 pushes: `memory_allocated` within 1 MB of the first; `seconds` stable. Covers C5, G-MEM.
- **G-MS1 `count_syncs` exact** [s1: MS2; s2: T111]. 1,000 `.item()` calls on one line count 1,000 (not 1); `.cpu()`
  1, `tolist()` 1, `torch.cuda.synchronize()` pinned, an async kernel 0; modes `default` and `error` restored, also after an
  exception; the user's `warnings.simplefilter("ignore")` and the filter list are restored/not suppressing; nested blocks
  count independently (an outer block also counts the inner block's syncs). Validation against nsys `cuda_api_trace` per

  thread only) for one update range is written to `c0_summary.json`. Covers C0 step 1, G-SP4.

  (`torch.cuda._sleep`): the indices on the device equal the numpy plans of both chunks. Covers C1 step 1, C4 step 4.

- **G-DT1 determinism** [s2: T129]. 10 repeats of `patchify`, `rope_positions`, `window_from_meta` give identical bytes; another

### C.9.5 End-to-end and performance gates (box, `gpu` + `slow`)

Protocol: same host and seed, R5 settings, the numerics preset of C.6, the B1 rows root, 17 steps read (`--steps 20`, C0 files), means over steps 3-15, nsys on steps
16-17. The speed reference is the same-rental baseline arm; R5's 23.43 s is only the "host comparable" check.

- **E-EQ6 step-1 identity (G-EQ6)** [s1: C-E1; s2: T121]. Fast arm vs baseline arm step 1: `rewards/iou_tc/mean`,
  `rewards/legal/mean`, `completions/mean_length` exactly equal; `grad_norm` and `sampling/sampling_logp_difference/mean` equal
  to 4 significant digits (round both with `float(f"{x:.4g}")` then `math.isclose(rel_tol=5e-4)`; if the values straddle a
  rollover like 0.99995 vs 1.0000 fall back to `rel_tol=1e-3`; a `.3e` string compare is NOT 4 s.f.). Reference: IoU_tc 0.5467,
  legal 0.8984, length 117.89, grad norm 0.003264, logp diff 0.009515. V2 (front 6.3 item 3) runs one baseline arm and one
  fast arm, so a step-1 mismatch is a G-EQ6 fail: Gate C-adopt fails, C is not adopted, and the fast arm's
  `--expect-step1` check (C0 files) exits after step 1, so front 6.3's stop rule acts inside the plan. Optional, not in V2 (each is priced in front 6.3 only if the owner adds it): a second baseline arm as a
  control (a self-mismatch is reported as "baseline noise") and a bisect by flag (each of C1-C5 alone). If G-EN0
  showed different encode bits (`bits_equal` false in `{rd}/c_check/encoder.json`), `grad_norm` and the logp
  difference use relative difference <= 1e-3; the three reward
  numbers stay exact. Covers C1-C5, G-EQ6.
- **E-SP1 step time (G-SP1)** [s1: C-E2; s2: T140]. Relative rule: pass if `fast_mean <= base_mean - margin`, with the
  margin literals of C.6 (merged: 3.4 s A, 2.7 s B; F: 2.7 s A, 2.1 s B). Anything above is "not adopted"; above
  `base_mean - 2.25 / 1.55 s` (merged) or `- 1.5 / 1.25 s` (F) the report also says "re-profile". The margins are
  literals fixed before the rental; the recompute from the measured push is printed beside them and never replaces
  them (assert the gate uses the literals and the same-rental `base_mean`, never 23.43). Report both means, their ratio
  and "host not comparable to R5" when `base_mean` is outside 23.43 s ± 10 %. Report the per-arm median and SD of steps
  3-15 and the Welch 95 % interval of `base_mean - fast_mean` as report lines; they never change the G-SP1 result, and no
  arm is rerun. Reference: R5 SD over steps 3-15 is 1.89 s (base arm) and 2.11 s (shared arm) [measured:
  runs/r5/base_rl.json, runs/r5/shared_rl.json `step_time`]; with 13 steps per arm the SE of the difference is about
  0.79 s, so the 3.4 s margin is about 4 SE [estimate: sqrt(1.89^2/13 + 2.11^2/13)]. A Mac unit test (U-SP1) feeds a fake baseline of 25.0 s: a
  fast arm of 21.5 s passes in mode A (the old absolute 20.0 s rule would fail it), 21.7 s fails; with a baseline of
  21.0 s, a fast arm of 19.9 s fails (the old rule would pass it). Covers C1-C5, G-SP1.
- **E-SP3 prepare range (G-SP3)** [s1: C-E3; s2: T142]. NVTX `prepare` at most 0.5 s per step. Own test id per gate so a failure does not mask others. Covers C1, C2, C4, G-SP3.
- **E-SP4 host syncs (G-SP4, report only)** [s1: C-E3; s2: T143]. Target from the adopted set (C.6): below 200 if C4 step 6
  and C4b are adopted, else at most 25 % of the baseline count with TRL's metric reads and the DeepStack indexing removed
  from both counts and reported apart; assert baseline count > 0. Optional, not in V2 (priced in front 6.3 only if the
  owner adds it): a B = 128 arm to show the count does not scale per row (B = 128 vs 256 within 10 %). A miss is reported, not a failure of Gate C-adopt. Covers C0, C1, C2, C4, G-SP4.
- **E-SP5 H2D bytes (G-SP5)** [s1: C-E3; s2: T144]. Trainer-side H2D below 50 MB per step; vLLM's own H2D reported, not gated. Covers C1, C3, G-SP5.
- **E-SP6 GPU-active share (G-SP6)** [s1: C-E3; s2: T145]. At least 70 % over steps 16-17 via `gpu_active.py`; the same script on
  a deliberately idle trace (1 s sleeps between kernels) gives under 30 %. Covers C0, C1-C5, G-SP6.
- **E-MEM peak memory (G-MEM)** [s1: C-E3; s2: T146]. `max_memory_allocated` and `nvidia-smi` peak at most 30 GB on every V2 arm;
  drift under 100 MB across steps 3-15. Optional, not in V2 (priced in front 6.3 only if the owner adds it): a run with
  all 256 answers forced to 1,536 tokens. Covers C3, C5, C9, G-MEM.
- **E-REP repeatability** [s1: C-E4]. Optional, not in V2 (a second fast arm; priced in front 6.3 only if the owner adds
  it). The fast arm twice with the same seed: step times within 5 %, step-1 numbers identical; report the spread. A
  report line only: it covers no gate, and G-EQ6 and G-SP1 never wait for it.
- **E-ST1 `n=8` statistics (G-ST1)** [s1: C-GR5; s2: T147]. Reward, legal, IoU_tc within 2 baseline standard deviations
  (SD from steps 3-15, at least 10 samples, fail closed on SD 0), mean length within 5 %, at least 0.2 s per step saved; report
  effect sizes. Covers C6, G-ST1.
- **E-GC combined gate (new)**. With C7 and C8 added (in the first run after Gate B3): mean step at most 18.0 s; logs
  `completions/clipped_ratio` and the share of answers in (L, 1,536]. Covers C7, C8, G-C.
- **E-C9 arms (new)**. Optional, not in V2 or V3 (no rental row, front 6.3; C9). Each of the C9 arms (k = 4, 8 layers; 32 x 8) reads 17 steps (`--steps 20` on the rows root, C0 files); adopted only if step time falls by at least
  0.5 s and peak memory stays at most 30 GB; the log shows both numbers. Covers C9.
- **E-RC2 runaway-cut arm (G-RC2, rev 3)**. Inside a B run, 17 steps with `--runaway-cap` vs without: tail seconds fall by
  at least 50 %; reward, legal, IoU_tc within the G-ST1 spread; `completions/capped_share` logged. Covers C11, G-RC2.

### C.9.6 Pytest sketches (the most important tests)

Ranking rule: (1) breaks numbers silently, (2) breaks the C1-C5 equality contract, (3) hard to see in a normal run. Order:
rope no-false-good fuzz, patchify equality (hostile, random sizes, constants), encoder-once equality and alignment, meta equals
device, ImageMemo contract, `gpu_active` (the tool that measures G-SP6). The set-1 rope sketch (random batches) is folded into
the stronger fuzz below.

```python
# tests/test_gpu_pixels.py  (U-PX2, U-PX6, P-PX1, U-PX4, U-PX8)
import numpy as np, PIL.Image, pytest
torch = pytest.importorskip("torch")
from transformers import Qwen2VLImageProcessor
from objdel.train import gpu_pixels

def ip(**kw):
    return Qwen2VLImageProcessor(**{**dict(patch_size=16, temporal_patch_size=2, merge_size=2), **kw})

def hostile():
    ramp = (np.arange(512 * 512 * 3) % 256).astype(np.uint8).reshape(512, 512, 3)
    check = np.indices((512, 512)).sum(0) % 2 * 255
    return [np.zeros((512, 512, 3), np.uint8), np.full((512, 512, 3), 255, np.uint8),
            np.repeat(check[..., None], 3, 2).astype(np.uint8),
            np.where(np.indices((512, 512)).sum(0)[..., None] % 2, 127, 128).astype(np.uint8).repeat(3, 2),
            ramp, np.roll(ramp, 1, axis=2)]

@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["hf", "torch"])
def test_patchify_is_bit_equal_on_hostile_pixels(backend):
    proc, imgs = ip(), [PIL.Image.fromarray(a) for a in hostile()]
    want = proc(imgs, return_tensors="pt")
    pv, grid = gpu_pixels.patchify(imgs, proc, device="cpu", backend=backend)
    assert pv.dtype == torch.float32 and pv.shape == (len(imgs) * 1024, 1536)
    assert grid.dtype == torch.int64 and grid.device.type == "cpu"
    assert torch.equal(grid, want["image_grid_thw"]) and torch.equal(pv, want["pixel_values"])

@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["hf", "torch"])
def test_patchify_is_bit_equal_for_random_valid_sizes(backend):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    proc = ip()
    for case in range(200):
        n = int(rng.integers(1, 6))
        imgs = [PIL.Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 256, (int(h), int(w), 3), dtype=np.uint8))
                for h, w in zip(32 * rng.integers(1, 9, n), 32 * rng.integers(1, 9, n))]
        want = proc(imgs, return_tensors="pt")
        pv, grid = gpu_pixels.patchify(imgs, proc, device="cpu", backend=backend)
        assert torch.equal(pv, want["pixel_values"]), (case, backend)
        assert torch.equal(grid, want["image_grid_thw"]) and grid.device.type == "cpu"

def test_constants_come_from_the_processor_and_unchecked_settings_raise():
    proc = ip(); proc.image_mean, proc.image_std = [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], [0.5, 0.4, 0.3]
    img = PIL.Image.fromarray(np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 256, (512, 512, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
    pv, _ = gpu_pixels.patchify([img], proc, device="cpu", backend="torch")
    assert torch.equal(pv, proc([img], return_tensors="pt")["pixel_values"])
    for bad in (dict(patch_size=14), dict(merge_size=1), dict(temporal_patch_size=1)):
        with pytest.raises(gpu_pixels.UnsupportedImage):
            gpu_pixels.patchify([img], ip(**bad), device="cpu", backend="torch")

def test_rejects_unreadable_or_resized_inputs_and_bad_backend_is_not_a_fallback_signal():
    for b in (PIL.Image.new("RGB", (500, 500)), PIL.Image.new("RGBA", (64, 64)), PIL.Image.new("P", (64, 64))):
        with pytest.raises(gpu_pixels.UnsupportedImage):
            gpu_pixels.patchify([b], ip(), device="cpu")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as e:
        gpu_pixels.patchify([PIL.Image.new("RGB", (64, 64))], ip(), backend="nope")
    assert not isinstance(e.value, gpu_pixels.UnsupportedImage)   # must not trigger ImageMemo's fallback
```

```python
# tests/test_rope_positions.py  (P-RP2, U-RP2)
import numpy as np, pytest
torch = pytest.importorskip("torch")
from objdel.train import fast
from tests.test_train_fast import tiny_model, IMG, START, END

def make_prompt(n_img_tokens=16, text=(5, 6, 7)):
    return [START] + [IMG] * n_img_tokens + [END] + list(text), [0] + [1] * n_img_tokens + [0] * (1 + len(text))

def hf_positions(base, ids, mask, types, grid):
    return base.get_rope_index(input_ids=ids, image_grid_thw=grid, attention_mask=mask, mm_token_type_ids=types)[0]

def test_rope_never_calls_a_mutated_row_good_unless_it_equals_hf():
    base = tiny_model().model
    p_ids, p_types = make_prompt()
    grid = torch.tensor([[1, 8, 8]])
    tmpl = fast.rope_template(base, torch.tensor([p_ids]), torch.tensor([p_types]), grid)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0); flagged = 0
    for case in range(500):
        B, W = 4, 80
        ids, mask, types = (torch.zeros(B, W, dtype=torch.long) for _ in range(3))
        for i in range(B):
            pad, ans = int(rng.integers(0, 20)), int(rng.integers(0, 30))
            seq = list(p_ids) + [int(x) for x in rng.integers(0, 90, ans)]; ty = list(p_types) + [0] * ans
            ids[i, pad:pad + len(seq)] = torch.tensor(seq); types[i, pad:pad + len(seq)] = torch.tensor(ty)
            mask[i, pad:pad + len(seq)] = 1
            for _ in range(int(rng.integers(0, 3))):                      # mutations
                j, kind = int(rng.integers(0, W)), int(rng.integers(0, 3))
                if kind == 0: ids[i, j] = int(rng.integers(0, 90))
                elif kind == 1: types[i, j] ^= 1
                else: mask[i, j] ^= 1
        pos, bad = fast.rope_positions(tmpl, ids, mask, types)
        flagged += int(bad.sum())
        assert pos.dtype == torch.int64 and bad.dtype == torch.bool
        for i in range(B):
            if not bad[i]:
                assert torch.equal(pos[:, i:i+1], hf_positions(base, ids[i:i+1], mask[i:i+1], types[i:i+1], grid)), (case, i)
    assert flagged > 25                                                   # the fuzz has teeth
```

def test_image_ids_follow_rows_through_shuffle_order_and_split():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1); G, K = 8, 32
    for case in range(100):
        base_ids = np.repeat(np.arange(K), G)
        if case % 3 == 0: base_ids[G:2 * G] = base_ids[:G]    # two groups share one image object
        meta = fast.RowMeta(rng.integers(10, 40, K * G).astype(np.int32), rng.integers(0, 200, K * G).astype(np.int32),
                            base_ids.astype(np.int32), (np.arange(K * G) // G).astype(np.int32))
        for order in (rng.permutation(K * G), fast.length_order(meta), fast.group_order(meta, G)):
            ids = base_ids[order]
            for chunk in (8, 16, 4):
                for s in range(0, K * G, chunk):
                    assert np.array_equal(ids[s:s + chunk], base_ids[order[s:s + chunk]])
        go = fast.group_order(meta, G).reshape(K, G)
        assert (go // G == (go // G)[:, :1]).all()            # whole groups stay together
    # the real test (P-EN1 second half) runs the tiny model with unequal grids and compares per-row encoder rows
    # to standalone tower outputs with torch.equal

```python
# tests/test_row_meta_equals_device.py  (P-RM1, P-RM2)
import numpy as np, pytest
torch = pytest.importorskip("torch"); pytest.importorskip("trl")
from objdel.train import fast

def build(rng, B=16, L=64, P=24):
    plen, clen = rng.integers(4, P + 1, B), rng.integers(0, L + 1, B)
    am = torch.zeros(B, P + L, dtype=torch.long)
    for i in range(B):
        am[i, P - plen[i]:P] = 1; am[i, P:P + clen[i]] = 1
    return am, plen, clen

@pytest.mark.parametrize("buckets", [fast.BUCKETS, fast.FINE, (32, 64, 128)])
def test_window_and_orders_equal_the_device_versions(buckets):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2); L = 64
    for case in range(500):
        am, plen, clen = build(rng)
        meta = fast.row_meta([[1] * int(p) for p in plen], [[2] * int(c) for c in clen],
                             np.repeat([0, 1], 8), 8, mask_truncated=False, max_completion_length=L)
        for rows in (slice(0, 8), slice(8, 16), slice(0, 16), [3, 9, 12]):
            r = np.arange(16)[rows] if isinstance(rows, slice) else np.array(rows)
            assert fast.window_from_meta(meta, r, L, buckets) == fast.window(am[r], L, buckets), case
        n = am.sum(1)
        assert np.array_equal(fast.length_order(meta), torch.sort(n, descending=True, stable=True).indices.numpy())
        batch = {"prompt_mask": am[:, :24], "completion_mask": am[:, 24:], "x": torch.arange(16)}
        assert np.array_equal(fast.group_order(meta, 8), fast.by_group_length(batch, 8)["x"].numpy())
```

# tests/test_image_memo.py additions  (U-IM2, U-IM3, U-IM5)
def test_per_image_order_counters_and_fallback(counted):
    ip, seen = counted
    a, b, c = image(0), image(1), image(2, 96, 64)
    memo = fast.ImageMemo(ip); memo.per_image = True
    rows = [b, a, b, c, a, a, c, b]
    got = memo(rows, return_tensors="pt")
    plain = Qwen2VLImageProcessor(patch_size=16, temporal_patch_size=2, merge_size=2)
    assert torch.equal(got["pixel_values"], plain([b, a, c], return_tensors="pt")["pixel_values"])
    assert torch.equal(got["image_grid_thw"], plain(rows, return_tensors="pt")["image_grid_thw"])
    assert (memo.misses, memo.hits) == (3, 5)
    memo.clear(); big = [image(i) for i in range(32)]; d0 = (memo.misses, memo.hits)
    memo.per_image = False; memo(sum(([x] * 8 for x in big), []), return_tensors="pt")
    assert (memo.misses - d0[0], memo.hits - d0[1]) == (32, 224)
    bad = PIL.Image.fromarray(np.zeros((500, 500, 3), np.uint8))          # UnsupportedImage -> wrapped processor
    mixed = [a, bad, a]
    assert torch.equal(fast.ImageMemo(ip)(mixed, return_tensors="pt")["pixel_values"],
                       plain(mixed, return_tensors="pt")["pixel_values"])

```python
# tests/test_gpu_active.py  (U-GA1, U-GA2, P-GA1; experiments/phase2/gpu_active.py)
import json, pytest
from experiments.phase2 import gpu_active

INTERVALS = [(0, 40), (30, 60), (50, 80), (90, 100), (100, 110)]          # ns; 2 streams, one memcpy
def brute(iv, lo, hi):
    on = [False] * (hi - lo)
    for s, e in iv:
        for t in range(max(s, lo), min(e, hi)): on[t - lo] = True
    return sum(on) / (hi - lo)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("rng_", [(0, 200), (10, 50), (85, 95), (150, 200), (0, 110)])
def test_union_share_is_exact_and_csv_equals_json(tmp_path, rng_):
    lo, hi = rng_
    csv = tmp_path / "t.csv"; csv.write_text("Start (ns),Duration (ns),Name\n" + "".join(f"{s},{e - s},k\n" for s, e in INTERVALS))
    js = tmp_path / "t.json"; js.write_text(json.dumps({"traceEvents": [
        {"ph": "X", "cat": "kernel", "ts": s / 1000, "dur": (e - s) / 1000, "name": "k", "pid": 0, "tid": i % 2}
        for i, (s, e) in enumerate(INTERVALS)] + [{"ph": "X", "cat": "cpu_op", "ts": 0, "dur": 500, "name": "cpu"}]}))
    want = brute(INTERVALS, lo, hi)
    assert gpu_active.share(csv, lo, hi) == pytest.approx(want, abs=1e-12)
    assert gpu_active.share(js, lo, hi) == pytest.approx(want, abs=1e-12)
```

`gpu_active.share(path, lo, hi)` is an assumed name; the spec fixes only the module path and behaviour (adapt the call).
Helpers `tiny_model`, `make_batch`, `Plain_logps`, `Fast_logps_encoder_once`, `trainer`, `visual_calls`, `image`, `counted` come from
or extend `tests/test_train_fast.py` and `tests/test_image_memo.py`.

### C.9.9 Spec rules for the questions found while writing the tests (rev 3: one rule each; tests assert only that rule)

Revision 2 listed these as open questions, and some tests accepted either outcome. Such a test cannot fail (QA review
item 10). Each item now has one rule. The owner may change a rule; the default is written here.

1. C1 input forms. A 3-D uint8 tensor is always a grey batch `(N, H, W)`. One RGB image is passed as `(1, H, W, 3)`, as a
   numpy `(H, W, 3)` array in a list, or as a PIL image. Float, int64 and uint16 inputs raise `UnsupportedImage` (never
   cast). An empty list or `(0, H, W, 3)` raises `ValueError` (U-PX4, U-PX5, U-PX9).
2. C2 template choice. The template key includes the grid, and `RopeCache.positions` looks up each row by its own
   (prompt ids, grid) from `RowMeta`. So a row never meets another grid's template. `bad` is not meant to detect a wrong
   grid. U-RP2 asserts the lookup (a strict test, not an xfail); `--check-rope-every` stays as the run-time guard.
3. C4 truncation. `row_meta` takes `eos_and_pad_ids`; truncated = last completion id not in that list (TRL's rule,
   grpo_trainer.py:2604-2606). An empty completion raises `ValueError` (U-RM2).
4. C6 blocks. `group_requests` cuts by position into blocks of G; each block must be uniform; equal neighbouring blocks
   are allowed (16 identical rows with G = 8 give 2 requests) (U-GR1).
5. C0 counter keys. `perf/host_syncs/<phase>` and `perf/host_syncs_vllm`. Nested blocks: each block counts its own
   syncs, and an outer block includes its inner blocks. An explicit `torch.cuda.synchronize()` counts as whatever torch
   reports on the box stack; G-MS1 records that value once and pins it (U-MS1, G-MS1).
6. Errors. `UnsupportedImage` subclasses `ValueError`. An unknown backend raises a plain `ValueError`. ImageMemo
   catches only `UnsupportedImage` (U-PX8, U-IM5).
7. C4 lengths. TRL zeroes `completion_mask` for truncated rows when `mask_truncated_completions` is on
   [code: grpo_trainer.py:2608], so `completion_len` (0 for those rows) equals the device mask sum. P-RM2 asserts
   equality with no fallback.
8. C1 threads and counters. ImageMemo is called only from the trainer's main thread; it stores the owner thread id and
   raises `RuntimeError` from any other thread (the reward prefetch thread never calls it). `clear()` empties the memo
   and does not reset `hits`/`misses`; tests assert deltas (U-IM3, U-IM8).
9. G-EQ6 "4 significant digits": the rounding rule of E-EQ6, plus the relative 1e-3 rule when G-EN0 shows different
   encode bits.
10. A7 list. The A7 start-up check covers exactly the four names of C.4 (`_tokenize_prompts`, `_compute_loss`,
    `VLLMGeneration.sync_weights`, and vLLM's `LLMEngine.add_lora`, checked only when the preset is `lora-seqmask`);
    U-LM1 tests those four. C11 adds no private name (it wraps the existing `llm.generate` patch).
11. `--record-batches DIR` on an existing non-empty directory raises `FileExistsError`; nothing is written (U-CF2).
12. C2 routing. The host (`rope_bad_rows`) decides which rows take HF `get_rope_index`. The device `bad` is read only
    on check steps; a row bad on the device but good on the host raises there (U-RP7, U-RP6).
13. C11 masking. `--runaway-cap > 0` requires `mask_truncated_completions=False`; start-up raises otherwise (U-RC5).

## D.1. Goal and why

**Goal.** The owner rule says the checker, the scorer and the polygonizer use CUDA. Phase D makes that true in
production. It makes the polygonizer work-optimal, it moves the checker's topology layer (labels, size filter,
signatures) and the evaluation pixel work to the GPU, and it builds expert tables on the device. The CPU build of the
same source stays the oracle and the Mac path.

Evidence:

1. The production polygonizer is numpy, not CUDA. `targets/build.py:93` calls `checker.polygonize`, and
   `checker/certify.py:46` does too. `_gpucheck.check_masks` has no production caller; only tests and
   `experiments/cuda_checker/compare.py:76` call it [code: grep, verified 2026-11-08].
2. The CUDA polygonizer does dense work. `check_mask_chunk` sweeps all S = 4(W+1)(H+1) slots in each of 2·L rounds,
   with L = ceil(log2 S) + 1 [code: cuda/gpucheck.cpp:931-937, 966-1057]. CPU-build time follows S, not the edge
   count: 15.3 ms for E = 100 and 15.1 ms for E = 804 on a 512x512 mask [measured: docs/implementation2.0/notes/D1.md §1.3].
   The work ratio is 48x (24x24 crop) to 28,949x (512x512, E = 100) [note-D1 §1.3, arithmetic].
3. K1-draft is ready and exact. It matches numpy `polygonize`, `bitquads` and `check_masks` on all 37,093 LIDC crops:
   38,002 rings, 1,476,508 corners, 0 mismatches. It also passes 4,453 random/adversarial masks in 15 configurations
   and 3 item orders [measured: docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K1/results/cross_numpy_m3.txt, test_cpu_m3.txt]. CPU-build speed
   against `check_masks`: x95.5 on lesion512 b256 and x22.2 on the real LIDC crops [measured: K1/results/bench_cpu_m3.txt].
   nvcc 13.0.88 builds it for sm_120 [measured: K1/results/nvcc_docker_sm120.log]. It has not run on a GPU yet.
4. The checker's topology layer is cv2 in production. `topology._label` is `cv2.connectedComponentsWithAlgorithm`
   (Spaghetti) [code: checker/topology.py:75-77]. Production callers: `targets/build.py:151-155, 208`,
   `reward/cache.py:230`, `checker/certify.py:43-45`, `eval/probes.py:154, 308, 316, 571`,
   `experiments/phase2/build_views.py:57` [code: grep, verified 2026-11-08].
5. Evaluation reads pixels on the host. `eval/metrics.py` `_samples` calls `to_masks`, which unpacks the masks to numpy
   [code: metrics.py:249-271, geometry/shape.py:136-160]. Then `_pairwise_iou` (numpy matmul, :172), `_surface`
   (scipy EDT, :199), `soft_dice` (:160) and `hm_iou` (:189) run on the CPU. The 2,200-item test eval took 634 s wall,
   generation included [measured: REPO/runs/r5/eval_test.log]. The CPU share is not measured.
6. Expert caches are not offline. `ExpertCache.__init__` runs `_band` (2 scipy EDTs), k cv2 signatures, `boundary`
   (cv2.erode) and `cv2.boundingRect` on every construction, and `load` constructs from the npz, which stores only the
   raters, tau and T5 [code: reward/cache.py:222-238, 276-293]. Cost: 1.0 / 3.6 / 7.5 ms per load at 128 / 256 /
   400 px [measured: docs/implementation2.0/notes/D1.md C6, 4 raters].
7. K2-draft has exact device versions of EDT, set intersections and warp-per-shape validity totals. Digests match on
   macOS clang and Linux g++: scale 1 `b158d8132b18be83`, scale 4 `f92b9a3939cec10f` [measured:
   docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K2/build/run_cpu_mac.txt]. A one-thread-per-shape straggler (adversarial 10 rings x 1,000 vertices)
   drops from 310 ms to 39 ms of device time on the CPU build [measured: same file].
8. The scorer labels 4 times per call (fg, bg, fg, bg), even when the size filter changes nothing
   [code: gpucheck.cpp:1612-1615]. The host oracle skips that case [code: checker/topology.py:161].
9. Phase D is NOT an RL speed item. Reward scoring takes a mean 0.0046 s (median 0.0045, range 0.0039-0.0054 s, 15
   steps) of a 23.4 s step [measured: REPO/runs/r5/base/rl.json `time/rewards_s`]. The value is the owner rule, the 3D
   direction (dense slots cannot scale to 512x512x100 volumes: note-D1 §1.8 [estimate]), offline throughput, and fewer CPU
   dependencies. BUT Phase D code does run in the RL process. The reward path calls `add_tables`, `drop_tables` and the
   grow-only arenas, which call `cudaMalloc`/`cudaFree` [code: gpucheck.cpp:78-84, 135-150, 1741-1748, 1774].
   So D5c and D7b carry memory and time gates (D-G14, D-G15) next to vLLM and the trainer on one 32 GB card.
   `metrics()` does not run inside RL: live runs attach no audit callback [code: experiments/phase2/g_probe.py:93].
10. Only rented boxes run the GPU tests. GitHub-hosted GPU runners are T4 (sm_75) only [web: note-D2 F17]. `cuda/docker_check.sh`
    compiles sm_80/86/89/90/120 but never runs them [code: cuda/docker_check.sh:5-20]. Today it fails before the build:
    its `cp -r --parents` list names a `cpp` folder [code: cuda/docker_check.sh:17], and the repo has no `cpp` folder
    [measured: `ls cpp`, 2026-11-08]. D1 removes it from the list.

## D.2. Research basis (one line each)

- Playne and Hawick, lock-free min-root union-find for GPU CCL, IEEE TPDS 29(6) 2018. This is the `unite` already in gpucheck.cpp:1270 and in K1-draft.
- Allegretti, Bolelli, Grana, block-based GPU CCL (BKE, BUF), IEEE TPDS 31(2) 2020. The fallback if run-based union-find depth hurts.
- Bolelli et al., "CCL on GPUs: a state-of-the-art review with code", IEEE TPDS 2024. Block-based is fastest overall; run-based is weakest on vertical shapes. This is risk D-R2.
- Hennequin, Lacassagne et al., HA4 run-based labeling with warp ballots, DASIP 2018. Runs in bit words, as in K1-draft.
- Lemaitre, Maurice, Lacassagne, FLSL with holes, 2022. Fg/bg runs plus an adjacency tree: the prior art for K1-draft's surround rule.
- Kong and Rosenfeld, digital topology survey, CVGIP 48(3) 1989. The (8,4) pairing: one border per adjacent component pair (K1-draft lemma 1).
- Suzuki and Abe, border following, CVGIP 30(1) 1985. The classic contour order.
- Muñoz-Salinas et al., TRUCO [paper: arXiv 2610.37297]. Lock-free contour extraction with Suzuki-Abe output, multi-core CPU. An idea source only, not a GPU design.
- Yin et al., G-Contour, ICCAD 2025. Union-find, then start points, then per-contour tracing: the same macro-structure as K1-draft.
- Felzenszwalb and Huttenlocher, distance transforms of sampled functions, ToC 8:415 2012; Meijster et al. 2000. The integer separable EDT of K2-draft.
- Manduhu and Jones, work-efficient exact EDT with ballot/clz, IEEE TIP 2019. K2-draft's row pass.
- Cao et al., PBA+ (cuCIM `distance_transform_edt`). Not adopted for production. Ties change only the returned indices, and `float64_distances=True` matches SciPy [web: docs.nvidia.com/cucim/latest/api/], so exactness is not the reason. The reasons: the Mac has no CUDA, so the one-source CPU build needs our own EDT as the oracle and the Mac path; and cuCIM plus CuPy is a large new dependency for one kernel. Optional: cuCIM `distance_transform_edt(float64_distances=True)` as a second oracle in one box-only test of the K2-draft EDT (D7). Trigger to revisit: EDT time > 10 % of eval wall time in the D1 stage events. Front section 4 states the same decision.
- Kohl et al., Probabilistic U-Net [paper: arXiv 1806.05034] (GED); HPU-Net [paper: arXiv 1905.13077] and CAR [paper: arXiv 2006.13144] (HM-IoU).
- Nikolov et al. surface Dice (NSD), as google-deepmind/surface-distance. This is the metrics.py definition [code: metrics.py docstring].
- Tools: CUB `DeviceScan::ExclusiveSum` (CCCL in CUDA 13.0.3), NVTX3 (`cuda-toolkit[nvtx]`, nvidia-nvtx 13.0.85 [web: pypi.org/project/cuda-toolkit/13.0.3]), compute-sanitizer (memcheck, initcheck, synccheck, racecheck; racecheck covers shared memory only [web: docs.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer]), the CUDA stream-ordered allocator (`cudaMemPoolCreate`, `cudaMallocFromPoolAsync`, `cudaFreeAsync` [web: CUDA programming guide §4.3; CUDA runtime API, memory pools]).
- Libraries checked and NOT adopted for production: OpenCV CUDA CCL (8-way only, one image per call), CuPy and cuCIM `label` (one image per call, label order not documented), NPP UF (past wrong-result bugs), CV-CUDA label (connectivity pairing unclear) [web: note-D1 §5, note-D2 F2-F4]. No library traces exact crack-edge rings on the GPU [note-D2 F16, note-CL2 §3].

## D.3. Design

### D.3.1 Box diagram (after Phase D)

```
 host (Mac CPU build or box)                       device (RTX 5090, sm_120; same source as the CPU build)
 +---------------------------+   pinned H2D   +-----------------------------------------------------------+
 | targets/build.py           |-------------->| Pack (ballot) -> bit words                                |
 |  masks (store, host numpy) |   bytes       |   |-> Quads (bit-slice) ------------------> n1 n2 nD n3 n4 |
 | checker/certify.py         |               |   |-> RunCount -> scan -> RunEmit (fg runs, bg runs)       |
 | checker/topology.py        |               |   |      -> Merge (fg 8 / bg 4 union-find) -> Flatten      |
 | data/riga.py (Mac only)    |               |   |      -> HoleKey, RingMark, popc rank  ---> ring_part   |
 +---------------------------+               |   |-> RingInit -> Seeds -> Trace1 -> RingWalk -> scan     |
        ^  rings, quads, ring_part,           |   |      -> Trace2 -> corners, ring areas  (K1-draft)        |
        |  topology (areas, holes)            |   |-> PIXEL label chain (LabelInit/Merge/Flatten, Count,   |
        +-------------------------------------|   |      Filter, Holes) --> topology, b0/b1 (certify leg)  |
                                               |                                                            |
 +---------------------------+   polygons     | raster (warp/row) -> words -> validity: EdgePairs +       |
 | reward.score_many (RL)     |-------------->|   ShapeTotalsWarp (K2-draft, warp per shape) -> defects      |
 | eval/metrics.py (eval)     |   ints        |   words + resident tables -> scorer: labels (skip 2nd pair  |
 | reward/cache.py (tables)   |   raters      |   if no filter change) -> ScoreRows/ObjTerms -> terms      |
 +---------------------------+               |   raters -> TableBuild: union, core, vote, EDT map,        |
        ^  per-object terms (floats)          |   perimeter, rater sigs -> resident tables (pool memory)   |
        |  integer matrices (eval)            |   words + tables -> eval_sets: SetInter (M x M), raw K x K,|
        +-------------------------------------|   soft-Dice counts, corner border -> EDT -> NSD counts     |
                                               +-----------------------------------------------------------+
 host floats from integers: IoU, GED, HM-IoU (8 x 4 assignment), NSD, soft Dice, boundary F
```

Two labellers stay on purpose. K1-draft's run CCL feeds the polygonizer (rings, `ring_part`). The scorer's pixel
union-find feeds the topology layer and the certificate's b0/b1 leg. They are different algorithms on different inputs
(runs vs bytes), so the certificate keeps an independent check (D3).

### D.3.2 Data flow

1. Targets (offline, on the Mac CPU build, $0): store masks -> `rings.trace([crop], [offset])` -> rings plus
   `ring_part` -> `_parts` -> per name, all remaining ladder rungs in one `certify_polygons` call (device: rasterize,
   legality, IoU counts, equality, size-filtered signature) -> first passing rung -> RIGA rim check by a pair query in
   a second call -> text -> `target_set_hash`. RIGA data never leaves the Mac (run_box.sh refuses it
   [code: experiments/cuda_checker/run_box.sh]).
2. RL reward (box): unchanged API. `score_many` -> `score_polygons`. Inside: the new validity totals and the label skip.
   Table uploads and arenas come from a stream-ordered pool (D5c).
3. Eval (box, in the `final_eval` process): parse -> `score_many` (terms) plus `eval_sets` calls on the
   scorer lane, chunked so that scratch stays under a cap. Only integer matrices come back. Host formulas make the
   same floats as today.
4. Expert caches: built offline at prepare time with the device EDT (`cache.edt`, bit-identical to scipy, so the
   fingerprint stays). Loaded at run time from the npz. Construction is host-only and cheap (no EDT, no labeling, no
   engine call). The first `device()` call builds union, core, vote, the EDT map, the perimeter and the rater
   signatures ON the device in one call (D7b). This is NOT offline: it runs in the RL and eval processes.

### D.3.3 Where each step runs (GPU everywhere; every CPU item has a reason)

| Step | Runs on | Reason if CPU |
|---|---|---|
| Mask to rings (polygonizer), bit-quads, ring parts | GPU (box) / CPU build (Mac) | The Mac has no GPU. The CPU build is the same source and is the oracle. Target builds stay on the Mac: RIGA must not leave it, and they cost $0. |
| Topology layer: `instance_topology`, `betti`, `size_filter`, `signature` | GPU / CPU build (D4b) | Same as above. The cv2 versions move to `tests/oracles/topology_oracle.py`. |
| Ladder certify (raster, legal, IoU, equality, signature, rim pair) | GPU / CPU build | Same as above |
| Validity totals, raster, scorer, labels | GPU | - |
| Expert tables at load: union, core, vote, EDT map, perimeter, rater signatures | GPU (D7b) | - |
| Expert-cache EDT at build (`cache.edt`, also inside `f5_tolerance` leave-one-out bands) | GPU / CPU build | The build is offline (prepare time). The map returns to the host only for tau/T5. |
| Eval pixel work (intersections, raw sample intersections, soft-Dice counts, NSD EDT) | GPU | - |
| Eval floats (IoU, GED, HM-IoU, NSD, soft Dice) from integer matrices | CPU | The inputs are K x (K+k+1) integers (scores, not pixels). Host formulas keep today's values bit-identical. HM-IoU is an 8 x 4 assignment. |
| Bounding-box crop before trace, and the cache's union box (`cv2.boundingRect`) | CPU | The mask already sits on the host, and the crop cuts H2D bytes. It is a few microseconds [estimate]. |
| Text parse (regex, JSON), `pack_objects` | CPU | The text arrives on the host from vLLM. It sits inside the 5 ms reward time [measured: rl.json]. |
| Ring simplifier (`targets/simplify.py`, numba) | CPU | Out of D scope. It works on rings of at most 1,000 vertices [code: text.py:59] and runs offline on the Mac. Revisit after D (note-D1 C3). |
| Data readers, augment, `data/riga.py` ndimage ops | CPU | Offline data prep, not geometry scoring (note-D1 C10) |
| `checker/volume.py` `betti3d` (`scipy.ndimage.label`) [code: volume.py:56-57] | CPU | 3D is the next direction, not Phase D. Deferred to the voxel phase: the run CCL extends to z-runs with 26/6 connectivity there. |
| `eval/probes.py` ndimage label, dilation, EDT [code: probes.py:236-268] and `surface` (:476) | CPU | Offline report, not a gate or a reward. Optional D7c moves `surface` to K2-draft `Directed` + `Select`. |
| `_kept` interval loop for an unknown size rule | removed | Every production caller passes `min_area` [code: dataset.py:98, probes.py:157, build_views.py:80]. D4 makes it required. |

## D.4. Tasks

Order: D1's Mac parts (step 0 runbook paths, engine counters, NVTX, stage events, `bench_checker.py`), then
D2 -> D3 -> D4 -> D4b; D6 after D1; D5 after D2; D7b after D4b; D7 after D7b and Phase A's A5; D5c with D7b; D8 grows
with each task; D9 with each merge. D1's Mac parts gate D2. The R-D1 GPU numbers gate only speed claims (D-G7 and the
D5 step 4 rule). D2-D8 use the CPU build as the oracle, so they do not wait for R-D1. R-D1 runs only before D2
merges (D1 step 4 tree rule). If back decision 3 or that rule drops R-D1,
D-G1 and D-G2 are covered by D-G3 (the ported engine on the GPU) in R-D2, and the stage events come from R-D2's bench. Each merge keeps `make test` and `make lint` green, and
archives the old code in the same commit.

Common toolchain (all tasks): CUDA toolkit from PyPI `cuda-toolkit[nvcc,cccl,nvtx]==13.0.3` (nvcc 13.0.88, CCCL 13.0.85,
nvidia-nvtx 13.0.85) plus `nvidia-cuda-sanitizer-api==13.4.92`. Today `run_box.sh` installs `[nvcc,cccl]` and the
sanitizer [code: run_box.sh:24]; D1 adds `nvtx`. `cuda/docker_check.sh` runs `run_box.sh --build-only`
[code: docker_check.sh:19], so it picks up the same extra. C++17 for gpucheck [code: CMakeLists.txt:17]. Keep
`--fmad=false` and `-ffp-contract=off` [code: CMakeLists.txt:21-22]. Architectures: `native` on the box;
`CUDA_ARCHS="80;86;89;90;120"` for docker_check.

Engine counters (new in D1, used by D-G8, D-G14, D-G15): a process-wide `Stats` struct in `gpucheck.cpp`, outside the
`__CUDACC__` split, counts these events:
- `waits`: calls of `wait()`.
- `drain_syncs`: stream syncs made by `Drain`. Today `Drain` calls `cudaStreamSynchronize` on both lanes directly,
  not through `wait()` [code: gpucheck.cpp:177-184]. D1 routes it through a counted helper, so no host sync escapes
  the counters. Both lanes stay: `check_polygons` runs a batch of >= 64 shapes as two halves on lanes 0 and 1
  [code: gpucheck.cpp:1060, 1671-1692]. The scorer entries use lane 0 only, so `Drain` syncs an idle lane 1 there.
- `label_pairs`: crop rows that the scorer's second label pair relabels (D5 step 1, test I14). It is NOT a launch
  count. `label(which)` always enqueues its three kernels over all crop rows [code: gpucheck.cpp:1597-1601, 1614],
  and the D5 skip happens per row inside the kernel, so a launch count is the same whether the skip works or not.
  The device counts the rows into each object's `ObjOut`, and the host adds them to `label_pairs` after the
  existing wait (D5 step 1). No new wait or copy.
- Allocation calls, split by whether they synchronize. All engine memory goes through the `alloc`/`release`
  helpers [code: gpucheck.cpp:78-84; call sites :146 (`Block::get`), :1741, :1746 (`add_tables`), :1772
  (`drop_tables`)], so the counters sit inside those helpers and no call escapes them:
  - `sync_alloc` / `sync_free`: calls of `cudaMalloc` or `cudaMallocHost` / `cudaFree` or `cudaFreeHost`. These
    synchronize the device. After D5c the only path left that makes them is pinned staging (`Block<false>`) growth.
    Today every device path makes them too.
  - `pool_allocs` / `pool_frees`: calls of `cudaMallocFromPoolAsync` / `cudaFreeAsync` on the engine pool (D5c).
    They do not synchronize. They rise, with no defect, when a call is larger than every earlier call (the
    grow-only `Block<true>` arenas `dev` and `score` [code: gpucheck.cpp:131-154], plus `scan`, the CUB scratch
    arena that D2 step 1 adds) and when a new image's tables are
    uploaded or dropped [code: reward/cache.py:247-257]. They are recorded, never gated, outside the fixed-shape tests.
  - On the CPU build, device-kind calls count as `pool_allocs` / `pool_frees` and host-kind calls count as
    `sync_alloc` / `sync_free` (both use `operator new`/`delete`), so the Mac tests model the CUDA build after D5c.
  These four names replace `device_allocs`, `device_releases`, `host_allocs` and `host_releases` in the D.spec.md
  `stats()` list.
- `arena_bytes`: the sum of `cap` over every device arena (`Block<true>`: `dev`, `score` and, after D2 step 1,
  `scan`) of both lanes [code: gpucheck.cpp:135-156]. It counts the rounded-up `cap`, not the bytes asked for.
- `table_bytes`: the sum of the sizes of the live expert-table blocks in the registry (`add_tables`,
  `add_tables_many`, `add_tables_from_raters`; `drop_tables` subtracts). Today `resident()` returns only a count
  [code: gpucheck.cpp:1778], so this is a new counter.
- `eval_scratch_peak`: the largest scratch that one `eval_sets` chunk asked for (D7), in bytes before `Block::get`
  rounds up. 0 until the first `eval_sets` call.
- `live_device_bytes` (device bytes allocated and not yet released: arenas, tables, pool blocks). After D5c every
  device block is an arena or a table, so `live_device_bytes == arena_bytes + table_bytes` in a correct engine.
- `pinned_grows`: growths of a pinned staging block (`in`, `out`) after its one sizing to the lane bound, which the
  first engine call of the process does, whatever the entry (D5c). D-G15 reads it at the end of a run.
- `contexts`: 1 after the first engine call that opens a CUDA context in this process, else 0 (D-G17). The CPU build
  always reports 0.
- `pool_reserved` and `default_pool_reserved`: `cudaMemPoolAttrReservedMemCurrent` of the engine pool and of the
  device's default pool (D5c). The CPU build reports 0.

The CPU build counts the same calls, so the Mac tests check them. Binding: `gc.stats() -> dict`, `gc.reset_stats()`.
`reset_stats()` zeroes the event counters and `eval_scratch_peak`. It leaves the current-state values unchanged:
`arena_bytes`, `table_bytes`, `live_device_bytes`, `contexts`, `pool_reserved` and `default_pool_reserved`.
Today `score_polygons` makes 4 `wait()` calls (gpucheck.cpp:1802, then 1574, 1626, 1639 inside `score_words`) plus 2
`Drain` syncs [code: gpucheck.cpp:1784-1806, 1549-1641]. D-G8 uses the totals that D1 measures, not a literal.

1. Use gpucheck's `Lane` (lowest-priority non-blocking stream [code: gpucheck.cpp:66-71]) and its arenas in place of
   K1-draft's `Engine`. K1-draft's `Engine` holds three device blocks, `Block<true> devA, devB, tmp;`
   [code: K1/k1poly.cpp:162], and a `Lane` holds two, `Block<true> dev, score;` [code: gpucheck.cpp:154]. `tmp` is
   CUB's scan scratch [code: K1/k1poly.cpp:140-142], and `chunk` calls `scan(..., E.tmp)` six times while layouts A
   and B are live [code: K1/k1poly.cpp:824-825, 871-872, 876, 884]. So add a third device arena,
   `Block<true> scan;`, to `Lane` (CUB scratch only), and map K1-draft to the lane like this: `devA` -> `L.dev`,
   `devB` -> `L.score`, `tmp` -> `L.scan`, `in` -> `L.in`, `out` -> `L.out`. Never pass a block that holds live
   data to `scan`. Reason: `Block::get` returns the same base pointer when the capacity is enough
   [code: gpucheck.cpp:139], so `L.dev` or `L.score` as scratch makes CUB write over layout A or B on the GPU, and
   the CPU `scan` ignores the block (`(void)st, (void)tmp;` [code: K1/k1poly.cpp:144]), so no plain CPU test sees
   it (step 7 adds the poison build that does). Masks are processed in chunks of at most `chunk_pixels` pixels. A larger mask runs alone.
   Run-sized scratch above `max_scratch_bytes` halves the chunk, down to one mask [K1-draft k1poly.h:46-51].

3. `ring_part[r]` = the 0-based raster rank of the ring's foreground component: for an outer ring, its component;
   for a hole, S(B), the component left of the hole's first run (`bleft` [K1-draft DESIGN lemma 3]). An outer ring's
   order key is its component's first pixel [K1-draft lemma 4]. So `ring_part` of outer ring j is its rank among the
   outer rings, and a hole takes the rank of its S(B).
4. `betti[m] = (number of fg components, number of bounded bg components)`, counted from the Flatten roots. This
   comes from the SAME run CCL as the rings, so `certify` does not use it as its b0/b1 leg (D3).

   - Load guard: the child asserts `objdel._gpucheck.__file__` is under `build/variants/<name>/site` and

   - `tests/variants.py` holds `build(name, defs)`, `run(name, pytest_args) -> int` (the child above),

### D4. Ladder certify on the device

Maps to: note-D1 R4. It removes the per-rung `to_mask` host unpack and the cv2 signature from the target builder, for LIDC
and RIGA.

Files:
- change `cuda/gpucheck.cpp`, `gpucheck.h`, `gpucheck_py.cpp`: a new entry `certify_polygons` (signature in
  D.spec.md §3.2). It reuses `launch` (raster + validity) and the scorer's label chain (`CropFill`, `Label*`, `Count`,
  `Filter`, `Holes`) on the candidate and on the reference mask. Then it compares. Per shape it returns
  `legal`, `inter`, `union`, `equal` (XOR popcount == 0), and the size-filtered signature of candidate and reference
  (holes per component, sorted descending, as `topology.signature` [code: topology.py:157-163]). An index array
  `ref_of[i]` names the reference plane of shape i, so all rungs of one name share one uploaded reference.
  Pair queries (for the RIGA rim): optional `pairs int32[P, 2]` (indices of two shapes of this call),
  `ref_pairs int32[P, 2]` (indices of two reference planes) and `pair_min_area int64[P]`. For each pair (a, b) the
  device builds `a AND NOT b` in words and returns its size-filtered signature, and the same for the reference pair.
  No pixel returns to the host.
- change `src/objdel/targets/build.py` `_build` (:214-246). Keep the control flow: each name advances its own ladder
  level; the rim check can raise all levels [code: build.py:220-243]. New inner step: for name n at level L, build the
  parts of every remaining rung L..end that passes the `MAX_VERTICES` check (at most 14 rungs: tau 3.0 down to 0 in
  0.25 steps, plus exact rings [code: build.py:69-71]) and certify them in ONE `certify_polygons` call against the
  reference `src[n]` with `min_area[n]`. Take the first rung with `legal`, `iou >= iou_min`, `sig == ref_sig` and
  (exact names) `equal`; `iou = inter / union` (1.0 if union == 0). This picks the same rung as today, so the text
  does not change (D-G4). The rim check is a second call with shapes = the chosen disc and cup parts, references =
  `src["disc"]`, `src["cup"]`, `pairs=[(0, 1)]`, `ref_pairs=[(0, 1)]`, `pair_min_area=[min_area["rim"]]`; pass =
  equal signatures. On a rim failure, levels rise as today and the per-name calls run again.
- change `build_target`: `min_area` becomes required. Remove the interval loop in `_kept` (:146-163); move it to
  `tests/oracles/kept_oracle.py` as the reference for a property test. Update the 16 test calls without `min_area`
  [measured: grep tests/*.py, 2026-11-08] and `experiments/phase2/lab/A6/cold_start.py:29` (pass
  `min_area=min_areas(...)`), unless CLEAN has archived that lab script first.

### D5. Scorer labels: skip the second pair; conditional device bit-packing; pool memory

Maps to: Direction D3; Architecture.md §5.2 row "Memory" [code: docs/research/research2.0/Architecture.md:282].

Files: `cuda/gpucheck.cpp` (`score_words` :1549-1643, `Filter`, `LabelInit/LabelMerge/LabelFlatten` :1302-1350,
`pack_plane` :1167, `alloc`/`release` :78-84, `Block` :135-150, `add_tables` :1720-1763, `drop_tables` :1765-1776,
`score_masks`), `tests/test_gpu_scoring.py`.

Steps:
1. Label skip. `Filter{c, 1}` and `Filter{c, 0}` set a per-object flag `changed[o]` (integer `atomicOr`) when they
   remove a component or fill a hole. The final `label(1), label(0)` pair (:1614) runs per crop row only when
   `changed[o]` is set. The `zero(c.aux, ...)` at :1615 and `Holes` at :1616 always run. The kernel returns early otherwise, and the first-pass labels stay. This mirrors
   topology.py:161. The flag lives in the arena. There is no host read, so no new sync. Arenas are reused and
   never cleared [code: gpucheck.cpp:135-150]. So each call runs `zero(changed, sizeof(i32) * n, st)` before
   `CropFill`. Without it, a stale 1 costs only a relabel, but a read of never-written memory fails initcheck (D-G5).
   Row counter (`label_pairs`, D.4). The skip is per row on the device, so the host cannot count it by launches. A
   per-object `i64 relabelled[n]` sits in the `score` arena and is zeroed by the same `zero` call as `changed`.
   The second-pair `LabelInit{c, 1}` does `atomic_add(&relabelled[o], 1)` once per crop row that it does not skip
   (the existing `atomic_add(i64*)` helper works in both builds [code: gpucheck.cpp:209-211]; the CPU build's
   `for_each` is a plain loop). `ObjTerms` copies `relabelled[o]` into a new `ObjOut` field `i64 relabelled`
   [code: gpucheck.cpp:1199-1202, 1476]. So the existing `ObjOut` D2H copy before the wait at :1626 brings it back,
   and the host adds the sum over objects to `label_pairs`. No new wait and no new copy, so the D-G8 count stays 4
   waits and 2 `Drain` syncs. Expected value per call: the sum of (bh + 2) over objects with area > 0 and
   `changed[o]` set, because each object with area > 0 has bh + 2 crop rows [code: gpucheck.cpp:1583]; 0 when the
   size filter removes nothing.
   Test (CPU build): two calls with different objects give the same `label_pairs` and results as fresh calls
   (stale-flag check).
2. Device bit-packing (conditional, after D7b): `score_masks` and `add_tables` would copy byte planes and pack them on
   the device with K1-draft `pack_kernel`, in place of the host loops `pack_plane` (gpucheck.cpp:1167, 1727-1730, 1826).
   Bytes multiply the H2D bytes and the pinned staging by 8, and the host loop is small [note-D1 C12]. D7b already moves
   the table planes to the device, so this step covers only `score_masks`. Merge it only if the replay benchmark shows
   `score_masks` time is not worse (median <= 1.05 x old).
3. D5b is DROPPED. Replacing the scorer's pixel union-find with K1-draft's run CCL would leave one labeller in the
   engine, and the certificate (D3) needs the pixel chain as its independent b0/b1 leg. Recorded in the ADR (D9).
4. Path halving in `find` (:1262) only if `LabelMerge` is >= 20 % of `score_words` time in the D1 stage events on the
   replay set. If so, use `atomicMin(par[x], par[par[x]])` (parents only decrease, so this stays a valid forest).
5. D5c, pool memory and batched uploads. On the CUDA build, the engine creates its own pool with `cudaMemPoolCreate`
   (location = the current device, `cudaMemAllocationTypePinned`). It sets `cudaMemPoolAttrReleaseThreshold` =
   `UINT64_MAX` on that pool (no shrink at sync) [web: CUDA programming guide §4.3.4.2]. Device `alloc` calls
   `cudaMallocFromPoolAsync(&p, bytes, pool, lane_stream)`. `release` calls `cudaFreeAsync` on the lane stream.
   This covers all three grow-only `Block<true>` arenas of a `Lane`: `dev`, `score` and `scan` (CUB scan scratch,
   D2 step 1). Never call `cudaDeviceSetMemPool`, and never change the default pool's attributes.
   Why: `cudaMallocAsync` takes no pool. It allocates from the current pool of the stream's device [web: CUDA runtime
   API, memory pools]. Setting the device pool changes process-wide state for torch, vLLM and other libraries.
   `Block::get` growth frees the old buffer with `cudaFreeAsync` in stream order. Tables (`add_tables`, `add_tables_from_raters`) come from the same pool, and
   `drop_tables` frees with `cudaFreeAsync` on the lane stream (no device-wide sync). Add list forms
   `add_tables_many([...])` and `add_tables_from_raters` (batched, D7b): one H2D copy and one wait per batch of caches.
   Pinned staging (`Block<false>`) keeps `cudaMallocHost`. `Block::get` grows whenever a call needs more bytes, and
   the growth calls `cudaFreeHost`, which synchronizes the device [code: gpucheck.cpp:84, 135-150]. So each lane's
   two pinned blocks have ONE bound each, whatever the entry (final round 13, cuda-1): `in` = the `score_polygons`
   input bound and `out` = the `score_polygons` output bound, both below. The engine sizes `in` and `out` of every
   lane to these bounds once, inside the first engine call of the process, whatever that entry is, before the call
   stages a byte. No entry sizes them from its own call. `score_polygons`, `check_polygons`, `check_masks` and
   `score_masks` stage through them. `add_tables_from_raters` (D7b) and `eval_sets` never touch `in` or `out`: they
   copy their host bytes through pageable host memory (`std::vector`, as `add_tables` does today
   [code: gpucheck.cpp:1726, 1743]). Why: in RL the first engine call is D7b's batch, because `TRLReward.prefetch`
   builds the step's cold tables before `score_polygons`. Its outputs are a few KB. Sized from that call, `out` would
   get the 4,096 B minimum [code: gpucheck.cpp:140], and the 256-answer `score_polygons` (defects alone
   256 x 13 x 8 = 26,624 B [arithmetic]) would grow it: a `cudaFreeHost`, which synchronizes the device, and
   `pinned_grows` = 1 on correct code, so D-G15 would fail. Today every device-to-host result goes through `L.out`
   [code: gpucheck.cpp:991, 1572, 1623, 1638, 1681, 1799], so this rule is new code, not a kept behaviour. The bounds:
   - `score_polygons`: 256 answers x names per answer x `MAX_VERTICES` x `MAX_RINGS` x 8 bytes (int32 x, y)
     [code: geometry/text.py:59 (1000, 10); geometry/shape.py:120], plus the handle and offset arrays. That is
     20.5 MB per name [arithmetic].
   - `score_polygons` output staging (`Lane::out`, one block reused by all copies of a call): the largest of these,
     with n_max = 256 x names: the defects, n x 13 x 8 B [code: gpucheck.cpp:1799]; the boxes, n x 5 x 8 B (:1572);
     `ObjOut` plus `sig_start`, n x `sizeof(ObjOut)` padded to 256 B plus (n + 1) x 8 B (:1622-1623; `ObjOut` is
     2 x i64 + 4 x double = 48 B today [code: gpucheck.cpp:1199-1202]; 56 B with D5 step 1's `relabelled`, 72 B
     with B3's `sum_x`, `sum_y` [arithmetic]); and the signatures, 4 B x the total component count (:1638).
     The grammar does not bound the component count of a rasterized object (a thin ring can rasterize into several
     8-components). So the bound uses C_max = 64 components per object [estimate], or twice the largest per-object
     count in the D1 replay set (`sig_start` steps in `runs/d1/bench.json`), whichever is larger. At C_max = 64 the
     signatures dominate: 256 B per object.
   `eval_sets` runs only in `final_eval`, and D-G15 does not read that process; its integer results go to pageable
   host memory, so its scratch cap (D7) never sizes a pinned block.
   Any growth of `in` or `out` after that one sizing (a call of a staging entry larger than the bound) adds 1 to
   `pinned_grows` and logs the entry, the call's n and component total, so a fail names the bound to raise. The CPU build keeps `operator new`. A `gc.trim(bytes)` binding calls `cudaMemPoolTrimTo` for tests and end of run.
   The D7b batch upload stages its host bytes in plain host memory (`operator new`, pageable), as `add_tables` does
   today with a `std::vector` [code: gpucheck.cpp:1726, 1743]. It never uses a pinned `Block`, because the number of
   cold caches changes from step to step and a pinned block would grow (a `sync_free` and a `sync_alloc`).
   Tests (Mac, CPU build, through `gc.stats()`): after one warm-up call, 50 repeated `score_polygons` calls of the same
   shape make 0 `pool_allocs`, 0 `pool_frees`, 0 `sync_alloc` and 0 `sync_free`; `drop_tables` adds 0 waits. Then one
   call larger than the warm-up call, but inside the pinned bound, raises `pool_allocs` by at least 1 (one per grown
   arena) and leaves `sync_alloc`, `sync_free` and `pinned_grows` unchanged. This proves the pool counters are live
   and that arena growth is not counted as a synchronizing allocation.
   Leak check (replaces memcheck `--leak-check full`, see D8): record `live_device_bytes` after warm-up. Then run 50
   `score_polygons` calls and 20 `add_tables_many` / `drop_tables` cycles. After the last `drop_tables`,
   `live_device_bytes` equals the post-warm-up value. The same test runs on the box inside `tests/test_gpu_sanitize.py`.
   Pool test (box, `test_san_pool` in `tests/test_gpu_sanitize.py`): after warm-up, `gc.stats()["pool_reserved"]` is
   greater than 0 and stays the same over 50 calls. `default_pool_reserved` does not grow.

### D6. Validity totals: one warp per shape (port K2-draft §2.1); park the grid for model output

Maps to: Direction D4.

Files:
- change `cuda/gpucheck.cpp`: paste K2-draft's `for_each_warp` and the collectives (`wballot`, `wany`, `wodd`, `wsum`,
  `wmin`, `wsync`) and `ShapeTotalsWarp` from `docs/implementation2.0/kernels/K2/k2score.inc` after `ShapeTotals` (:626). In
  `launch` (:1124), replace `for_each(st, c.n, ShapeTotals{…})` with `for_each_warp(st, c.n, ShapeTotalsWarp{…})`.
  Archive `ShapeTotals` to `archive/cuda_validity/shape_totals.cpp`.
- keep `EdgePairs` as it is.

Steps and decision:
1. Do NOT port the grid chain (`GridBox…GridPairs`) for now. The grid applies only to shapes with >= 512 vertices
   [K2-draft §8.2]. Model output: a 1,536-token completion is about 3,300 characters [code: text.py:60, 2.14 chars/token],
   about 330 vertices at about 10 characters per vertex [estimate: note-D1 §1.6], so model output does not reach the grid.
   Target-builder rungs DO reach validity with up to 1,000 vertices per ring and 10 rings [code: text.py:59,
   build.py:210], through `certify_polygons` (offline, Mac). Decision rule: keep the grid parked only if rungs with
   >= 512 vertices take < 5 % of target build time in `runs/d1/rungs.json` (D1 step 3); write that number in the ADR.
   Otherwise port the grid for `certify_polygons` only. On typical shapes the grid is slower: 17.5 ms against
   EdgePairs 12.5 ms on 512 shapes [measured: K2/build/run_cpu_mac.txt]. Revisit for model output if
   `max_completion_length` rises above about 2,400 tokens [estimate: 512 vertices x 10 chars / 2.14].
2. Tests: the defect counts (13 classes) and the ring-pair matrix are equal to the old kernel on
   `C.fuzz_polygons` and on K2-draft's adversarial families (rings at 10 x 1,000 vertices, touching strips, ±2^31
   coordinates). Port these to `tests/test_cuda_checker.py`. GPU equality goes in `tests/test_cuda_checker_gpu.py`.

Steps:
1. Build and test the two new kernels on the CPU build first, as K2-draft did: brute-force references, a digest, ASan/UBSan.
2. Host cuts: the soft-Dice cut for K samples and threshold t is the smallest integer c in [0, K] with
   `float64(c) / K >= t`. numpy's `samples.mean(0)` on a bool stack is the exact integer sum divided by K, one
   rounding. So the cut test equals today's `mean >= t` exactly [code: metrics.py:155-163]. The same for k raters.
   NSD cut = the largest integer q with `sqrt(float64(q)) <= tau`. Then `d2 > q` holds exactly when `dist > tau`.
3. Gate on saved answers (Phase A saves all 8 answers): run `metrics()` old and new on the val split. Every field is
   equal, `soft_dice` included (the per-threshold Dice values come from the same integers by the same formula and are
   averaged in the same order). Only `nsd` may differ, by <= 1e-12 abs (float surfel lengths summed in another order).

  union, core, vote, the two EDTs (`edt(~union)`: outside the union, the distance to the union; `edt(core)`: inside
  the core, the distance to the nearest non-core pixel [code: cache.py:185-188]) combined into the one float32 map
  that `add_tables` stores today
  (`where(union, dist_in_core, dist_out_union)` [code: reward/cache.py:252]), the perimeter (`max(1, ·)` of the 4-neighbour boundary
  count of the union, as `boundary` [code: cache.py:124-128]), the rater areas, the rater signatures at `min_area`
  (pixel label chain, D4b), the voter flags (non-empty signature, or all raters when all are empty, as `voters`
  [code: cache.py:108-111]) and `n_vote`. It returns the handles plus the scalars the host needs (perimeter, areas,
  signatures, voter flags, n_vote). One H2D copy and one wait per batch; memory from the D5c pool.
  `add_tables_from_raters` copies the returned scalars (perimeter, areas, signatures, voter flags, `n_vote`) into
  pageable host memory (`std::vector`) after the batch's one wait, never through `Lane::out` (final round 13,
  cuda-1). A device-to-pageable copy "might be synchronous with respect to host" [web: CUDA runtime API, API
  synchronization behavior]; the device is already idle after the wait, so the copy adds only its own time and no
  `cudaMallocHost`/`cudaFreeHost`. Same reason as the upload (D5c): the cold-cache count changes from step to step,
  so a pinned block sized by this entry would grow. This call still sizes `in` and `out` to the lane bound when it is
  the first engine call of the process (D5c).

  collect the step's caches that have no tables for this pid. Build them in ONE `add_tables_from_raters` call through
  a helper `reward.cache.device_many(caches)`.
  Why: `score_many` calls `cache.device()` once per cache [code: reward/score.py:114]. Each call takes the engine
  lock, copies to the device and waits [code: gpucheck.cpp:1737, 1743-1744]. The B1 run sees each prompt once
  (300 steps x 32 prompts = 9,600 [arithmetic]), so each step would make about 32 separate builds.

  safety: a parent must not create a CUDA context before forking; `device()` already uploads per process
  [code: cache.py:241-259]). Eager host fields: `raters`, `tau`, `t5`, `k`, `union`, `core`, `vote`, `n_vote`,
  `rater_areas`, `min_area`, `box`, `digest` (numpy counts, no EDT, no labeling). `device()` calls
  `add_tables_from_raters` and stores the returned scalars. `perimeter`, `rater_sigs`, `voters` and `same_sig` become
  lazy properties that call `device()` first. `dist_out_union` and `dist_in_core` become lazy properties computed by
  `cache.edt` on first host access (tests, probes). `build` (prepare time) still computes tau and T5 on the host with
  the device `edt` (D7).
- keep the host `_band` path as the oracle in `tests/oracles/reward_reference.py`.
- create `tests/test_tables_device.py`: device tables (map, perimeter, areas, signatures, voters, n_vote) are
  byte-equal to the host-built tables (`add_tables` inputs from the oracle path) for 1,000 caches; constructing and
  loading an `ExpertCache` makes 0 engine calls (`gc.stats()`).

Steps: write the test first; land after D4b and D5c; then rerun `tests/test_reward.py` and the reward goldens
(bit-identical terms).

If it is >= 1, the count, sampled every 5 s, stays equal to it: no new context appears. If it is 0 (a container often shows an empty process list [web: nvidia-docker issue 1460]), (a) uses the container's own view instead: the number of processes in `/proc` that hold `/dev/nvidia[0-9]*` open (`for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do ls -l $p/fd 2>/dev/null \| grep -q '/dev/nvidia[0-9]' && echo $p; done \| wc -l`), sampled every 5 s, must be >= 1 before scoring and must not rise during scoring. `$OBJDEL_RUN_DIR/d/topology.json` (written by the `final_eval` sampler thread, D7 step 5; on the Mac `runs/<V3 run>/d/topology.json`) records which method ran. Why not PIDs: in a container the driver reports host PIDs, which do not exist in the container [web: github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker/issues/1460]. ## D.7. Risks and rollback

| # | Risk | Detect | Mitigation / rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-R1 | K1-draft fails on the GPU (memory model, a CUB scan, the ballot pack) | D-G1 | Bisect with `seed_rows=0`, then memcheck on the failing case [K1-draft GPU_RUN "If something fails"]. Rollback: D2 is not merged; `check_masks` and numpy stay. |
| D-R2 | Run union-find depth (no compression in Merge) is slow on vertical snakes [K1-draft §10.1] | spiral/comb lines in D-G1 | Per-row local merge first, or BKE blocks [Allegretti 2020]. It is an offline path, so slow is not wrong. |
| D-R3 | `ring_part` + 1 differs from cv2 labels on some mask | `test_rings.py` | The labels only group holes under parts. If cv2's order differs, map by grouping, and keep the hashes as the gate (D-G4). |
| D-R4 | A target hash changes | D-G4 | Do not merge. Diff the texts of the first differing row. The usual causes are ring order, offset, or a different rung picked (D4 batched rungs). Rollback = revert the commit (the oracle files move back with git mv). |
| D-R5 | `nsd` float sums differ in the last ulp | D-G9 | Tolerance 1e-12 for `nsd` only. Every other field, `soft_dice` included, must be equal. |
| D-R6 | Device EDT is not bit-identical | D-G10 | Stop. Owner decision: keep scipy for caches (offline), or accept a fingerprint change and rebuild about 24.6 k caches. |
| D-R7 | A new entry adds host syncs or allocations to the RL step | D-G8, D-G15 (counters) | `score_polygons` changes only by the label skip, the warp totals and the pool allocator. Roll each back on its own. |
| D-R8 | The price assumption is wrong (runbooks used $0.440/h) | §8 | Front section 6 prices every row (planning `dph_total` $0.641/h plus the bandwidth estimate) (measured range $0.544-0.628/h [measured: ledger.csv rows r3, r4, r5]). Setup time belongs to the shared rental, not to D. |
| D-R9 | A GPU CI lane rents without the owner's go | owner | No workflow file in Phase D (D8). Manual Vast `make gpu-check` only, with preflight. |
| D-R10 | Phase E moves files (checker -> geom/verify) at the same time | merge conflicts | One order (front section 1): D lands on the pre-E paths first; E's moves come after the last D commit. E3a then moves `checker/rings.py` -> `geom/rings.py` and `checker/certify.py` -> `geom/certify.py` unchanged. |
| D-R11 | Device work in `ExpertCache` construction or in forked workers (CUDA context before fork; one context per worker) | `tests/test_tables_device.py` (0 engine calls at construction/load); I06; D-G17 | Construction stays host-only. The device work happens at the first `device()` call in the one scoring process (D7 step 6). A forked child that calls `device()` raises. |
| D-R12 | `eval_sets` scratch competes with vLLM and the trainer for memory | D-G14 | Scratch cap with chunked sets; lower the cap in `final_eval` until fixed. |
| D-R13 | A failed launch eats the budget (r5's first launch was destroyed after 15 min, $0.2385 [measured: ledger.csv 2026-11-08T15:35:00Z]) | D-G13 | Use the one stop rule of front section 6.4: destroy the rental if the first sync has not finished 35 min after launch (r5's good launch took 31 min [measured: ledger.csv 15:35:45 -> 16:06:35]). The failed-launch reserve is in the front section 6 table. |

Open owner questions: Q1, may the hole-ring order change (it changes hashes)? Default: no. Q2, GPU CI runner: a
hosted RTX 5090 runner (StarSling lists $0.03022/min [web: note-D2 F18]; a new vendor), or Vast-only manual runs?
Default: Vast manual, no workflow file. Q3, approve `min_area` becoming required in `build_target` (D4)?
Q4 of revision 2 (a $1.40 Phase D ceiling) is withdrawn: D has no rental of its own, and its share is <= $0.85
(D-G13).

## D.8. Cost, time and dependencies

GPU (Vast, RTX 5090, North America, preflight before each rental). Front section 6 is the one rental table and the
one rate table. Phase D has NO rental of its own. Its two GPU work packages ride shared rentals:
- R-D1 (D1) is V2 item 4, after the C items (front section 6.3, back decision 3). It is optional. V2 runs only
  after a budget raise (back decision 1), and R-D1 is dropped first if the raised amount is too small. It runs `r_d1.yaml`: the K1/K2 runbooks and, if D1 has merged, the bench. It runs only before D2 merges (D1 step 4 tree rule).
- R-D2 (D2-D8, `make gpu-check` with D-G7/D-G8) is V3 item 1, after D8 merges. It cannot run earlier: it needs the
  D2-D8 code and the pre-D2 engine (D-G7).

Front 6.3 prices these rows (rental V2 item 4 and rental V3 item 1); D holds only its work breakdown in minutes.
Setup (18, 20 and 31 min launch to first sync in r3/r4/r5 [measured: experiments/phase2/vast/ledger.csv]) is
billed to the shared rental, not to D. D-G13 counts D's share as work minutes x the rental's billed `dph_total`,
which the front offer limit keeps at or below $0.641/h; so 79 min stays at or below $0.85 [estimate: 79 x 0.641 /
60 = $0.84].

| Work package | Inside | Work | GPU minutes | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-D1 (D1) | V2 item 4 (front 6.3; optional) | K1-draft runbook about 12-15 min [K1-draft GPU_RUN §7], K2-draft runbook about 15 min [K2-draft GPU_RUN], `bench_checker.py --stages` on the current engine about 5 min [estimate] | 32-35 | front 6.3, V2 item 4 |
| R-D2 (D2-D8) | V3 item 1 | `make gpu-check` (`run_box.sh --gpu-check`): build about 3 min (old + new about 6), `pytest -m gpu` on D's box test list (`D_GPU_TESTS`, D8) about 5, 4 sanitizer tools at most 4 x 5 min (300 s caps), determinism about 2, D-G7/D-G8 interleaved benches about 6 [estimate]. A's G02b and G03 run after it as `d_gpu_test.yaml` step 2 (2 min, A's share, D8) | 25-44 | front 6.3, V3 item 1 |
| D-G14/D-G15/D-G17 | V3 (B3 run and its val eval) | First 6 steps of the B3 run, `pinned_grows` at its end, and the val eval's `final_eval` (`lidc-val-shifted`, V3 item 4); the code of D7 step 5 writes the records inside those processes; billed to that phase's run | 0 extra | $0 extra |
| Total D share | | | 57-79 | Gate D-G13: <= $0.85 at the billed `dph_total` (see above) |

Engineer time [estimate]: D1 1 day; D2 2 days; D3 1.5 days (including the hash rebuild); D4 2 days; D4b 1.5 days;
D5 1.5 days (incl. D5c); D6 0.5 day; D7 3 days (plus 0.5 day for step 6, process topology); D7b 1.5 days; D8 1 day;
D9 0.5 day. About 16.5 days in all. All but R-D1/R-D2 run on the Mac at $0.

Dependencies:
- Phase A: A5 (GED/HM-IoU/Dice in final_eval) and saved answers before D7 and before the replay set switches to saved
  completions. The NVTX conventions from A before D1.
- Phase B1: the train-view target sets (`data/views/lidc-train-*`) are hash gates for D3/D4/D4b. D3 may merge before
  or after a B1 rebuild, but only with D-G4 green. It never changes a target text.
- Phase C: none in code. D-G14/D-G15/D-G17 are read in V3. K3-draft belongs to C.
  D has no decoding task: the decode tail is a Phase C item (front review: C11 "runaway cut"), not D.
- Phase E: one order (front section 1). Every D path is pre-E. E's moves run after the last D commit. The seam is
  D3's design: E3a moves `checker/rings.py` -> `geom/rings.py`, `checker/certify.py` -> `geom/certify.py` and
  `checker/{topology,volume}.py` -> `geom/` unchanged, and re-exports `geom.polygonize = rings.polygonize`. The
  numpy polygonizer (B1.4a) and bit-quads (D3) are already in `tests/oracles/`, so E has no row for them. E's move tables
  also need rows for the modules D creates: `checker/rings.py` (above) and `eval/device.py` -> `verify/device.py`.

## D.9. Tests

Merged from two independent lists written from `D.spec.md` (set 1: 90 cases T01-T117; set 2: 46 cases). Duplicates are
removed and the stronger version is kept. Test ids here are `U` unit, `P` property/fuzz, `I` integration (engine
entries), `R` regression/golden/data, `F` failure mode, `S` static/repo, `GPU` GPU box, `Z` sanitizer, `B` performance
gate. Every test is tagged with the tasks (D1...) and gates (D-G1...) of §4 and §6 that it covers. Gate numbers follow
§6 of this file. The source lists used an older numbering G1-G3 (corpus equality, part labels); those map to D-G3 here.

Conventions.
- No marker = runs on the Mac CPU build in `make test`. `gpu` = RTX 5090 and the nvcc build. The root
  `tests/conftest.py` hook (A.9) skips a `gpu` test unless `gc.build() == "cuda"`. On the box, a CPU build still FAILS:
  `run_box.sh --gpu-check` asserts the CUDA build and fails on any skipped test (D8). `slow` = long. `data` = needs
  `data/` (skip when missing); these run only through `make test-data`, which runs pytest with `-I` (D8), and
  `make test` deselects them. A test carries `gpu` or `data`, never both: the box half of a data-backed check is a
  `gpu` test that reads only the R-D2 payload through `box_input()` and its module's `BOX_INPUTS` (D8), and fails,
  never skips, when an input is missing. `sanitizer` = fixed small corpus. "BOTH" = one test body with two parameters,
  `"host"` (no marker, runs in `make test`) and `pytest.param("gpu", marks=pytest.mark.gpu)` (runs in the box list).
  Why: the hook would skip a test that carries `gpu` as a whole, so the Mac half needs its own unmarked parameter.
- `gc` = `objdel._gpucheck`. Oracles live in `tests/oracles/` (`polygonize_oracle`, `bitquad_oracle`,
  `topology_oracle`, `kept_oracle`, `reward_reference`, B1.4a/D3/D4/D4b/D7b). Tests never import them from `src/objdel`.
  A reference is never `objdel.checker.polygonize`: after B1.4a that name is the engine under test (final round 12, qa-1).
- Expected values come from an oracle (numpy/cv2/scipy), a hand-computed literal or the spec, never from the code under
  test. Equality means `np.array_equal` or `tobytes()` equality, never `allclose`; the one exception is `nsd`
  (1e-12 abs, D-G9). Seeds are fixed (`np.random.default_rng(seed)`).
- Edge keys (for hand literals): key = (y*(W+1)+x)*4+d, d: 0 E, 1 S, 2 W, 3 N. Foreground lies right of every edge
  (y down, so below an east edge). The first edge of a ring is east. Outer ring area > 0, hole ring area < 0.
- Quad tuple order is (n1, n2, nD, n3, n4) (§3.1); chi8 = (n1 - n3 - 2 nD) / 4.
