| Risk | Likelihood / evidence | Mitigation | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hard-coded module and test paths break box chains (vast policy, Makefile, docker scripts, configs, pyproject, CI) | 32 `experiments.phase*` references today [measured: grep]; test paths in pyproject.toml:58, tests.yml:54, preflight.py:29-34, 6 configs [code]; module names in strings (serve.py:52); one moved path = a failed paid run | Golden 5 + `tests/infra/test_chain.py`; `test_module_strings_resolve`; `tests/infra/test_test_paths.py`; `make preflight` on the Mac before any rental; E8 grep gate | `git revert` of the move commit (owner runs it); moves are pure, so revert is clean |
| A move changes a hash or a reward | Low: `fingerprint()` hashes values (`astuple`) and library versions, not module paths [code: reward/spec.py:50]; no persisted pickle stores a module path (all `np.save/load` with `allow_pickle=False`; worker pickles are in-process only) [measured: grep] | Goldens 1-4 bit-equal after every commit | Revert |
| Merge conflicts with Phase B/C/D edits in `fast.py`, `dataset.py`, `reward/`, `checker/` | High if done mid-run | R-4: moves only between runs. E runs after the last `main` commit of the front "End state under (b')" list that edits `fast.py`, `dataset.py`, `reward/` or `checker/`; B1 runs on the tagged pre-E tree (with B1.5's `b1_rows.yaml`); A-D tasks name pre-E paths and E's move tables map them (final review r1, arch item 1) | A B/C/D fix that lands after E uses the move tables as a path map (mechanical) |

## E.8. Cost and time; dependencies

**GPU cost of Phase E itself: $0 on the Mac.** All tasks run on the Mac (Direction.md: "Phase E: structure (Mac,
beside B, C and D)"). But two gates have a box half: E-G13 and E-G10's box part (the E4 checks). The front time line
puts every B run (V1, V3) before E, so no rental follows E (final review r2, arch item 10, QA item 14). So:
- **V4 (optional, after E; owner approval and a budget raise needed).** One RTX 5090 rental, North America hosts
  only, `make preflight` first. E writes its plan file `specs/e_v4.yaml` (front 6.3 names it; a `RunSpec`, E6 step 8b),
  with these steps in order:
  0. the CUDA build, equal to `b1_rows.yaml` step 0 (`run_box.sh --build-only`, the `build() == 'cuda'` assert,
     `tests/test_gpu_scoring.py`). Without it `sync_up` leaves the CPU build [code: experiments/phase2/vast/
     policy.py:399; CMakeLists.txt:15], the A.9 hook fails GP1-GP4, and the sampler arm scores on the CPU checker;
  1. `bash experiments/phase2/docker/env_check.sh {rd}/ckpt {rd}/env_check.json` (E-G13: the `trl_private_names`
     check and `IMPORT_CHECK`). `env_check.sh` needs the model folder as its first argument [code:
     experiments/phase2/docker/env_check.sh:9]; the V4 launch lines fetch `rl-full-3ep` there (front 6.3);
  2. the E.9 box test list by file, as `CmdStage(name="box_tests", argv=("-m", "pytest", "-q", "-p",
     "no:cacheprovider", "-m", "gpu", "tests/verify/test_verifier_gpu.py", "tests/infra/test_box_smoke.py",
     "tests/policy/test_sampler_box.py"))`, which holds the E4 deterministic check (one vLLM engine start, prompt ids
     and SamplingParams on 64 rows [estimate: about 2 min]). The argv starts with `-m, pytest`, never with `pytest`:
     the chain runs every step whose first item is not `bash` as `/opt/venv/bin/python -I <argv>` [code:
     experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:486, `def job`], so a leading `pytest` becomes `python -I pytest ...`, fails
     ("can't open file .../pytest"), and the `&&` chain [code: policy.py:490] stops before step 3. B I22a pins the
     same form for V1 step 2;
  3. the E4 sampler arm: `EvalStage(name="eval_v4", ckpt="{rd}/ckpt", view=("{data}/eval_views/lidc-val-shifted",),
     split=("val",), out=("{rd}/eval_v4_sampler",), k=8, seed=11)` (tuple form, E6.1; argv
     `--ckpt {rd}/ckpt --view {data}/eval_views/lidc-val-shifted --split val --out {rd}/eval_v4_sampler -k 8
     --seed 11`): `final_eval` with K 8 and R5's seed, on the CUDA build with pool
     size 1 (as A3).
  After `pull.sh`, the Mac runs GP5 (the TOST) on `runs/<v4 run>/eval_v4_sampler/items.jsonl`. E-G10's box half
  passes when GP4 passes on the box and GP5 passes on the Mac. V4 has no `push_hf.sh` line: it trains nothing,
  and `push_target` dies on `e_v4.yaml` (E6 step 8b). Test U51 (E.9.1) checks the file. The sampler arm is the only eval. The trainer arm is
  already on disk (`runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl`), so the box runs one eval only: 1,084 items x K 8 took 415 s
  (about 7 min) on the RTX 5090 [measured: runs/r5/eval/eval_val/final_eval.json].
- V4 time and price: front 6.3 ("V4") holds the one value; E holds no copy. E's work inside it is about 9 min of
  checks [estimate]; the front adds launch to first `run`, the 3-min build and the eval-process imports. V4 needs a budget raise: after V1,
  $0.46-0.65 is left, and V4 costs more (front 6.3).
- The front owns the rental list: front section 6.3 lists V4, and 99_back decision 3b points to it. Until V4 runs, the box
  halves of E-G10 and E-G13 show "open until V4". The E phase gate passes on the Mac halves. E4's code is done at the
  E4 step 3 commit, which also archives `sample_vllm.py` and `hf_sample.py`; only E-G10's box half waits for V4.
- If a B run slips to after E (the post-E raise path), Gate B3 pairs within V3 (B3.9 step 2). V4's checks may ride on
  that V3 run only if the owner names them in the V3 approval. They then add about 9 min [estimate]; front 6.3 does
  not price them, so the main agent adds them to the V3 amount before the approval.

**Mac time [estimate]:** one full fast suite is 523 s [measured]. There are about 12 move or change commits, so about
2 h of test wall time. Engineering effort: E0 0.5 day, E1 0.5 day, E3 1 day, E5 1.5 days, E2 1 day, E4 1 day,
E6 1.5 days (with the CliApp spike and preflight on specs), E8 2 days (repo_root, test paths, k3 move), E7 1 day,
plus about 1 h for the R-6 docstring commits (final review r3, arch item 7): about 10 days of one engineer
[estimate].

## E.9. Tests

Merged from two independent lists written from `E.spec.md` only: set 1 (`docs/implementation2.0/tests/E_tests_1.md`, 82 cases) and set 2
(`docs/implementation2.0/tests/E_tests_2.md`, 85 cases). Where both lists had the same case, I kept the stronger version (the one with more
failure modes, an independent oracle, or a negative control). Cases that exist in one list only were kept as they are.
Cases I added to close a gap are marked **NEW**. Source tags in the "From" column: `1#n` = set 1 case n, `2#n` = set 2
case n.

Conventions (style of `tests/`): plain pytest, `hypothesis`, `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch`, the autouse secrets fixture,
`pytest.skip` when data is absent, `-I` for any Python that reads data. New files go under the layer folders of E8
(`tests/core`, `tests/geom`, `tests/verify`, `tests/data`, `tests/policy`, `tests/rl`, `tests/sft`, `tests/infra`,
`tests/experiments`) from E0 on; there is no `tests/phase_e/` stage, and basenames stay unique across `tests/**`
(U47). Shared helper fixtures live in the root `tests/conftest.py`. Goldens are recorded on the E0 commit only and
are never regenerated from new code. Expected values are literals, goldens or an independent
oracle, never recomputed from the code under test. Every static guard ships a planted-violation self test (U44).
Task ids are the E.md ids: E0, E1.1-E1.5, E3a/b/c, E5.1-E5.5, E2.1-E2.7, E4.1-E4.4, E6.0-E6.8, E8.1-E8.5, E7.1-E7.5.
Gate ids are the E-G1 to E-G16 of section 6. Marks: CPU unless stated; `gpu` = skipped without a GPU; `slow` = outside
the fast suite. E adds no new marker: A registers `gpu` with `--strict-markers` (front section 4 Tests row), so an
unregistered `box` marker would stop the suite at collection. GP1-GP4 carry `gpu`. GP5 carries `data` (a Mac test
after the V4 pull; it reads no GPU).
- **One skip rule** (final review r3, QA item 12). E writes no skip line of its own. A `gpu` test skips through the
  one root `tests/conftest.py` hook that A.9 adds: it skips unless `objdel._gpucheck.build() == "cuda"`, with no torch
  import. On a box (`OBJDEL_RUN_DIR` set) the same hook fails a `gpu` test on a CPU build (A.9); `e_v4.yaml` step 0
  makes the CUDA build first. If the hook is missing on the E0 commit, E0 adds exactly that hook in one change commit,
  never a per-file skip.
- **Each box test names its rental item and its command** (final review r3, QA item 9). GP1-GP4 run at V4 step 2
  (E.8) with one file list, run as the `CmdStage` argv `-m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m gpu
  tests/verify/test_verifier_gpu.py tests/infra/test_box_smoke.py tests/policy/test_sampler_box.py` (the chain puts
  `/opt/venv/bin/python -I` in front [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:486], so the argv starts with
  `-m, pytest`, never with a bare `pytest`). E never runs `pytest -m gpu` without a file list, because that would
  collect the A, B, C and D box tests, whose inputs V4 does not ship.
- A box test that needs a run artifact skips with a reason when the artifact is absent: GP3 without
  `env_check.json`. GP5 is not a box test: it runs on the Mac after the V4 pull (`OBJDEL_V4_RUN=<v4 run>
  .venv/bin/python -I -m pytest -q tests/policy/test_sampler_tost.py::test_e_g10_tost`). Without `OBJDEL_V4_RUN` it
  skips with the reason "V4 not run". With it, a missing `runs/<v4 run>/eval_v4_sampler/items.jsonl` or
  `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/items.jsonl` fails the test; it never skips.

### E.9.2 Property tests (hypothesis, CPU)

| ID | Test | Tasks | Gates | From |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | **length_order_property.** Random lengths (1-1536 or 1-200), group size 8, random micro-batch counts: the ordering is a permutation (each index once); whole groups are not split when shared-prefix is on; the dr_grpo loss on a toy linear model equals the unsorted loss to 1e-12 relative; micro-batch max-length sum is never worse than random order; deterministic for equal seeds; `None` and 0-d entries pass through. Edge: one prompt, equal lengths, length 1, 1536. | E5.3 | E-G6 | 1#24, 2#23 |
| P2 | **unknown_key_at_every_level.** Walk every nested mapping path of each valid spec (not `grpo`), inject `zz_unknown`: `ValidationError` whose loc ends with it; inside `grpo` any JSON key is accepted and a non-JSON value (set, timestamp) raises; `compute.regions` raises; a walk over the model tree fails when a model lacks `extra="forbid"`. | E6.1 | E-G9 | 1#32, 2#34 |
| P3 | **flags_to_argv.** For random `TrainerFlags`: `--shared-prefix` iff set, `--plain` iff set, `--lr X` iff `lr is not None` (0.0 present), `--compile mode` iff set, `--trace` iff set; `grpo` serialised with sorted keys and round-trips; false flags absent. | E2.1, E6.1 | E-G9 | 1#37 |
| P4 | **verifier_batch_independence.** For random batches from the recorded corpus (duplicates allowed): `score(batch)[i]` equals `score([batch[i]])[0]` bitwise (reward and terms); a permutation permutes the results; empty batch gives `[]`. Catches state shared between items in the engine. | E7.1 | E-G12, E-G3 | 1#57, 2#60 |
| P5 | **verifier_math_symmetries.** Square nodule against a fixed reference store: IoU of a polygon with itself is exactly 1.0; shifting polygon and reference together by integer pixels changes nothing; reward stays inside the REWARD_V4 range over 1,000 random boxes; shrinking a box that covers the reference never raises IoU; swapping hole and outer gives a defect. | E7.1 | E-G12 | 2#61 |
| P6 | **verifier_thread_safety.** 8 threads, 200 concurrent `score` calls on different batches: each result equals the single-thread result bitwise. | E7.1 | E-G12 | 2#63 |
| P7 | **polygonize_seam.** `geom.polygonize(mask, offset=(0,0))`: empty or 0x0 mask gives `[]`; single pixel gives one ring of 4 vertices and area 1; rectangle gives 4; hole gives outer plus hole with opposite orientation; two blobs give two rings; full 512x512 mask; diagonal touching pins the connectivity; `offset` shifts every vertex by exactly `(row, col)` (asymmetric mask pins the order; negative offsets work); `rasterise(polygonize(m)) == m` for random blobs; dtype `bool`, `uint8 0/1`, `0/255` behave as documented. AST: production code calls only the seam, no other `polygonize*` or `mask_to_poly*`. | E3a | E-G3 | 1#67, 2#68 |

#### Sketch 1: verifier bit-equal (I24, I12, U37) - `tests/verify/test_verifier.py`
```python
import copy, json, platform, shutil, subprocess, sys, inspect
from pathlib import Path
import pytest
from hypothesis import given, settings, strategies as st

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]      # tests/<layer>/<file>.py
GOLD = ROOT / "tests" / "goldens" / "phase_e"


def hx(x):  # None stays None, floats become exact hex
    return None if x is None else float(x).hex()


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def corpus():
    return json.loads((GOLD / "corpus64.json").read_text())      # [{"id","key","text","truncated","job"}...]


def test_verifier_bit_equal_to_score_batch(corpus, view_root):
    from objdel.verify.api import Verifier, ScoreItem
    from objdel.verify.reward import score_batch

    items = [ScoreItem(c["id"], c["key"], c["text"], c["truncated"]) for c in corpus]
    got = Verifier("reward_v4", view_root).score(items)
    ref = score_batch([tuple(c["job"]) for c in corpus])          # independent entry point
    assert [r.id for r in got] == [c["id"] for c in corpus]
    for i, r in enumerate(got):
        assert hx(r.reward) == hx(ref["reward"][i]), (i, corpus[i]["text"][:80])
        for k, v in r.terms.items():
            assert hx(v) == hx(ref[k][i]), (i, k)
        assert dict(r.defects) == ref["defects"][i]
    plat = f"{sys.platform}-{__import__('platform').machine()}"
    gold = GOLD / f"invariance.{plat}.json"
    if not gold.exists():
        pytest.skip(f"no golden for {plat}")
    assert [hx(r.reward) for r in got] == json.loads(gold.read_text())["score_batch_rewards"]

```

#### Sketch 2: batch independence (P4)
```python
# ---- 2. Batch independence / permutation invariance (case 60) ---------------------------------------------------
@settings(max_examples=50, deadline=None)
@given(st.data())
def test_score_is_batch_independent(data, corpus, view_root):
    from objdel.verify.api import Verifier, ScoreItem

    v = Verifier("reward_v4", view_root)
    idx = data.draw(st.lists(st.integers(0, len(corpus) - 1), min_size=1, max_size=40))   # duplicates allowed
    items = [ScoreItem(f"{n}", corpus[i]["key"], corpus[i]["text"], corpus[i]["truncated"]) for n, i in enumerate(idx)]
    together = v.score(items)
    for it, r in zip(items, together):
        alone = v.score([it])[0]
        assert hx(r.reward) == hx(alone.reward) and dict(r.terms) == dict(alone.terms)
    perm = data.draw(st.permutations(range(len(items))))
    shuffled = v.score([items[p] for p in perm])
    assert [hx(shuffled[j].reward) for j in range(len(perm))] == [hx(together[p].reward) for p in perm]

```

#### Sketch 3: TRL drift guard (I4, I5) - `tests/rl/test_trl_adapter.py`
```python
# ---- 3. trl_adapter.check negative cases (case 16) ------------------------------------------------------------
SIX = ["_get_per_token_logps_and_entropies", "_generate_and_score_completions", "_prepare_inputs",
       "_compute_loss", "_generate", "_calculate_rewards"]   # the real six come from the adapter's recorded table


def test_check_passes_on_pin():
    from objdel.rl import trl_adapter
    assert trl_adapter.check() is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", SIX)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["missing", "signature", "source"])
def test_check_detects_drift(monkeypatch, name, mode):
    monkeypatch.delenv("OBJDEL_TRL_UNPINNED", raising=False)      # A7's opt-in must be off
    from trl import GRPOTrainer
    from objdel.rl import trl_adapter as A

    orig = getattr(GRPOTrainer, name)
    if mode == "missing":
        monkeypatch.delattr(GRPOTrainer, name)
    elif mode == "signature":
        ns = {}
        exec("def f(self, renamed_param): pass", ns)
        monkeypatch.setattr(GRPOTrainer, name, ns["f"])
    else:  # same signature, different body -> SHA-256 differs
        ns = {}
        params = ", ".join(inspect.signature(orig).parameters)
        exec(f"def f({params}):\n    return None", ns)
        monkeypatch.setattr(GRPOTrainer, name, ns["f"])
    with pytest.raises(A.TRLContractError) as e:
        A.check()
    assert name in str(e.value) and "1.17.1" in str(e.value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("ver", ["1.17.2", "1.17.1.dev0", "", None])
def test_version_drift(monkeypatch, ver):
    monkeypatch.delenv("OBJDEL_TRL_UNPINNED", raising=False)
    import trl
    from objdel.rl import trl_adapter as A
    monkeypatch.setattr(trl, "__version__", ver)
    with pytest.raises(A.TRLContractError, match="1.17.1"):
        A.check()

```

#### Sketch 4: spec strictness (U21, P2) - `tests/core/test_spec.py`
```python
# ---- 4. Spec strictness incl. YAML duplicate keys and unknown keys at every level (cases 34, 35) -----------------
SPECS = sorted((ROOT / "specs").glob("*.yaml"))


def _paths(node, prefix=()):
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        yield prefix
        for k, v in node.items():
            if k != "grpo":                      # free-form mapping by design
                yield from _paths(v, prefix + (k,))
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for i, v in enumerate(node):
            yield from _paths(v, prefix + (i,))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("spec", SPECS, ids=lambda p: p.name)
def test_unknown_key_rejected_at_every_level(spec, tmp_path):
    import yaml, pydantic
    from objdel.core.spec import load_spec
    base = yaml.safe_load(spec.read_text())
    load_spec(spec)                                                    # control: valid
    for path in _paths(base):
        doc = copy.deepcopy(base)
        node = doc
        for p in path:
            node = node[p]
        node["zz_unknown"] = 1
        f = tmp_path / "s.yaml"
        f.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(doc))
        with pytest.raises(pydantic.ValidationError):
            load_spec(f)


def test_duplicate_yaml_key_is_an_error(tmp_path):
    from objdel.core.spec import load_spec
    text = (ROOT / "specs" / "b1_rows.yaml").read_text()
    f = tmp_path / "dup.yaml"
    f.write_text(text + "\nschema_version: 1\n")                       # second top-level key of the same name
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="schema_version"):           # rule: ValueError naming the key
        load_spec(f)                                                   # (pydantic's ValidationError is a ValueError)

```

#### Sketch 5: the contract guards itself (I1) - `tests/infra/test_layers_contract.py`
```python
# ---- 5. lint-imports guards the guard: planted violations must fail (case 2) -------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize("target, line", [
    ("core/__init__.py", "import objdel.rl"),
    ("verify/__init__.py", "import objdel.data"),
    ("sft/__init__.py", "import objdel.rl"),
])
def test_planted_layer_violation_fails(tmp_path, target, line):
    dst = tmp_path / "repo"
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / "src", dst / "src", ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.so"))
    shutil.copy(ROOT / "pyproject.toml", dst)
    for extra in (".importlinter",):
        if (ROOT / extra).exists():
            shutil.copy(ROOT / extra, dst)
    with open(dst / "src" / "objdel" / target, "a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"\n{line}\n")
    r = subprocess.run(["lint-imports", "--no-cache"], cwd=dst, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    assert r.returncode != 0, r.stdout
    assert "BROKEN" in r.stdout.upper() and "objdel" in r.stdout
    clean = subprocess.run(["lint-imports", "--no-cache"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    assert clean.returncode == 0, clean.stdout
```

```python
# 2. no ML stack below policy, fresh process per package
LOW = ["objdel.core", "objdel.geom", "objdel.verify", "objdel.data"]
BAD = {"torch", "trl", "transformers", "vllm", "peft", "datasets", "accelerate"}
@pytest.mark.parametrize("pkg", LOW)
def test_no_ml_stack(pkg):
    import importlib, pkgutil
    code = (
        "import importlib, pkgutil, sys\n"
        f"p = importlib.import_module({pkg!r})\n"
        "for m in pkgutil.walk_packages(p.__path__, p.__name__ + '.'):\n"
        "    importlib.import_module(m.name)\n"
        "print(sorted({k.split('.')[0] for k in sys.modules} & " + repr(BAD) + "))\n"
    )
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    assert out.stdout.strip() == "[]", out.stdout
```

```python
# 5. spec -> argv golden, string for string
@pytest.mark.parametrize("spec", ["b1_rows", "rl_full", "r5_shared"])
def test_to_argv_matches_pre_phase_e_chain(spec):
    from objdel.core.spec import load_spec, to_argv
    rs = load_spec(ROOT / "specs" / f"{spec}.yaml")
    gold = json.loads((GOLD / "chain_argv.json").read_text())[spec]   # ordered list of argv lists, E0 commit
    got = [to_argv(s, "RD", "DATA") for s in rs.stages]               # stage order and flag order both count
    assert got == gold
```

#### Sketches 9-11: the NEW gap tests

```python
# 9. U41: the TID251 ban fires (E0). Run once per banned name in a temp file.
@pytest.mark.parametrize("src", [
    "from trl.trainer import grpo_trainer\n",
    "import trl.trainer.grpo_trainer\n",
    "import objdel._gpucheck\n",
])
def test_banned_import_fails_ruff(tmp_path, src):
    f = tmp_path / "x.py"
    f.write_text(src)
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "ruff", "check", "--no-cache",
                        "--config", str(ROOT / "pyproject.toml"), str(f)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert r.returncode != 0 and "TID251" in r.stdout          # adapt: the temp path must not match a per-file-ignore


# 10. U40: objdel.rl stays lazy (E5.1)
def test_rl_package_is_lazy():
    code = "import sys, objdel.rl.rows; print(sorted({'trl', 'vllm'} & {m.split('.')[0] for m in sys.modules}))"
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    assert out.stdout.strip() == "[]"


# 11. U39: prepare takes the prompt table as an argument (E3c); the manifest bytes stay equal to the E0 commit
def test_prepare_manifest_bytes_unchanged_and_table_used(tmp_path, tiny_prepared_inputs):
    from objdel.data.prepare import prepare
    from objdel.policy.prompt import PROMPTS
    a = prepare(**tiny_prepared_inputs, out=tmp_path / "a", prompts=PROMPTS)
    assert (tmp_path / "a" / "manifest.json").read_bytes() == (GOLD / "prepare_manifest.json").read_bytes()
    b = prepare(**tiny_prepared_inputs, out=tmp_path / "b", prompts={k: v + " x" for k, v in PROMPTS.items()})
    assert (tmp_path / "b" / "manifest.json").read_bytes() != (GOLD / "prepare_manifest.json").read_bytes()
```

### E.9.10 Decided rules (formerly open questions; each test asserts only this rule)

Final review r1, QA item 10: a test that accepts "raises or returns null" pins nothing. Each former open question now
has one rule (the first option, unless a measured reason says otherwise). The owner confirms them in the 99_back list.

1. `save_steps` defaults to 50, and the `save_steps <= steps` rule applies to the default too: `steps=10` without an
   explicit `save_steps` raises (U21). A short stage sets `save_steps`.
2. `truncated(ids, stops)` is True when the last token is not a stop id, also when a stop id occurs earlier (vLLM
   `finish_reason == "length"` semantics; U28).
3. CPU and GPU builds are bit-equal (one source, ADR 0001). A mismatch fails GP1 and prints the maximum ulp
   difference; there is no tolerance unless the owner adds one in an ADR.
4. `SOURCE_SHA256` hashes the raw `inspect.getsource` text, so a comment or whitespace change in a TRL method raises
   (I5).
5. `ScoreResult.terms` is `{}` when `error` is set (U32). `stages: []` raises (U21). An empty HTTP `items` list gives
   200 and `[]`, as `Verifier.score([])` does (I27, P4). An empty `CmdStage.argv` raises (U23).
6. `REGION` matching is exact and case-sensitive: only `US` and `CA` pass; `us` is rejected (U16).
7. `trl_adapter.check()` raises `TRLContractError` when `inspect.getsource` fails (pyc-only install; I5).

## DOC.1. Goal and why

**Goal.** Every engineering document is tracked in git, builds into one site with no warning, and is checked by tests
against the code. The headline test and validation numbers in the README and the HF card come from one tracked
results file. A new engineer finds the current system, the live plan and each phase's pages from one index. Old
research stays frozen and is labelled.

**Why (evidence).**

1. The engineering docs are not in git. 385 files exist under `docs/` outside `docs/research/`; only 8 are tracked
   (the figures). Of the 385, 37 are the engineering pages and figures, and 348 are `docs/implementation2.0/` (this plan
   and the kernel drafts): 298 of those sit in the kernel `build/` folders (arm64 Mach-O binaries, `.dSYM` folders,
   logs), 1 is a `.log` (git-ignored by `*.log`), and 49 are text to track. `docs/research/research2.0/` (the plan)
   has 0 of 4 files tracked [measured, 2026-11-08: `find docs -type f -not -path 'docs/research/*' | wc -l` = 385;
   `find docs/implementation2.0 -type f | wc -l` = 348; `find docs/implementation2.0 -path '*/build/*' -type f | wc -l` =
   298; `git ls-files docs | grep -v '^docs/research/' | wc -l` = 8; `git ls-files docs/research/research2.0 | wc -l`
   = 0]. `.gitignore` ignores only the root `/build/`, so `git add docs/implementation2.0` would take 13.5 MB of
   binaries (K1 `build/` 3.5 MB, K2 `build/` 10 MB) [measured: `du -sh docs/implementation2.0/kernels/*/build`]. The
   planning notes, specs and reviews that the plan cites exist only in the session scratchpad, which macOS clears.
   One lost laptop, or one cleared scratchpad, loses all of them.
2. Docs are not tested. `docs/README.md` says so: "These documents are not checked by a test"
   [code: docs/README.md:60]. Only the root README has a test (`tests/test_readme.py`: quick start, make targets).
3. Stale facts sit in code that the docs point at:
   - `policy.py` docstring says "$10 alarm, $15 stop", "passes $15" and "reaches $10"
     [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:16,19]; the constants are `ALARM, HARD_STOP = 10.0, 17.5`
     [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:58]. Front section 6.1 step 0 raises `HARD_STOP` to $19.90 before V1
     (owner approval), so no DOC check or test asserts 17.5 as the value of the constant (the U17 parser fixtures are
     only sample text). Docs record the gap twice [code: docs/runbooks/gpu-run.md:121;
     docs/architecture/decisions/0009-vast-ai-north-america-and-preflight.md:74,81].
   - "TRL 1.16" appears in 8 places in code and tests [measured: grep, 2026-11-08]: `src/objdel/train/sample.py:28`,
     `rewards.py:1,47`, `configs.py:1`, `callbacks.py:45`, `experiments/phase2/train_sft.py:49`,
     `experiments/phase2/docker/Dockerfile.phase2:6`, `tests/test_train_trl.py:1`. Five TRL source links still point
     at `blob/v1.16.0`: `src/objdel/train/configs.py:48`, `sample.py:30,33`, `rewards.py:50`, `callbacks.py:46`
     [measured: grep, 2026-11-08]. The pin is `trl==1.17.1` [code: pyproject.toml:21] and the image locks agree
     [code: experiments/phase2/docker/locks/train.txt:335; locks/vllm_native.txt:891].
4. Numbers are copied by hand. README line 121 quotes the test result and the validation result; the sources are
   git-ignored files `runs/r5/eval/eval_test/final_eval.json` [measured: iou_tc 0.6448, f5 0.8164, precision_vote
   0.6946, recall_vote 0.7478, dice_vote 0.7007, legal 0.9938, items 2200, K 8, seed 11, view `lidc-test-shifted`]
   and `runs/r5/eval/eval_val/final_eval.json` [measured: iou_tc 0.6182, f5 0.8065, precision_vote 0.6893,
   recall_vote 0.7159, items 1084, view `lidc-val-shifted`]. The evaluated model is HF `svenk029/objdel-sft`
   revision `rl-full-3ep`, fetched into `runs/r5/final_model` [code: docs/research/notes/final_eval_2026-11-08.md:3;
   experiments/phase2/configs/rl_shifted.yaml:20]. `docs/testing.md:5` hard-codes "1,484 tests".
5. The README layout block says `docs/  research reports and notes, figures` [code: README.md:179]. `docs/` now has
   11 engineering areas. `ROADMAP.md` is dated 2026-10-18 [code: ROADMAP.md:3] but `docs/README.md` calls it "the
   plan"; the live plan is `docs/research/research2.0/Direction.md`, inside the frozen research folder.
6. 63 public classes, functions and methods in `src/objdel` have no docstring
   [measured: `ruff check src/objdel --select D100,D101,D102,D103,D104,D106` = 25 D102 + 23 D103 + 15 D101].
7. Phases A to E and CLEAN each add pages, ADRs and glossary words. With no checks and no owner table, those pages
   will drift the way the items above drifted.
8. Owner rules: old code is archived, not left beside new code; `make test` and `make lint` must pass; GPU budget
   $3 on Vast AI, North America hosts, preflight before every rental [BRIEF section 3]. No doc states the $3 rule
   today, and `Direction.md` quotes phase costs above it ("Phase B ... $4.4-5.0") [code: Direction.md:123].
   Archive rules exist only as one line [code: docs/contributing.md:61] and one good README
   [code: archive/cpu_checker/README.md].

## DOC.3. Design

### DOC.3.1 Box diagram

```
 +------------------+   +-------------------+   +------------------------------+
 | src/objdel/**.py |   | docs/**/*.md      |   | runs/<id>/eval/eval_{test,val}|
 | (docstrings)     |   | docs/plan/*.md    |   | /final_eval.json (ignored)   |
 +--------+---------+   +---------+---------+   +---------------+--------------+
          |                       |                             |
          | griffe (static)       |                             | make headline RUN=<id> (owner, Mac)
          v                       v                             v
 +--------------------------------------+        +------------------------------+
 | zensical build --strict  (mkdocs.yml)|        | docs/results/headline.json   |
 | links + anchors validated            |        | docs/results/runs.md         |
 | api-autonav -> reference/objdel/**   |        +---------------+--------------+
 +-----------------+--------------------+                        |
                   |                                             v
                   v                   +------------------------------------------+
          +----------------+           | tests/test_docs.py  (pytest, fast)       |
          | site/ (ignored)|           |  links outside docs/, paths, make targets|
          +----------------+           |  ADR index+headings, configs, versions,  |
                                       |  cost table, headline, CITATION, archive,|
                                       |  attribution, nav, no scratch paths      |
                                       +--------------------+---------------------+
                                                            |
        +---------------------------------------------------+---------+
        v                         v                                   v
 +--------------+        +------------------+                +-----------------+
 | make test    |        | CI job "docs"    |                | CI lychee       |
 | make lint    |        | lock install +   |                | weekly + PR *.md|
 | (ruff D1xx;  |        | build --strict   |                | (cron: non-     |
 |  python job) |        |                  |                |  blocking)      |
 +--------------+        +------------------+                +-----------------+

 hf_push --card-only --revision rl-full-3ep --headline docs/results/headline.json
   download README.md of the revision -> replace "Evaluation" + "Limitations" -> upload README.md only (owner, Mac)
```

### DOC.3.2 Data flow

1. An engineer changes code or a doc in one pull request.
2. `make lint` runs ruff, now with D100-D104 and D106 on `src/objdel`: a public def with no docstring fails.
3. `make test` (and the CI `python` job, which already runs pytest) runs `tests/test_docs.py`. It reads Markdown,
   `Makefile`, `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the lock files, `policy.py` constants, `CITATION.cff` and
   `docs/results/headline.json`. It never reads `runs/` or `data/`.
4. `make docs` runs `zensical build --strict`. A broken internal link or a missing anchor under `docs/`, or an
   unresolved API reference, is an error. Pages missing from `nav` are caught by check 13, not by the build.
5. After a new evaluation, the owner runs `make headline RUN=<id>` on the Mac. It copies the metrics of
   `runs/<id>/eval/eval_test/final_eval.json` and `eval_val/final_eval.json` into the tracked
   `docs/results/headline.json`, at full precision. The README test then fails until the README quotes the new numbers.
6. `hf_push --card-only` reads the same `headline.json` to write the Evaluation section of the HF model card.

### DOC.3.3 GPU vs CPU

This phase has no numeric work. Everything runs on the CPU: the Mac and the CI runners.

| Item | Where | Why not the GPU |
|---|---|---|
| Site build (`zensical build`) | CPU | Text parsing and HTML output. 2.1-2.7 s on the Mac for the tree without `docs/implementation2.0/`; 3.4 s with it (kernel sources excluded) [measured: docs/implementation2.0/notes/doc/r1build/build.txt, 2026-11-08]. A GPU gives nothing. |
| `tests/test_docs.py` | CPU | Regex and file reads. Today 106 `.md` files are under `docs/`; 37 are outside `docs/research/`: 29 engineering pages and 8 under `docs/implementation2.0/` (this plan, the kernels README, 3 `DESIGN.md`, 3 `GPU_RUN.md`) [measured, 2026-11-08: `find docs -name '*.md' \| wc -l`; `find docs -name '*.md' -not -path 'docs/research/*' \| wc -l`; same with `-not -path 'docs/implementation2.0/*'`]. DOC1 adds 4 plan pages and the copied notes. No arrays. |
| ruff D rules | CPU | Static analysis of source text. |
| lychee | CPU + network | HTTP requests. |
| `make headline` | CPU | Reads two JSON files of means and CIs. The numbers were made on the GPU by `final_eval` (phase A owns that). |
| `hf_push --card-only` | CPU + network | One download and one upload of `README.md`. No rental. |

GPU minutes in this phase: 0. The rule "GPU everywhere" is about training, scoring and polygonizing; DOC only writes
about them. DOC must keep the docs true to that rule: DOC9 writes today's CPU/GPU facts (polygonizer path, CPU
`pixel_values`) into the existing table in `architecture/overview.md` section 5, and phases C and D update it.

## DOC.4. Tasks

Order:
- DOC1 step 0 (copy the planning evidence out of the scratchpad) runs at the hand-off of this plan, before the
  planning session ends. The scratchpad is session storage; after it is cleared, step 0 cannot run.
- DOC1 and DOC2 run before any phase starts (front section 1, time line step 1). DOC1 protects everything else and
  fixes the paths every later check reads. DOC2 removes the "TRL 1.16" text, so phase A's test S06 is green when A
  starts.
- DOC2 and DOC5 edit `src/objdel` text. The preflight stamp holds `objdel_and_script_sha256` and refuses a launch
  when it changes [code: experiments/phase2/preflight.py:69,78-91]. So DOC2 and DOC5 land before B1's preflight, or
  after B1's teardown; no `src/` edit between a preflight and its teardown.
- DOC5 writes docstrings only after CLEAN has published its removal list (CL1), so no docstring is written for code
  that CLEAN deletes; the ruff gate is enabled in the same pull request.
- DOC3, DOC4 and DOC6-DOC12 can run in any order after DOC1, on the Mac, beside phases A to E.
- DOC4 and DOC5 land before phase E moves code. So their checks are live during E and CLEAN. Rule: `make test` and
  `make lint` stay green on every commit (CLAUDE.md). Each E move commit and each CLEAN archive commit fixes its own
  doc paths (E R-1):
  - it rewrites, with the same old -> new path map, every backtick repo path in the DOC4 `doc_files` set;
  - the E6 switch commit adds each new `specs/*.yaml` to `docs/reference/configs.md` (check 6);
  - the E8.1 move commit sets `POLICY_MODULE = "objdel.infra.vast.ledger"` in `tests/docs_check.py` (check 8);
  - a commit that moves a folder named in `FROZEN_GLOBS` or the docs lock path updates that constant too.
  A move into `src/objdel` gets its docstrings in a change commit first (E R-6), so DOC5's gate stays green.
- DOC13 runs last, after phase E and CLEAN have moved code. It re-runs the checks; it does not carry a backlog.

Git rule for every task: the agent edits files only. The owner runs every git command. Each task ends with the exact
commands for the owner. No `Co-Authored-By` or "Generated with" lines anywhere (CLAUDE.md).

### DOC6. One source for headline numbers; the run index

Files to create:
- `docs/results/headline.json` (tracked). Schema (values copied by the script at full precision, never typed):
  ```json
  {"run": "r5", "model_ref": "svenk029/objdel-sft@rl-full-3ep", "ckpt": "/workspace/runs/r5/final_model",
   "seed": 11, "K": 8, "ci_unit": "item",
   "test": {"source": "runs/r5/eval/eval_test/final_eval.json", "view": "lidc-test-shifted", "items": 2200,
            "metrics": {"iou_tc": {"mean": 0.6448..., "ci95": [..., ...]}, "f5": {...}, "precision_vote": {...},
                        "recall_vote": {...}, "dice_vote": {...}, "legal": {...}}},
   "val":  {"source": "runs/r5/eval/eval_val/final_eval.json", "view": "lidc-val-shifted", "items": 1084,
            "metrics": {... same 6 keys ...}}}
  ```
  `view` is the last path part of the input's `view` field. `ci_unit` is `"item"` because `final_eval` uses an item
  bootstrap [code: experiments/phase2/final_eval.py:10,34]; phase A writes `"patient"` when it switches
  the gate CI to the patient-cluster bootstrap (key `group_id`; nodule and item CIs become second lines [A.md, A1
  step 5]). `model_ref` comes from the `--model-ref` argument (the input holds only the box path).
- `experiments/phase2/headline.py` (module script, `-I`): `main(argv) -> int`; args `--test PATH --val PATH` (two
  `final_eval.json` files, each under `runs/`) or `--run ID`, plus `--model-ref REF`, `--out
  docs/results/headline.json`. `--run ID` is a short form for `runs/<ID>/eval/eval_test/final_eval.json` and
  `runs/<ID>/eval/eval_val/final_eval.json` (the R5 layout [measured: ls runs/r5/eval]). Give one form only; both
  or neither exit 2. Why two paths: A3 writes `{rd}/eval_val` in the V1 run and `{rd}/eval_test` in the V3 run
  [A.md, A3 plan files], so no one run folder holds both, and A1 step 5b writes R5's schema-2 files to
  `runs/r5/eval_a1/`. It reads both schemas. Schema 1 (no `schema` key, R5 today): `ci95 := f[m]["ci95"]`,
  `ci_unit := "item"`. Schema 2 (`"schema": 2`, A1): `ci95 := f[m][f["gate_ci"]]`, `ci_unit :=` `gate_ci` without

  (non-zero exit, writes nothing) when a file is missing, its `split` is not the expected one, it has no `view`, the
  test and val files differ in schema or `gate_ci`, or a schema-2 `gate_ci` names a CI that is null. Keeps the 6

  VAL=runs/r5/eval_a1/eval_val/final_eval.json` after A1 step 5b, or the A3 files after V3 (A9).

     Phase 1 stack and algorithms/data_engineering.md:94].

     in another scan's XML [web: TCIA LIDC-IDRI page, "Annotation and Markup Issues/Comments" item 2, fetched
     2026-11-08].

     places contours by z (`imageZposition`) and reads no rating value [code: src/objdel/data/lidc.py:140-147], so the
     0510 value has no effect. But the CT fetch picks slices by SOP UID: `lidc.sop_z` maps each `imageSOP_UID` to its

     nodule >= 3 mm but gave no characteristic ratings [web: same page, item 5]. In the local copies (folder 187), those

     [measured: grep of data/raw/lidc_xml/tcia-lidc-xml/187/{044,191}.xml, 2026-11-08]. The parser keeps a nodule only
     when that element exists [code: src/objdel/data/lidc.py:147], so these two outlines are dropped. Whether other
     readers outlined the same nodules is not checked here [unverified]. Before writing this line, DOC11 counts the
     affected items with a `-I` script over `data/`, or writes "count not measured".

     experiments/phase2/build_eval_views.py:57,60], and B1 trains on draws from the same law. A test gain shows fit to
     that law; it does not prove robustness to clinical framing.

Non-blocking metric (reported, not a gate): sentences over 25 words in `docs/implementation2.0/Implementation.md` and in
the pages DOC writes. The final round 1 review counted 803 of about 4,965 prose sentences over 25 words in the plan
[measured: docs/implementation2.0/reviews/final_r1_qa.md item 17]; round 2 counted 993 of 5,203 [measured:
docs/implementation2.0/reviews/final_r2_qa.md item 25]; round 3 counted 1,165 of 7,034 [measured:
docs/implementation2.0/reviews/final_r3_qa.md item 21]. The round 3 rule splits list items apart, so its count is not
comparable with the round 1 and 2 counts. The plan also grows, so DOC reports the share, not the count alone.
- Rule (write it beside every count, so the next count is comparable): join wrapped lines; split list items apart;
  skip code blocks and tables; split on sentence ends; count a sentence when it has more than 25 words.
- DOC re-counts with this rule after the edits and writes the count and the share in the DOC phase report.
- Split first: gate cells and task steps. One rule per sentence; the reason goes on its own "Why:" line.
- New DOC pages aim at 20 words or fewer per sentence in procedures (ASD-STE100).

## DOC.7. Risks and rollback

| Risk | Sign | Rollback |
|---|---|---|
| Zensical 0.1 breaks or drops a feature | `make docs` fails after an upgrade | Pin stays `zensical==0.1.0`. Swap the `docs` extra to `mkdocs-material==9.8.1`, `mkdocs-api-autonav==0.4.0`, `mkdocstrings-python==2.0.10`; same `mkdocs.yml` [measured: both built it, DOC phase trial, 2026-11-08]; the weekly rollback build shows it still works |
| A transitive docs package releases a breaking version | strict build red with no repo change | CI installs from `locks/docs.txt`; only a deliberate re-compile changes it |
| `src/` text edit after a preflight | launch refused: "stale (code changed since it passed)" [code: preflight.py:89-90] | DOC2 and DOC5 land before B1's preflight or after its teardown; PR template box |
| Drift tests are too strict and block real work | many false failures on backtick paths or versions | Narrow `backtick_paths` (prefix list) or add a path to `FROZEN_GLOBS` rather than delete the test |
| A stale version in a doc equals some lock's pin (e.g. "torch 2.13.0" in a training doc) | not caught | Accepted: one allowed set per package keeps the check simple and has 0 false hits today [measured] |
| Phase E or CLEAN moves code that docs name | path, config or cost checks fail on the move commit | Expected to be caught: each E or CLEAN commit fixes its own doc paths, `configs.md` rows, `POLICY_MODULE`, `FROZEN_GLOBS` and lock path in the same commit (E R-1; section 4 order), so `make test` stays green. DOC13 only re-runs the checks and rewrites `package.md` |
| The plan folder move breaks references in other phase pages | links to `docs/research/research2.0/` | Only `docs/README.md` and `Research2.0.md` reference it in REPO [measured: grep, 2026-11-08]; the implementation doc's phase pages are read with the new path (DOC1 note) |
| lychee rate limits (GitHub, arXiv) | 429 on cron | `accept` includes 429; cache restored across runs; cron failure does not block |
| The PDF has no redistribution licence | owner unsure | It stays git-ignored (DOC1); cite arXiv 2212.07020 only |
| A secret or RIGA-derived result reaches the public repo | DOC1 scan hit | Scan before `git add`; owner reads `git diff --cached --stat`; RIGA items need owner OK |
| The scratchpad is cleared before DOC1 step 0 runs | cited notes, specs and reviews missing; check 14 has nothing to fix but links point at nothing | Step 0 runs at plan hand-off, before the session ends (section 4 order). If it is too late: mark each lost citation `[unverified: source lost]` and re-measure only the facts a gate needs |
| Kernel binaries or a local path enter git with `docs/implementation2.0` | `--stat` lists `build/` or a file over 1 MB; scan (a) hit | `.gitignore` line for `kernels/*/build/` lands in the same commit; step 0 scrubs paths; DOC-G13 and DOC-G14 |
| Banner edits to frozen records seen as editing evidence | owner objects | Banner is one prepended line; the checks do not depend on it; `git revert` removes it |
| Headline drift: a new eval without `make headline` | README and card show old numbers | Only the owner runs evals; the definition of done lists `make headline` |
| Card update overwrites card text | licence or base-model lines lost | `card_update` keeps every line outside the two sections; test checks it; HF keeps the previous commit for revert |
| Card update leaks a token | n/a | Same path as today: token on stdin only, never argv/env/disk [code: hf_push.py:7-9]; `token_problems` first |

Every task is text plus tests. Rollback for any task is the owner's `git revert <commit>`.

## DOC.8. Cost, time and dependencies

- GPU: 0 minutes, $0. No rental. The $3 budget is untouched. The card update runs on the Mac.
- Network: PyPI installs for the docs lock; lychee requests in CI; one HF download and one upload for the card.
- Engineer time on the Mac [estimate]: DOC1 2 h (step 0 copy and scrub included); DOC2 1 h; DOC3 2.5 h; DOC4 5.5 h (check 16 included); DOC5 3 h; DOC6 2.5 h; DOC7 1.5 h;
  DOC8 0.5 h; DOC9 4 h; DOC10 0.5 h; DOC11 3.5 h; DOC12 0.5 h; DOC13 2 h (a re-run, no backlog). Total about 29.5 h.
- CI time: the site build took 2.1-2.7 s on the Mac [measured]; the job time is dominated by the install
  [estimate: not measured on a runner].

Dependencies:
- DOC1 and DOC2 land before any phase starts, so phase pages are tracked, the plan path is final, and phase A's S06
  is green from A's first task.
- DOC2 and DOC5: before B1's preflight or after its teardown. DOC5 also after CLEAN's removal list.
- Phase A provides the numbers for `metrics.md` and a new `headline.json` (via `make headline TEST=... VAL=...`,
  `ci_unit: patient`): from R5's schema-2 files (A1 step 5b, $0 on the Mac), or from the A3 files when V3 re-runs
  the final test (A9).
- Phases B, C, D write their own pages (DOC9 table); DOC4 checks keep them true.
- Phase E: moves code and adds the import-linter contract. Each E commit keeps the DOC4 checks and the DOC5 gate
  green (E R-1, E R-6; section 4 order). DOC13 runs after it.
- CLEAN: creates `archive/<name>/` folders; DOC8 rules and check 11 apply to them. Each archive commit keeps check 2
  green under the same rule; CLEAN adds no second doc-path test. DOC13 runs after it.
- Owner-only steps: every git command, the HF card update, any `CLAUDE.md` edit, the PDF licence decision, the
  `CITATION.cff` author name, OK for each RIGA-derived figure. (The `HARD_STOP` value is 99_back decision 4 and front
  section 6.1 step 0; DOC only keeps the runbook in line with it.)

## DOC.9. Tests

Merged from two independent lists written from the same spec: `docs/implementation2.0/tests/DOC_tests_1.md` (103 cases, called S1) and
`docs/implementation2.0/tests/DOC_tests_2.md` (40 cases, called S2). Each merged test names its sources as `S1 Tnn` / `S2 Tn`. Where the
two lists said the same thing, the stronger version is kept (the one with more edge cases, or a harder-to-fake oracle).
No test was run: the code under test does not exist yet. The only measured items are marked [measured].

### DOC.9.0 Conventions and what changes in the design

- Levels: **U** unit (pure function or `tmp_path` tree), **P** property, fuzz, performance, **I** integration (real repo,
  real `make`, real build, fake Hub), **E** end to end or owner-run, **M** meta (tests that prove the other tests are
  not empty). GPU level: none. DOC writes no kernel and changes no library behaviour; the GPU checks of CPU/GPU
  exactness are only "unchanged" (I16).
- Files: `tests/docs_check.py` (pure helpers), `tests/test_docs.py` (the 16 checks of DOC4 + their negative tests),
  `tests/test_docs_content.py` (new: content tests for DOC2 and DOC6-DOC13, section 9.6), `tests/test_headline.py`,
  additions to `tests/test_p2_hf_push.py`. Helper `tree(root, {rel: text})` writes a fake repo.
- Libraries: `pytest`, `hypothesis>=6.100` and `pyyaml>=6.0` are already in the `dev` extra [code: pyproject.toml:29-31],
  so no new test dependency. `pytest-timeout` is not installed: time limits use `signal.alarm` (Unix; skip on Windows).
  Where a rule says "property", a seeded `random.Random(0)` loop is the fallback if the owner bans hypothesis here.
- **Design change needed (finding F7).** DOC4 lists only pure helpers, but its negative tests must run a whole check on a
  `tmp_path` tree. Add one function per check to `tests/docs_check.py`, each `*_offenders(root: Path) -> list[str]`
  (sorted, items `"relpath:line: text"`, empty list means pass): `link_offenders`, `path_offenders`, `make_offenders`,
  `adr_offenders`, `heading_offenders`, `config_offenders`, `version_offenders`, `cost_offenders(root, policy)`,
  `headline_offenders`, `citation_offenders`, `archive_offenders`, `attribution_offenders`, `nav_offenders`, `scratch_path_offenders`, `adr_number_offenders`. Each of the
  15 tests in `test_docs.py` is `assert X_offenders(REPO) == []`; each negative test calls the same function on a seeded
  tree. Test names in sketches below use these names.
- Pinned behaviours (S1 and S2 both said "pin"; the choice is written once here and the tests assert it):
  1. `broken_links`: a directory target is found if the directory exists; a root-absolute link (`/abs.md`) and a link
     leaving the repo root are reported; `?query` and `#anchor` are dropped; the lookup compares names from
     `os.listdir`, so `A.md` does not match `a.md` (the Mac passes, Linux CI would fail).
  2. `backtick_paths`: content of fenced blocks is ignored; a `:NN` or `::name` suffix is stripped before the existence
     test; a span with a leading `./` or `/`, or with the prefix not at the start, is not a path.
  3. `make_mentions`: only a backtick span, a fenced line, or a line starting `make X` or `$ make X` counts; prose such as
     "make sure" never counts; flags (`-C dir`, `-j4`) and `VAR=value` words are skipped; `Make docs` does not count.
  4. `make_targets`: a target needs a rule line; `.PHONY` alone does not define one; `%`, `$(...)`, dot-targets,
     variables and tab-indented lines are excluded.
  5. `adr_files`: pattern `^\d{4}-.+\.md$`; a file in the folder that looks like an ADR but breaks the pattern
     (`001-a.md`, `0001_a.md`) is itself reported by `adr_offenders`, because a typo would hide the ADR.
  6. `config_files`: globs `specs/*.yaml` and `experiments/**/configs/*.yaml` (`.yml` and nested folders are not
     collected; frozen paths are not exempt; an empty result raises). A config counts as documented when its path, or its bare name when that name is unique, appears in
     `docs/reference/configs.md` as a whole token (no substring match: `ra.yaml` does not document `a.yaml`).
  7. `version_mentions` and `allowed_versions` both drop a `+local` label (`2.14.1+cu130` -> `2.14.1`), so `torch 2.13.0`
     in `Dockerfile.vllm_native` is legal when the lock says `2.13.0+cu130`. A bare integer after the name is not a
     mention. `>=`, `~=` and `:` are not mentions.
  8. `cost_mentions`: every `$X` in an Alarm or Hard stop row is checked, so history ("was $15") goes in prose, not in the
     row; bold markers are stripped; `~$10` and `$1,000.50` parse; `USD 10` and `$PATH` give nothing; sentences are single
     line.
  9. `headline_strings`: an unknown view raises `ValueError` naming the view; no returned string is empty; a missing key
     raises `KeyError` naming the key; `ci_unit` empty raises.
  10. Check 9 matches each string with a boundary: `(?<![\d.])<string>(?!\d)`, so `IoU 0.6451` does not satisfy
      `IoU 0.645` (stronger than the plain substring in DOC4 check 9; DOC4 check 9 is amended, see 9.5).
  11. `card_update`: `## Evaluation notes` and `### Evaluation` are different headings and are kept; a section runs to the
      next `## ` or end of file; a heading inside a fenced block is not a heading; a card without a trailing newline
      or with `\r\n` still gives an idempotent result that ends with one `\n`.
  12. `--card-only`: a missing revision is an error (no branch is created); `--run` together with `--card-only` is an
      argparse error; a missing old card (404) is an error, never an overwrite of an empty base.

**Measured: two defects in the DOC4 check 7 regex** (checked 2026-11-08 on CPython with
`(?i)\b{name}(?:\[\w+\])?(?:==|\s+)v?(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\b(?!\s*(?:s|ms|GB|MB|%|x)\b)`):

| Input | Regex as written in DOC4 | Wanted |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm 0.5 %` | `['0.5']` (the `\b` after `%` needs a word character next, so `%` never exempts) | `[]` |
| `vllm 0.5.1 ms` | `['0.5']` (the optional `.1` backtracks, `\b` fits between `5` and `.`) | `[]` |
| `vllm 0.5.1 GB` | `['0.5']` (same backtrack) | `[]` |
| `vLLM 0.09 s`, `vllm 0.5 x`, `vllm 0.5 GB`, `vllm 0.5s` | `[]` | `[]` |

A candidate fix, tested on the rows above and on `2.13.0 sources`, `2.13.0.`, `2.13.0,`, `1.17.10`, `==0.20.1+cu130`:
`(?i)\b{name}(?:\[\w+\])?(?:==|\s+)v?(\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?![\d]|\.\d)(?!\s*(?:(?:s|ms|GB|MB|x)\b|%))`.
U14 fails on the DOC4 regex and passes on the fix. This is why U14 lists the three bold rows.

```python
import ast, importlib
from pathlib import Path
from tests import docs_check as D

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

def test_testing_md_lists_every_docs_test():                       # X10
    names = {n.name for n in ast.walk(ast.parse((REPO / "tests/test_docs.py").read_text()))
             if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name.startswith("test_")}
    text = (REPO / "docs/testing.md").read_text()
    section = text.split("## Docs checks", 1)[1]
    assert {n for n in names if n in section} == names
    assert "not checked by a test" not in (REPO / "docs/README.md").read_text()

ALLOW_EMPTY_GLOBS: set[str] = set()                                # X9: grows only by owner decision
def test_constants_resolve_and_frozen_globs_match_something():
    importlib.import_module(D.POLICY_MODULE)
    assert (REPO / "experiments/phase2/docker/locks/docs.txt").exists()   # DOC13 updates this path
    dead = [g for g in D.FROZEN_GLOBS
            if g not in ALLOW_EMPTY_GLOBS and not list(REPO.glob(g))]
    assert dead == []
```

```python
"""Merged DOC sketches. Pure helpers from tests/docs_check.py (names: see 9.0)."""
import importlib, io, json, re
from pathlib import Path
import pytest
from tests import docs_check as D

def tree(root: Path, files: dict[str, str]) -> Path:
    for rel, text in files.items():
        p = root / rel
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return root

# U14 + U15: version rule, both sides of every exemption (covers the two measured regex defects)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("name, text, expected", [
    ("trl", "TRL 1.16", ["1.16"]), ("trl", "pin trl==1.16.0 now", ["1.16.0"]),
    ("trl", "https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/v1.16.0/trl/x.py", ["1.16.0"]),
    ("torch", "torch==2.14.1+cu130", ["2.14.1"]), ("torch", "torch 2.13.0 sources", ["2.13.0"]),
    ("torch", "torch 2.13.0.", ["2.13.0"]),
    ("vllm", "vLLM 0.09 s", []), ("vllm", "vllm 0.5s", []), ("vllm", "vllm 0.5x", []),
    ("vllm", "vllm 0.5 %", []), ("vllm", "vllm 0.5.1 ms", []), ("vllm", "vllm 0.5.1 GB", []),
    ("torch", "torchvision 0.99", []), ("trl", "xtrl==1.2.3", []), ("trl", "TRL: 1.16", []),
    ("transformers", "transformers>=5.0", []),
])
def test_version_mentions(name, text, expected):
    assert D.version_mentions(text, name) == expected

@pytest.mark.parametrize("m, ok", [("1.17.1", True), ("1.17", True), ("1.1", False),
                                   ("1.17.10", False), ("1.16", False), ("1.170", False)])
def test_two_part_legality(m, ok):
    assert D.is_legal_version(m, {"1.17.1"}) is ok          # the production predicate

def test_version_check_scope(tmp_path):                      # U16 (bad strings built at run time)
    bad = "TRL " + "1.16"
    root = tree(tmp_path, {
        "pyproject.toml": '[project]\nname="x"\nversion="0.1.0"\ndependencies=["trl==1.17.1"]\n',
        "experiments/phase2/docker/locks/vllm_native.txt": "torch==2.13.0+cu130\n",

# M01: seeded faults reported exactly; a check that always passes is caught
SEEDED = {"README.md": "see [x](docs/gone.md) and `make nope`\n",
```

## CLEAN.1. Goal and why

**Goal.** A new engineer sees only live code in `src/`, `experiments/` and `tests/`. Retired code sits in `archive/`
with a README that says what it was, what replaced it, and how to restore it. No dead path stays beside the live one.
Libraries replace our own code where a library does the same job without moving a hashed number. No result changes.

**Why (evidence).**

1. Most tracked files are frozen research, not live code. Of 802 tracked files, 276 are in `experiments/phase1/lab`,
   130 in `experiments/phase2/lab` and 20 in `experiments/phase0` [measured: `git ls-files | wc -l`, per folder].
   That is 426 files (53 %).
2. The lab holds byte-identical copies. 34 of the 39 files in `experiments/phase1/lab/t_stack/vendor/` have an
   identical twin elsewhere in the lab [measured: md5 of every vendor file against the rest of the lab tree]. The other 5
   (`vendor/rewardcore/{advantages,batch,fixtures,reward,topology}.py`) differ.
3. Some old code is already broken. `experiments/phase0/baseline_medsam.py:21` and `baseline_vlm.py:27` import
   `objdel.models.medsam`, which does not exist [code]. `experiments/phase2/lab/A1/a0_ceiling.py:9` imports the archived
   `objdel.checker.polycore` [code].
4. The GPU bundle can ship files that are not code. `policy.code_files()` lists untracked files (`git ls-files -co`)
   [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:377] and drops only `data/`, `docs/`, lab and results folders
   [code: policy.py:379]. Today it lists `.claude/settings.json`, the agent worktree folder
   `.claude/worktrees/agent-a178181ba1474b754/` (1.5 GB on disk) and 10 files under `archive/` [measured: same filter
   run on the repo; `du -sh .claude/worktrees`]. `rsync -az --files-from` does not recurse into a listed folder, so the
   worktree content is not sent today, but `settings.json` and `archive/` are [code: policy.py:247].
5. `train_rl` forks a CPU process pool and never sends it a job. It creates `serve.fork_pool(a.procs)` at line 50 and
   calls only `pool.shutdown()` at line 61 [code: experiments/phase2/train_rl.py:35,50,61]. Idle forked processes hold
   the preloaded store. `fork_pool` also calls `gc.freeze()` on the preloaded store [code: src/objdel/train/serve.py:172];
   the training process keeps that call after the pool goes (CLEAN2).
6. Retired-model paths stay in the library. ADR-0008 says "Do not train LFM2.5-VL-450M again" and "LoRA only. No full
   fine-tune" [code: docs/architecture/decisions/0008-qwen3-vl-2b-over-lfm25-vl-450m.md:1,66]. But `configs.py` still
   has `smolvlm-256m` and `lfm2.5-vl-450m` in `MODELS` and `MAX_COMPLETION`, a SmolVLM image-size branch and
   `use_vllm: model != "smolvlm-256m"` [code: src/objdel/train/configs.py:70-75,136,192]. The `make preflight` default
   config is `r1_lfm.yaml` [code: Makefile:28].
7. The hack-audit `Controller` is not used by any run. No file in `experiments/phase2` installs it; only tests do:
   `tests/test_train_trl.py` (lines 26-511), `tests/test_breakit_wiring.py:51,94` (the `chain` fixture),
   `tests/test_breakit_reward.py:59-107` and `tests/test_eval.py:358-368` (`alarms_for`) [measured: `grep -rn
   "Controller\|audit_alarm\|alarms_for" tests`]. Its `trl_reward` link is shared: `FastGRPO.prefetch_rewards`
   finds the reward through the same attribute [code: src/objdel/train/fast.py:633, rewards.py:107].
8. One test executes lab code: `tests/test_targets.py::test_fixtures_differential_vs_lab_builder` puts
   `experiments/phase1/lab/t_targets` on `sys.path` and imports its builder and crop code [code: tests/test_targets.py:382-414].
   Three more tests import phase 2 lab modules, and two read lab files as fixtures
   [code: tests/test_p2_signal.py:95-97,190; tests/test_p2_probes.py:17,175,238; tests/test_vast.py:31,789].
   The three importing tests check LIVE code (`objdel.eval.signal.per_item`/`group`, `c2_analyze.pooled_ci`,
   `objdel.eval.probes.stratified_ci`) against the lab reference [code: tests/test_p2_signal.py:91-120,189-196;
   tests/test_p2_probes.py:174-180]. They are rewritten, not archived (CLEAN5 step 2).
9. Two copies of the same box-overlap rule exist: `data/lidc.py:257 crowded` and `targets/frame.py:124 crowded`
   [code]. Same expression, two inputs.
10. Owner rules: old code is archived, not left beside new code; remove dead code; prefer a good library over own code;
    `make test` and `make lint` must pass [BRIEF section 3; CLAUDE.md].

**Corrections to the notes (checked against code).**

### CLEAN.3.3 Data flow of one cleanup step

```

                          +--> edit imports and tests --> make lint --> make test --> hygiene test
                          |                                                           |

                                                code_files, pass count delta
```

### CLEAN.3.4 GPU versus CPU

The owner rule is GPU everywhere. CLEAN moves and deletes source files; it runs no numeric work in the product.

| Work | Where | Why not GPU |
|---|---|---|
| File moves, deletions, import edits | Mac CPU | No computation. |
| `make test`, `make lint`, vulture | Mac CPU | The repo's required gate runs on the Mac and in CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml:31-32`). The CUDA path is unchanged in Waves 1 and 3, so the CPU build of the same source covers it (ADR-0001). |
| CLEAN4 golden recording | Mac CPU, once | Runs the frozen lab builder (numpy/numba, CPU code by design) one last time to freeze its outputs. |
| CLEAN11 polygonizer check | GPU in production (phase D3), CPU build in tests | D3 moves the work from CPU to GPU: `targets/build.py` and `checker/certify.py` call `checker/rings.py`, which calls `_gpucheck.check_masks`. B1.4a moves the numpy polygonizer and D3 the bit-quads to `tests/oracles/`. CLEAN11 only checks that state; it moves nothing. |
| `gc.freeze()` after `serve.preload` in `train_rl` | CPU, training process | Not computation: it keeps the preloaded store out of Python's GC scans during the 23.4 s steps. It was a side effect of `fork_pool`; CLEAN2 keeps it explicitly so the step time does not move for an unmeasured reason. |
| `serve.fork_pool` in `select_ckpt`, `g_probe`, `final_eval` | CPU (stays for now) | It runs the eval-only metrics (NSD, GED, HM-IoU, soft Dice) in numpy/scipy. Phase D7 step 6 moves them to the GPU in one process and deletes the `--procs` flags; E3b archives the pool names (E R-2); CLEAN16 step 1 checks that they are gone (final round 8, arch-3). CLEAN2 deletes only the idle copy in `train_rl`. |

## CLEAN.4. Tasks

Rules for every task:
- The engineer uses plain `mkdir`, `mv`, `rm` and file edits. The engineer runs no git command that changes anything.
  The owner runs the git commands listed in the task (global rule).
- Each task ends green: `make lint` and `make test` pass. Any test removed is listed in the archive README of the
  thing it tested, with its node id. The pass-count delta must equal that list.
- Python that reads `data/` runs with `-I`. Tests with the `data` marker run only through `make test-data`
  (`$(PY) -I -m pytest -q -m data`), and `make test` runs `-m "not slow and not data"`. The first phase that needs
  the target adds it (A uses it in its "All" gate; D8 adds it if it is still missing). CLEAN adds no target.
- The pass-count rule uses the CLEAN baseline that CLEAN0 records at phase start (and again at the start of Waves 2
  and 3), not the 2026-11-08 count: phases A-D add tests before CLEAN runs.
- No task changes `src/objdel/reward/`, `src/objdel/targets/build.py`, `simplify.py` or `frame.py` behaviour
  in Wave 1 (hashed outputs).
- No CLEAN commit, in any wave, changes a file under `cuda/`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tests/test_cuda_checker_gpu.py` or
  `tests/test_gpu_scoring.py` (CLEAN.spec constraint C1, read as a rule on CLEAN's own commits). Other phases do
  change these paths between Waves 1 and 3: D1 edits `cuda/gpucheck.cpp` and `CMakeLists.txt` (NVTX), D2 deletes
  engine symbols from `cuda/gpucheck.cpp`, D8 deletes the file-level `skipif` [code: tests/test_cuda_checker_gpu.py:27]
  and adds GPU cases to `tests/test_gpu_scoring.py` (D.md D1, D2, D8). So no CLEAN gate diffs these paths against the
  tag `pre-clean-2026-11-08` (that diff fails on a correct tree after D1). CT-73 checks the staged files of each
  CLEAN commit; CT-72 and CT-55 check only CLEAN's own commits, found by the subject rule below.
- Commit subject rule: the subject of each CLEAN commit starts with its task id and a colon (`CLEAN5: archive phase 0
  and the lab trees`). No commit of another phase starts its subject with `CLEAN`. A CLEAN step that lands inside
  another phase's commit (CLEAN8 step 4 in the E6.6 commit) keeps that phase's subject; CT-73 still checks it.
- Precondition for every owner commit: the owner's unrelated work is not swept in. Today `README.md` is modified and
  most of `docs/` is untracked [gitStatus at session start]. Before the first CLEAN commit, `git status --porcelain
  README.md docs/` must be empty (the owner commits the docs work first), or the owner stages CLEAN's hunks only
  with `git add -p <file>`. No task gives a blanket `git add -A` over `README.md` or `docs/`.
- Order: CLEAN0, then Wave 1a (CLEAN2, CLEAN6, CLEAN7; CLEAN6 before CLEAN7 because both edit
  `tests/test_breakit_wiring.py`), then Wave 1b. CLEAN4 before CLEAN5. CLEAN9 step 3 before CLEAN10.
- Wave 1 is part of the owner tag `v1-b1` (front order rule 2: be52b1c + A3, A6, B1 + CLEAN wave 1). Every Wave 1
  commit lands before the owner tags it. The tag's checks (B E08 dry run, reward goldens, `tests/test_p2_train_rl.py`,
  `make preflight`) then run on a tree that holds CLEAN2's `train_rl` edit and CLEAN6's `rewards.py` edit.
- CLEAN does not touch `ALARM, HARD_STOP` [code: experiments/phase2/vast/policy.py:58]. Front 6.1 step 0 owns that
  edit ($19.90 with owner approval). CLEAN1 and CLEAN13 edit other lines of `policy.py`; the owner commits them apart
  from the step 0 edit.
- Live RL plan: B1.5 archives `rl_shifted.yaml` to `archive/phase2_runs/configs/` and makes `b1_rows.yaml` the live
  plan (B1.5; one archive folder for old plans, final review r2, arch item 1). B1 and Wave 1 run in parallel, so each
  CLEAN check that lists the RL plans reads "`rl_shifted.yaml`, or `b1_rows.yaml` after B1.5".
- Docs stay green on every CLEAN commit (final review r3, arch item 3; E R-1; DOC task order). DOC4 lands before
  CLEAN, so `tests/test_docs.py` runs inside `make test` on every CLEAN commit. No CLEAN commit leaves a doc check
  red for DOC13 to fix. Each archive, move or rename commit does these things in the same commit:
  - It rewrites every backtick repo path in the DOC4 `doc_files` set with the commit's old -> new path map. This
    covers CLEAN5 (step 4 sweep) and CLEAN8 step 4 (scripts to `archive/phase2_runs/`).
    DOC4 check 2 (`test_backtick_paths_exist`) then stays green.
  - It keeps DOC's config assertions true. CLEAN5 step 6 changes ruff `extend-exclude`, so the same commit updates
    DOC test I14 (CLEAN5 step 6).
  - It leaves `FROZEN_GLOBS` and `POLICY_MODULE` unchanged. CLEAN moves no live module that DOC names. The trees that
    CLEAN5 moves land in `archive/` (only `archive/*/README.md` is a doc file) or in `docs/research/records/phase0/`
    (frozen by `docs/research/**`). DOC U01 pins the 11 glob families on synthetic paths, so a glob that matches no
    real file after CLEAN5 stays. If DOC X9 reports it, the CLEAN5 commit adds it to `ALLOW_EMPTY_GLOBS`.
  - A new doc page joins the DOC indexes in the same commit: CLEAN14's ADR gets its index row and its `nav` entry.
  - Each new archive README passes DOC check 11 (CLEAN5 step 7).
  Gate for the rule: `make test` before each owner commit, with `tests/test_docs.py` collected and not skipped.

   `lab/A4/rater_ceiling.py` to `archive/phase2_lab/A4/` before CLEAN (A test S05), so `lab` can be lower at CLEAN0.
   Also record the environment for CT-72: `uv pip freeze --python .venv/bin/python > runs/clean/freeze.txt`.

   - Before E6.8 (the file `experiments/phase2/configs/r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml` exists): `make preflight

   plus a new constant `P.LIVE_CLIS = ("experiments.phase2.train_rl", "experiments.phase2.g_probe",

   [measured: bundle probe run, 2026-11-08]. (c) `tests`, `tests.oracles` and `experiments.phase1` have no
   `__init__.py`, so they are namespace packages with `__file__` None; the child reports their `__path__` entries,
   and every entry must be inside the copy. The final assertion then proves every first-party module came from the
   copy, not from the editable install. The listed modules import

   the test starts with `pytest.importorskip("cv2")` and `("scipy")`; the CI `train` job (`.[dev,data,train]`) runs it.
   Mark it `slow` only if it takes more than 30 s. Run it before and after CLEAN5.
6. Gate: `code_files()` on the real repo: 0 entries under `.claude/`, 0 under `archive/` (today 2 and 10 [measured]);
   `test_bundle_imports_standalone` passes.

folders hold macOS binaries (K1 3.5 MB, K2 10 MB [measured: du -sh, 2026-11-08]); DOC1 keeps them out of git with a

## CLEAN.7. Risks and rollback

| Risk | Sign | Mitigation | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| A moved file is still imported somewhere | `make test` import error | grep before each move; the hygiene test (CLEAN12) catches lab imports | `git restore --source=pre-clean-2026-11-08 -- <path>` (owner) |
| The golden in CLEAN4 hides a real change in the lab comparison | integers differ from the old test | CLEAN4 gate compares the integers before the move (Mac only, `-rs` shows no skip) | keep the old test and the lab until fixed |
| A tracked golden redistributes RIGA data | review or licence complaint | CLEAN4 stores hashes and one RIGA total only; CLEAN-G16 guard test | delete the file; re-record without the field |
| CLEAN5 moves git-ignored RIGA results past their anchored `.gitignore` lines and `git add -A` stages them | `git status` lists `??` paths under `docs/research/records/phase0/results/` or `archive/phase1_lab/` | CLEAN5 step 0 rewrites the RIGA block before the moves; step 9 RIGA gate (CLEAN-G19) and CT-89 run before the owner's `git add`; CT-73 at commit | before a push: `git rm --cached` the paths and amend; after a push the files are public and history must be rewritten by the owner, so the gate runs before step 8 |
| Live code loses its lab reference check | phase A bootstrap CI drifts unnoticed | CLEAN5 step 2 keeps the three tests against `p2_lab_refs.json` (CLEAN-G18) | restore the lab modules from the tag |
| Prefetch silently turns off | GPU wait grows; no error | CLEAN6 keeps `f.trl_reward = self`; new assertion in a reward test (CLEAN-G17) | restore the line |
| GC scans the preloaded store after the pool goes | slower RL steps | CLEAN2 keeps `gc.freeze()` (CLEAN-G17) | none needed |
| The bundle drop rule or the CLEAN5 moves remove a file the box needs | `IMPORT_CHECK` fails at `sync_up` (on a rented GPU) | `test_bundle_imports_standalone` (CLEAN1, CLEAN-G15) runs the same imports at $0 on the Mac; `test_code_snapshot_ships_tests_for_k3_harness` pins the needed files | revert the one-line regex |
| The $0 bundle probe passes because the editable install serves the repo | probe green on the Mac, `IMPORT_CHECK` red on the box | child runs `-I -S` with site-packages passed in; namespace `__path__` entries checked; canary (CLEAN1 step 5, CT-30) | none needed (test-only) |
| Phase-start test count differs from 2026-11-08 | CLEAN-G2 fails on a correct tree | CLEAN0 records `runs/clean/baseline.txt` at phase start and at each wave start | re-record the baseline |
| SmolVLM test migration changes what a CPU test checks | a test passes for a different reason | pass the old values as explicit overrides (CLEAN7 step 1) | restore the key from the tag |
| `boxes_meet` changes window selection | view hash test fails | hypothesis equivalence test first | revert CLEAN9 step 1 |
| Owner wants the Controller later | B3 asks for a hack alarm | restore from `archive/controller/` (README "How to restore") | as left |
| DOC8 says `archive/` holds code only; a lab tree has code, notes and results together | DOC review objects | CLEAN moves each lab tree whole (splitting breaks the links between scripts and results); ask DOC to accept "a frozen lab tree moves as one unit" | move the lab `.md` files to `docs/research/records/` in a follow-up |
| vastai 1.11 changes JSON keys | CLEAN13 gate fails | do not pin; keep 0.3.1 | none needed |
| vastai's exact pins downgrade Pillow | image bytes or view hashes change | never in `pyproject.toml`; `uv tool install` only (CLEAN13) | `uv tool uninstall vastai` |
| `make preflight` default cannot load | `TypeError ... 'steps'` | default `r1_qwen3vl2b.yaml`, not `rl_shifted.yaml` (CLEAN9 step 3) | revert the Makefile line |
| A CLEAN commit sweeps in the owner's docs work | unrelated files in the cleanup commit | clean-tree precondition; `git add -p` (Rules) | owner amends before push |
| Conflicts with phase E moves | merge pain | CLEAN Wave 1 lands before E starts (fewer files to move) | none |
| Conflicts with phases B and C | merge pain in `train_rl.py`, `rewards.py`, `callbacks.py`, `configs.py` | Wave 1a (CLEAN2, CLEAN6, CLEAN7) lands before any B2, B3 or C branch starts | rebase the B/C branch |

## CLEAN.8. Cost, time and dependencies

GPU: 0 minutes, $0. Every task runs on the Mac. No rental. CLEAN13's gate is a read-only Vast API call ($0) by the
main agent.

Engineer time on the Mac [estimate]: CLEAN0 1 h (plus one 9-minute test run [measured: 523 s] and one preflight);
CLEAN1 1.5 h (bundle import test); CLEAN2 0.5 h; CLEAN3 0.5 h; CLEAN4 2.5 h; CLEAN5 6 h (lab-refs golden and the
stale-path sweep); CLEAN6 2 h; CLEAN7 2 h; CLEAN9 1.5 h; CLEAN10 0.5 h; CLEAN12 2 h; CLEAN13 0.5 h; CLEAN14 1 h;
CLEAN15 3 h (optional). Wave 1 total about 21.5 h without CLEAN15 (Wave 1a: CLEAN2 + CLEAN6 + CLEAN7 = 4.5 h). Each full `make test`
run costs about 9 minutes; plan one per task (about 2 h of test time in Wave 1). Wave 2 (CLEAN11, check only) about
0.5 h after D3.
Wave 3 (CLEAN8, CLEAN16) about 5 h after D and E.

Dependencies:
- Before CLEAN: DOC8 (`archive/README.md` text and check 11) should land first or in the same pull request; the owner
  tag in CLEAN0.
- CLEAN does not block phase A. Wave 1a (CLEAN2, CLEAN6, CLEAN7, about 4.5 h) edits `train_rl.py`, `rewards.py`,
  `callbacks.py` and `configs.py`, the same files as B2 (trainer-vLLM match), B3 (reward v5) and C (pixels on GPU,
  outline limit, n=8 requests). Land Wave 1a before any B2, B3 or C branch starts; the rest of Wave 1 can run in
  parallel with B and C. Wave 1 should land before phase E moves packages.
- Wave 1 (CLEAN5) before D3: the phase 0 and lab scripts that import `objdel.checker.polygonize`, `certify` or
  `bitquad` are archived first, so D3 need not keep them importable.
- Wave 2 needs D3 (production polygonizer switch; numpy code in `tests/oracles/`) and its hash gate D-G4.
- Wave 3 needs phase E2 (typed `build_trainer` with a token cap), E6 (4 ported specs; E6.6 archives the 12 old
  plans) and D7 step 6 (eval metrics on GPU in one process; D-G17).
- Front time line (section 1, step 8): the DOC final sweep (DOC13) runs after E, then CLEAN Waves 2-3. DOC13 covers
  the Wave 1 changes. Waves 2-3 change no doc text except the archive READMEs and the lines they must fix
  (DOC4 check 2, `test_backtick_paths_exist`, holds them). CLEAN11 is read-only, so it may run any time after D3.

Owner-only steps: the tag and its push (CLEAN0), every `git add`/commit (CLEAN5 and each task, after the clean-tree
precondition), the decision on the Controller, `uv tool install vastai==1.11.0` (CLEAN13), reinstalling the dev
extra (CLEAN12), deleting `data/_retired/`.

Merged from two independent lists written from the CLEAN spec only (`docs/implementation2.0/tests/CLEAN_tests_1.md`, ids CT-n, spec
ids B1..B23; `docs/implementation2.0/tests/CLEAN_tests_2.md`, ids Tn). Those lists name work items B1..B23 and gates G1..G16 of an
older spec. This section re-maps every test to the task ids CLEAN0..CLEAN16 and the gates CLEAN-G1..CLEAN-G18 of section 6. The
merged ids are `CT-nn`. Each entry lists the source ids it replaces (`S1:` = list 1, `S2:` = list 2). Where both lists
tested the same thing, the stronger version is kept (rules in 9.1). No REPO file was edited to write this section.
Tags as in the rest of this document. [code: file:line] facts I re-checked on 2026-11-08: `train_rl.main(argv=None)`
exists (train_rl.py:19); `--procs` is the only option starting `--pro` (train_rl.py:23-36), so `--proc` becomes an
argparse error once it goes; `serve.preload` runs once per root, so `--train-views a b` gives 3 calls
(train_rl.py:46-49); `die()` is `sys.exit("vast: ...")`, so tests use `pytest.raises(SystemExit, match=...)`
(policy.py:88); `code_files()` has no existence filter (policy.py:374-383); `tests/goldens/` holds only `polycore.npz`
and `tests/fixtures/` does not exist yet; `hypothesis>=6.100` is a dev dependency (pyproject.toml:29); `vulture` and
`shapely` are not installed in `.venv` [measured: docs/implementation2.0/tests/CLEAN_tests_2.md, 2026-11-08].

### CLEAN.9.1 Merge rules and conflicts resolved

| # | Conflict between the lists | Kept | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Both test `code_files` roots (S1 CT-1/CT-3, S2 T01/T02) | One keep-list plus one drop-list test, and one look-alike test using the union of both look-alike sets | Same behaviour; the union has more boundary cases |
| 2 | `boxes_meet`: S1 literal table + random loop; S2 pixel-raster oracle + algebra | Both: literals (CT-01) and raster oracle with algebra (CT-02) | The raster oracle is independent of the formula (stronger); the literals pin degenerate boxes, which the raster oracle excludes |
| 3 | Golden mask guard: S1 `ndim <= 1`, size < 2 MB; S2 adds `size <= 4096`, `riga` arrays of size 1, no `riga/x/y` key | S2 | `ndim <= 1` alone is defeated by `.ravel()` (a flat 512x512 mask is 262,144 values). The 4,096 cap is an [estimate] |
| 4 | Bundle import: S1 `PROBE` prints files; S2 asserts count >= 12 and a canary | S2 sketch, S1 negative-control idea | Both assert every `__file__` is inside the copy |
| 5 | Skips: S1 says an import test must fail, never skip; CLEAN1 step 5 says `importorskip("cv2")` and `("scipy")` | CLEAN1 step 5 for cv2 and scipy only; the Mac gate runs `pytest -rs` and must show 0 skips for this test. No other skip is allowed in CT-30, CT-44, CT-14 | CI runs a `train` job with both libraries |
| 6 | `--procs` spellings: S1 `--proc`, `--pro`, `--p`; S2 `--procs=2`, `-procs 2`, bare `--procs` | Union, plus "exit 2 before any preload" (S2) | A bad flag must not cost a preload on a rented box |
| 7 | gc.freeze: S1 one preload; S2 two views | S2 (`--train-views a b` = 3 preloads) plus S1's early-exit and double-call cases | "After the last preload" needs more than one |

| 10 | S2 T04: `git ls-files -c` lists a tracked file already moved on disk, so `rsync --files-from` aborts | Kept as CT-26; it fails on today's code and passes with CLEAN1 step 1's file filter | CLEAN1 step 1 keeps `-co` and adds the filter (rule Q-T2) |
